EIBUN.name: EIBUN
EIBUN.desc: Provisional #1 among the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten my way through (14/15). A famous shop featured on Horiemon's “Adult Playground” map. The No.1 most popular “BUNBUN soba” is a luxurious bowl topped with four kinds of meat.
t: It was featured in the “Horiemon 'Adult Playground' Nationwide Map” (paid), and after watching it I went to eat there right away in July 2022 lol

I've still only been to a fraction of the Okinawa soba shops on the main island of Okinawa, nowhere near conquering them all, but I think this is the most delicious Okinawa soba I've had so far. As expected of a recommendation from the gourmet Mr. Horie ☺

I'd heard there would be a line, so after enjoying my hobby of surfing first thing in the morning at the Suicide Cliff point in Itoman City, I arrived around 10 o'clock even though the opening time was 11 ☺ Naturally, at that hour I was easily the first one there.
However, there was a reception list placed at the shop entrance, and some people wrote down a reservation and then left the shop for a while, so I hurriedly put my name on the reception list too.
Right before the 11 o'clock opening time, customers started lining up. As expected, there are a lot of tourists. *The shop has no parking lot. There is coin parking in front of the shop.
The “EIBUN” entrance. The design is stylish, isn't it

This is the situation when I finished eating and left the shop: from just before the 11 o'clock opening, the number of customers suddenly increased. I think there's probably a line continuously until closing. It's better to put your name on the reception list early and eat early.
When I went inside, “BUNBUN soba,” whose name resembles the shop's name, was being recommended as the No.1 most popular, so I ordered it.
Recommended menu

First, a sip of the soup. The bonito-based broth really comes through and it's delicious. The moment I drank it, it was a deliciousness no shop before had. The noodles are thin and straight. There are four toppings (braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), makanai meat, soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and seared soft-bone pork ribs), and all of them are well-seasoned and the best lol. I thought the balance of soup, noodles, and toppings was the best of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at so far.
“BUNBUN soba” (¥1,000), recommended as the No.1 most popular

Rating (14/15): Wow, it seems the owner is from mainland Japan, and the shop's name seems to come from his own name; apparently he opened the shop after training at a famous Okinawa soba shop. I'm looking forward to seeing whether an Okinawa soba shop will ever come along that I think surpasses this deliciousness.

STAND EIBUN.name: STAND EIBUN
STAND EIBUN.desc: The second shop of provisional #1 “EIBUN” (14/15). The most popular item is the sea lettuce (āsa) soba. A hidden gem where you can enjoy a bowl of the same level without standing in the main shop's line.
t: “EIBUN” is the shop I think is the most delicious of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at so far, but I recently found out they opened a second shop around April 2023(?), so I went to eat there in February 2024 😁
STAND EIBUN (a stylish exterior that doesn't lose to the main shop 😆)
This second shop was really close to the main shop (^0^;)

On top of that, it was two doors down from “Okinawa Pork Soba,” which I visited the other day as the 6th of 34 shops in the 13th stamp rally (^0^;)　As usual, I go with no research and just wing it, so I didn't know (^0^;)

What surprised me even more is that on this day too the main shop had its usual line and didn't feel easy to drop into, but the second shop had no line in particular. When I stood in front of the entrance, a staff member guided me in, saying “Please, come in.”
The number of customers is completely different between the main shop and the second shop.

When I went inside, there was a meal ticket machine installed, so I ordered from the menu. I believe the main shop accepted cashless payment, but unfortunately this one seems to be cash only. The meal ticket machine is a new type too, so I hope they'll support cashless payment in the future.

In the staff member's explanation of the menu in front of the meal ticket machine, they said something like “the sea lettuce (āsa) soba is the most popular,” so this time I decided to order the “sea lettuce (āsa) soba” 😁
I was shown to a counter seat, and while I waited I looked around the stylish interior 😄
Drinks are self-service.
The condiment containers placed on the table are stylish too
Besides the usual “kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori),” there was also something called “gōmāgūsu.” That's new.
The regular “kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori).” As expected, the container has a stylish look 😆
There are various other condiments too 😄
T-shirts, roasted green tea (hojicha), bowls, and so on are sold inside the shop. Stylish 😄
While I was observing the interior, the “sea lettuce (āsa) soba” arrived. It looks delicious 😋
Sea lettuce (āsa) soba　¥1,080
The blue bowl is the same as at the main shop “EIBUN” 😄　I was about to taste the soup right away, but there were no chopsticks?
There were no chopsticks on the table, and thinking “Huh? Did the staff forget?”, I asked whether there were chopsticks, and the answer was “They're in the drawer” (°°)
Chopsticks, wet towels, and condiments were in the drawer (^0^;)　I didn't notice (^0^;)
When I checked the drawer, they were inside. Looking closely, there was a label-maker sticker in small letters on the counter wall saying that chopsticks and wet towels are in the drawer (^0^;)
I didn't notice (^0^;)　Starting over, I took a sip of the soup. It's a soup with the bonito broth coming through, and I thought, as expected, EIBUN is delicious.

Next, when I tasted the soup together with the sea lettuce (āsa), I could also feel the flavor of the seashore, and this was delicious too 😋　According to what I googled, before opening EIBUN the manager also trained at “Nakamura Soba” in Onna Village, and it reminded me of Nakamura Soba's sea lettuce (āsa) soba too 😆
Sea lettuce (āsa) soba　¥1,080

Next, I have the noodles. The medium-thick fresh noodles have a chewy, springy feel, and they're delicious too 😄　The toppings, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), still had a bit of sinewy texture, but they're tender and delicious. Moreover, unlike other shops, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were finished with a fairly sweet flavor, rich and deep, and I found these delicious too.

Then, in the second half, I changed up the flavor of the soup with the “gōmāgūsu.” I could feel the nice aroma of sesame oil and the sourness of vinegar too, and it became a new soup. It goes well with it, and I thought this was delicious too 😄

Rating (14/15): Although it's the second shop, I had EIBUN's Okinawa soba for the first time in a while, and as expected I thought it was high-level and delicious. Looking at “noodles,” “soup,” and “toppings” individually, there are other shops that are just as delicious, but I think what's amazing about EIBUN is that the noodles, soup, and toppings are all in balance. Moreover, while the main shop has a line, this one maybe isn't well-known yet, so you can eat the same taste without getting caught in a line, which makes it recommended 😆　Also, it would be even better if they supported cashless payment soon 👍

木灰そば とらや.name: Mokkai Soba Toraya
木灰そば とらや.desc: A famous mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye) shop in Akamine near Naha Airport. Clear soup with plenty of bonito broth, and house-made noodles you can choose from medium-thin or flat. The melt-apart bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) served on a separate plate are superb.
t: This article was written with AI (Chat GPT 4o) and partially edited by me 😁

I ate here in September 2024 😄　I went to “Mokkai Soba Toraya” in Akamine, Naha City, and was amazed at how delicious its Okinawa soba was ✨. From the atmosphere of the shop to the soba served, the overall quality is very high, and as an Okinawa soba lover it's a shop I really want to recommend to everyone, so it's listed in my “Okinawa soba shops that hold their own against my recommended shops” corner 😆
Mokkai Soba Toraya

When you enter the shop, the first thing that catches your eye is the ticket machine. There's a wide variety on the menu, such as Okinawa soba, bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, and set menus with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) (rice cooked with ingredients), and everything makes you want to eat it. I chose the “bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba” without hesitation, but next time I'd like to try the other menu items too 🍚.
You can choose the noodles from medium-thin or flat noodles, and I decided to go with the recommended “medium-thin noodles.”
The meal ticket machine installed near the shop entrance
The noodles are the choosable type

After ordering, while I waited I looked around the shop, and a warm space with a wood-based design spread out before me. Okinawan-style decorations line the walls, and pickled red ginger and glass cups are neatly arranged on the counter, giving the impression that attention has been paid to every detail. It's mainly counter seats, which makes it easy to go in even alone, a nice point too 😊.
The counter inside the shop
Bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, medium　¥850

After a while, the “bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba” was served. The clear soup, the medium-thin noodles, and the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) served on a separate plate are striking. First, a sip of the soup. The bonito broth really comes through, and the rich aroma that spreads softly in your mouth is irresistible 😋.
Bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, medium　¥850

Next, I had the noodles. These are house-made noodles, and this time I chose the recommended medium-thin noodles. They're springy yet slide down smoothly, a very pleasant texture. They go perfectly with the soup too, and my chopsticks kept moving. When you hear “mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye),” you expect a unique flavor, but this time I didn't really notice that flavor. However, the noodles were boiled just right, and the quality was delicious enough as is 🍜.

And the main event, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki)! These are served on a separate plate. I appreciate this consideration. It's a trick to avoid spoiling the taste of the soup, so you can enjoy the flavor of the bonito broth to the very end. The bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) are surprisingly tender, so tender they fall apart in your mouth. The sauce has soaked in thoroughly, and this alone is a very satisfying dish. Being able to enjoy them in a way only possible with separate-plate service is also one of the features of “Mokkai Soba Toraya.”

Overall, the Okinawa soba here comes together at a very high level. It's a shop I'd love for people who like bonito broth to try! Also, the atmosphere inside is comfortable, and you can drop in casually even alone. Next time I'd like to try the set with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) and other menu items ✨.
Please be sure to fully enjoy the charm of Okinawa soba at “Mokkai Soba Toraya”! I'm sure you'll be satisfied 😊.

Rating (12/15): I thought it was a high-level Okinawa soba shop with a good balance of noodles, soup, and toppings. It's close to the airport too, so how about trying it at least once, both tourists and locals? It's recommended 😄

宮古そば みやらび.name: Miyako Soba Miyarabi
宮古そば みやらび.desc: A Miyako soba specialty shop with a reddish-brown triangular roof, 10 minutes by car from Naha Airport. A bowl with a gentle pork-bone-based soup, thin straight noodles with a round cross-section, and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and lean pork on top. The interior has a Showa-retro feel, and turnover is quick.
t: This article was written with AI (Chat GPT o3) and partially edited by me 😁
I went to eat here in December 2024 😄

About 10 minutes by car from Naha Airport, a reddish-brown triangular roof appears all on its own in a corner of Gushi. That's “Miyako Soba Miyarabi” 🚗💨. A well-worn “Open” sign hangs from the wooden pillar at the entrance, and the purple flag proudly shows the words “Miyako Soba” in white. It makes your heart race.
Miyako Soba　Miyarabi
The meal ticket machine installed at the shop entrance

Right when you open the door, there's the meal ticket machine. More than 50 buttons, big and small, are lined up, and handwritten notes like “10-yen coins cannot be used” and “Lunch service” announcements are pasted all over it. Basic soba starts from around ¥700, and I'm surprised by the breadth of the lineup, which includes sets, soups, and even champuru (Okinawan stir-fry) 😲. This time I pushed the button without hesitation for the signature menu item that's even in the shop's name, “Miyako soba (¥750).” As soon as I put the meal ticket on the counter, cooking began briskly in the kitchen in the back.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

The wall side of the L-shaped counter inside has flower-patterned, mosaic-style glass, a bit like a Showa-retro coffee shop. At lunchtime it's sure to be full, but turnover is quick, and from handing over the meal ticket until the bowl arrives felt like about 5 minutes. A welcome speed for someone who wants to drop in quickly between sightseeing ⏱️.
Miyako soba　¥750

Now, the Miyako soba that appeared in front of me. The soup, clear yet slightly cloudy, has the gentle aroma of a pork bone base. It's not the “original Miyako style” where the toppings hide under the noodles; instead, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and lean pork (loin) sit proudly on top. Pale green chopped green onions float on it, and although it looks simple, it's a bowl with a certain dignity.
First, a sip with the soup spoon. It's pork bone based.
Miyako soba　¥750
The noodles are thin and straight with a round cross-section, typical of Miyako soba. The firmness is modest, on the soft side 🍜.
The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) has a just-right balance of fat and lean, while the lean pork has a solid bite. Both have a sinewy texture 😆.

When I suddenly looked around, the place was bustling with customers. Even though it's located near the airport, it doesn't go all-in on tourist-spot prices; it's a shop that stays close to local daily life, and that atmosphere fills the shop, making it comfortable.

Rating (9/15): There's no standout flashiness, but it was a Miyako soba that embodies “just plain delicious” and stays close to everyday life. That's what I felt Miyarabi's Miyako soba is. It's a little away from central Naha City, but it's perfect for filling up before returning your rental car or for lunch on the way to the airport. How about trying it at least once ✨. 🥢

沖縄そば くいな.name: Okinawa Soba Kuina
沖縄そば くいな.desc: Produced by Horiemon, opened in April 2024. The signature dish is “Island Soba,” with a smooth combined broth of chicken, bonito, and pork bone and Nago-style flat noodles. A shop where the creative items like nbusa soba and inamuruchi mixed soba also catch your interest.
t: I ate here in April 2024 😄　This shop is produced by Horiemon and had just opened on April 26. Since it's run by the gourmet Mr. Horie, I came this time with high expectations 😁
Okinawa Soba　Kuina

When I went inside, a staff member explained the menu using a menu sheet. I forgot to take a photo of the menu sheet, but I decided to order the “Island Soba,” which was recommended with “for first-timers.” The other soba menu items are “Island Noodle (apparently with a blend of house-made seasonings),” “nbusa soba (Shirinkawa tofu + sea lettuce (āsa) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku)),” and “inamuruchi mixed soba,” so they've narrowed it down.
A flyer from Okinawa Soba Kuina
An explanation of the house-made seasonings posted on the wall (apparently you can taste them if you order the Island Noodle)
Island Soba　¥950

Here it is 😆　First, I taste the soup. It seems to be a combined broth of chicken, bonito, and pork bone, and it has a smooth feel with a slightly pronounced pork bone flavor. I think it's a taste other shops don't have.
Island Soba　¥950

Next, I have the noodles. They're fresh noodles, a flat type like the ones you see in Nago's Okinawa soba. I thought they were just plain delicious, but somehow I could feel hard cores remaining here and there. Maybe because they'd just opened and weren't used to it yet, I thought the boiling was uneven.
The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are melt-in-your-mouth tender too, but a sinewy texture remains.
Rating (9/15): This time, since it's a shop produced by the gourmet Horiemon, I had pretty high expectations, but it felt about “just plain delicious, I guess” (^0^;)

I think the noodle boiling was inconsistent too, so that's a shame. But I'd like to try their other creative Okinawa soba menu items. It's close to Kokusai-dori (near the prefectural office), so how about trying it once?

SHIKAKU.name: SHIKAKU
SHIKAKU.desc: A luxurious Okinawa soba shop on the 1st floor of the Southwest Grand Hotel. Its feature is the kettle (teapot) style where the noodles and soup come separately, and the dashi chazuke, made by pouring the kettle's broth over the tuna nakaochi rice, is also recommended.
t: This article was written with AI (Gemini Pro) and partially edited by me 😁
I went to eat here in February 2025 😄

This time I visited “SHIKAKU,” located on the 1st floor of the “Southwest Grand Hotel” in Kumoji, Naha City. The aura is different from the exterior alone. Since it's on the 1st floor of a hotel, there's a shisa sitting against a stylish exposed-concrete wall, and even this shisa looks somehow sleek, like modern art ✨
SHIKAKU is on the 1st floor of the Southwest Grand Hotel
SHIKAKU is on the 1st floor of the Southwest Grand Hotel
SHIKAKU is on the 1st floor of the Southwest Grand Hotel
SHIKAKU
SHIKAKU
SHIKAKU
Standing in front of the shop, a sense of luxury is in the air. But as an Okinawa soba lover, I summoned my courage and charged in!

When I went inside, the lighting was turned down quite low, and it had an atmosphere like a bar at dinnertime or an upscale teppanyaki restaurant. It's moody even though it's daytime, a space you could use for a date. And above all, what surprised me was the staff's service! When showing me to my seat, they actually pulled out my chair and escorted me, just like at a hotel restaurant…! Having my chair pulled out when I came to eat Okinawa soba may be a first in my life (lol). It makes you sit up a little straighter 😳
Inside the shop
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

Now, when I sat down and opened the menu, it was another simple and stylish design. The “SHIKAKU soba” regular is ¥1,400 and the large is ¥1,600. I ordered the “SHIKAKU soba (regular)” and the side dish the staff recommended, “tuna nakaochi rice (¥700)” 🍜
After a while, this set was brought out.
SHIKAKU soba (regular) ¥1,400, tuna nakaochi rice　¥700

The style is unique! The bowl with the noodles and toppings and a silver kettle with the soup came out separately. This is the same style as the long-established “Yae Shokudo” in Nago City! I never thought I'd encounter this kettle style at a hotel in Naha. But it's not a homey kettle like Yae Shokudo's; it has the look of a sleek stainless-steel teapot, and I feel the stylishness here too ✨
This ritual of pouring the soup yourself from the kettle is exciting. Every time you pour, the nice aroma of bonito broth wafts up. The good thing about this style is that the soup stays piping hot.
First, I try a sip of the soup. Yeah, the bonito broth comes through.
SHIKAKU soba (regular) ¥1,400

Next, I have the noodles. The noodles are a thin type with a slight wave. When I slurp them, they have a smooth, slippery texture, and they're boiled fairly soft. As someone who likes noodles with strong firmness, I'd like a little more chewiness / bite 🤔

The toppings are braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and fish cake (kamaboko), plus green onions and bonito flakes. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is simmered tender, and the seasoning is neither too strong nor too light, just right. The bonito flakes sprinkled on top further bring out the aroma of the soup, and the flavor is really good 👍
Tuna nakaochi rice　¥700

And then the side dish, the “tuna nakaochi rice”! It comes with wasabi and looks delicious, but I poured the broth from the kettle holding the soba soup over the tuna rice and ate it like dashi chazuke.

This was exactly right! 🐟✨ The sweetness of the tuna's fat combines with the piping-hot bonito broth, and the half-rare tuna melts in your mouth. The wasabi adds an accent, and you can just shovel it down. I really want everyone to try it too!

Rating (9/15): My overall impression is that the taste is just plain delicious. However, there's no denying that it's “hotel pricing~.” With ¥1,400 for Okinawa soba, and over ¥2,000 with rice too, I think it's a shop for a sightseeing memory or for when you want a meal in a nice atmosphere, rather than an everyday lunch.

The atmosphere inside is supremely luxurious, and the staff's service is wonderful, so it has value as an “experience.” However, if it competes purely on “the taste of Okinawa soba,” compared with other shops, my honest feeling is that it ends up with a slightly harsher rating in terms of cost performance 😅
But the contrast of pouring the soup yourself from a kettle in this luxurious space was fun, and it's the perfect shop for a conversation topic! Thank you for the meal 🙏

宮古そば なかよし.name: Miyako Soba Nakayoshi
宮古そば なかよし.desc: An old-fashioned diner run single-handedly by a grandma. You can enjoy traditional-style Miyako soba, with a distinctive, slightly sweet soy-sauce-based broth and the toppings hidden under the noodles. A wide-ranging menu that also includes goat soba and curry.
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet), with some additions of my own.
This time I went to "Miyako Soba Nakayoshi" in Shimashi, Ginowan! I ate here in November 2024😄
Miyako Soba Nakayoshi
Miyako Soba Nakayoshi

"Nakayoshi" is on the ground floor of an apartment building, and its bright exterior in orange and yellow catches the eye. The noren (shop curtain) at the entrance reads "Miyako Soba Nakayoshi," and an "Open" sign was hanging too. Beer crates were stacked in front of the shop, giving it a somehow nostalgic look😌
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

Step inside and you'll find an old-fashioned diner-style interior. All kinds of menu placards are posted on the walls, and I really got the feeling that this is a shop long loved by the locals🎫 It seems a grandma runs the place by herself, so you may need to be prepared to wait a little when it's busy.
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall

Looking at the menu posted on the wall, there's plenty of variety, from standard dishes like "goat soba," "soki soba," and "vegetable soba" to "katsu curry" and "curry rice." Prices are reasonable too, in the ¥600 to ¥900 range👍 This time I decided to order the "Miyako soba" that's in the shop's name!

After a short wait, the "Miyako soba" arrived. At first glance it looks simple, like just noodles topped with green onion, but that's the hallmark of Miyako soba😄 The toppings are hidden at the bottom; digging around, I found braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and fish cake (kamaboko).
Miyako soba, large ¥700
Miyako soba, large ¥700 (fish cake and braised pork belly were hiding under the noodles😄)

First, a sip of the broth. The color is a little dark, and it looks like the broth of Tojin soba. It gives a different impression from the bonito broth or pork bone broth of typical Okinawa soba. If anything, it's soy-sauce-based with a bit of sweetness, with a distinctive flavor a bit like chicken broth. This is Miyako soba with a unique broth🤔
Miyako soba, large ¥700

Next, the noodles. They're the thin, straight noodles characteristic of Miyako soba, with a softish texture😋 The braised pork belly hidden at the bottom had a firm chew, with a somewhat strong sinewy texture. The fish cake, though simple, makes a nice accent too.

I think this is a shop where you can enjoy Miyako soba in its true form. I was able to savor a flavor different from the Okinawa soba at other shops. Since the grandma runs it alone, things look a little hard when it's crowded, but I think it's a good shop where you can feel the local taste, all of that included. If you want to experience Miyako's food culture, please stop by😊
Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty. Everyone, please do pay a visit to "Miyako Soba Nakayoshi"! Next time I'll introduce yet another Okinawa soba shop, so stay tuned~🍜✨

From the menu, I decided to go with the shop's signature dish, the "original soki soba." It's a reunion after a full four years, since I ate it at the main shop in Nago! Looking forward to that old-fashioned taste, I entered the shop feeling excited.

The shop is spacious, with local TV shows playing and the history of Okinawa soba and the shop's commitments displayed on the walls; it really feels like "a diner rooted in the community"🏠. Not just tourists but plenty of local regulars were there too, and it left an impression how everyone was relaxing and enjoying their meal.
Inside the shop
Well, after a while the "original soki soba"🍜 arrived.
Original soki soba, large ¥960

A big chunk of meat is plopped right on top; the volume is huge and it's really impressive! When I took my first sip of the broth right away...✨ the richness of the pork bone comes through clearly, and a deep flavor spreads out.
Original soki soba, large ¥960
Next, a scoop of noodles. The house-made noodles here are thick, and while soft, they're characterized by a chewy, springy bounce.

And then the meat of the "soki," which you could call the star of this soki soba. Because it's slowly simmered in a secret sweet sauce, its soft, falling-apart texture is irresistible. The sweet-and-savory sauce has soaked in deeply, and with every bite umami overflows in your mouth. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) in particular seem to melt the moment you put them in your mouth, and they go perfectly with the sauce. I guess this flavor is a skill that comes from many years of experience🤲.

The "original soki soba" from Gabusoka soba, tasted for the first time in four years, had the same reliable deliciousness as ever. There are no flashy twists or special surprises, but I felt that this "usual taste" is the reason it continues to be loved locally. It's no wonder so many regulars come, and this sense of reassurance is the very essence of Okinawa soba✨. It makes me feel relieved every time I visit.
Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty. It's ★3 in the sense of "reliable deliciousness." As a bowl you can eat with peace of mind and enjoy, I'm sure it will go on being loved for a long time😆

つるりんこう.name: Tsururinko
つるりんこう.desc: A neighborhood soba shop in a salmon-pink building in a residential area of Kaiho, Okinawa City. In a Showa-retro interior, you get a classic broth where the sweetness of pork bone is the star, with three bone-in pork ribs. The breadth of its menu, a hybrid of neighborhood diner and soba shop, is also part of the appeal.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT o3), with some additions of my own lol

I ate here in December 2024😄 Today I dropped by "Tsururinko," which stands alone in a residential area of Kaiho, Okinawa City, right at its 11 o'clock opening. The big signs "Oki," "na," "wa," "soba" displayed boldly on the salmon-pink building stand out even from afar; it truly has the air of a "neighborhood soba shop"😊.
Tsururinko
Tsururinko

The gradient noren at the entrance shades from red to golden yellow, and the red cut-out letters of the shop's name are a little Showa-retro and cute. Customers kept coming in one after another the moment it opened, and it warmed my heart to think, "Ah, this shop is loved by the locals."
Inside the shop

Step inside and you're welcomed by wood-grain wainscoting, a Showa-era tiled ceiling, and the soft glow of round rattan lamps. There's raised tatami seating in the back and table seating in the front, and both have a menu, a thermos of tea, and a large condiment holder, giving a reassuring feeling like being at your family home.
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall

The wall is lined with wooden-board menus. Besides soki soba, braised pork belly soba, and vegetable soba, there are also champuru, tonkatsu sets, and even fried rice; I was impressed by the broad range, a hybrid of "neighborhood diner" and "soba shop"👍
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Now, what I came for this time was the soki soba, large (¥780). Before long, the bowl arrived on a black square tray along with an empty small plate.
Soki soba, large ¥780

First, a spoonful of the broth. The sweetness of pork bone spreads gently, and there's a reassuring feeling that made me nod, "This is the classic...!" The aroma of the bonito broth is hidden well in the background, and the richness of the pork is the star.
Soki soba, large ¥780
The noodles are medium-thick and straight. They're cooked on the soft side.
The topping is three hefty bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki). The soki are seasoned firmly sweet with soy sauce and brown sugar. There's some sinewy texture and small bones.

Rating (9/15): Overall, the soki soba at "Tsururinko" may not be flashy, but it was a bowl full of reassurance, like "this is the daily soba of Okinawa City residents." 796（ナンクル）.name: 796 (Nankuru)
796（ナンクル）.desc: Provisional #6 (12/15, 3rd visit). The No.1 agu-broth shop, in Chuo, Okinawa City. A cloudy white broth that's pork-bone-based yet not too heavy, by far the creamiest and richest. It clings superbly to the thick, wavy noodles. There's also the famous soki soba and unusual monthly specials.
t: (3rd visit) This article was created with AI (Claude 4 Sonnet), with some additions of my own lol🍜✨ I ate here in December 2024.

This time I joined the Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally for the first time in a while, and revisited "796 (Nankuru)" in Chuo, Okinawa City, which I've already introduced among my recommended shops😊 This was my third visit here, and no matter how many times I eat it, it's reliably delicious; it's an Okinawa soba shop especially proud of its rich broth made with agu pork.
The Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally card. This time I revisited with this in hand
Menu: Supreme Soki Soba ¥980 (rich agu-broth soup)
Menu: Supreme Yushi-dofu Soba ¥850
Menu: Herb-Scented Butter Chicken Soba ¥980
Menu: Butter Chicken Curry Soba, recommended 3-item set ¥1,280
December's monthly special Okinawa soba, "Hokkaido Charred Miso Butter Soba" ¥1,080
Explanation of the order sheet (a style where you choose your soba, noodles, meat, and toppings and fill them in)

This time I ordered the "soki soba" with a soft-boiled egg topping. I've had it several times before, so I waited in the shop for a while expecting its reliable deliciousness. Looking at the bowl when it was brought out, the rich-looking broth really whets the appetite🤤
Soki soba (soft-boiled egg topping) ¥1,080 (soki soba ¥980, soft-boiled egg ¥100)

First, as usual, I taste the broth. The pork bone broth based on agu pork is by far the creamiest and richest of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at😋 When you take a sip, a mellow umami spreads out, and you can also taste the refined sweetness unique to agu pork. Despite being this rich, it isn't too heavy, and the exquisite balance that makes you want to drink it all to the last drop is wonderful. As a pork-bone-based Okinawa soba shop, I definitely think it's the most delicious.
Soki soba (soft-boiled egg topping) ¥1,080 (soki soba ¥980, soft-boiled egg ¥100)

Next, the noodles. These also have their reliably chewy texture and cling superbly to the rich broth. The thick, wavy noodles grab hold of the broth, so you can savor the umami of the agu broth with every bite. The noodle texture is the same as last time, with firm springiness yet a gentle mouthfeel, and delicious✨

This time I ordered a soft-boiled egg as a topping, but this turned out a bit disappointing😅 The egg was served cold, so the temperature difference with the piping-hot broth bothered me. The soft-boiled doneness was good, but I wish it had been served a little warmer.

As for the soki, compared to previous visits, some sinewy texture remained, and it felt a little lacking in that melt-in-your-mouth tenderness. I had the impression it used to be simmered softer, so maybe it comes down to cooking timing or individual variation.

Actually, this shop recently started selling online through an e-commerce site, so I once ordered enough for my family online and tried it at home. However, since it's shipped chilled, it couldn't match the freshly made deliciousness of eating it at the shop, and it felt pricey too💦 Okinawa soba really is best enjoyed piping hot at the shop.

Even so, the quality of the broth and noodles is as high as ever, and the rich deliciousness of the agu broth is something special you can't taste anywhere else. Even on my third visit, that deliciousness hasn't changed, and I can well understand why people want to come back😊

In the stamp rally you end up going around all sorts of shops, but having a delicious shop as a benchmark makes it easier to compare with other shops. Nankuru is definitely one of those benchmark shops.

Rating (12/15): Nankuru delivered reliable deliciousness again this time. The rich agu broth is superb as always, and it pairs perfectly with the noodles. The soft-boiled egg and the condition of the soki were a little disappointing, but overall I think it maintains a high level. When you're in the Okinawa City area, it's a recommended Okinawa soba shop I'd love for you to try at least once✨

When you open the glass door at the entrance, a fairly spacious interior with the warmth of wood opens up✨ The area around the counter feels a bit cluttered, but that has its own charm too. Handwritten menus line the walls, and there's a homey, very Okinawan atmosphere.
Inside the shop
Menu posted in the shop
This time I ordered the "soki soba (large)" from the menu!🍜
Soki soba, large ¥800
The soba that was brought out after a while looks simple, like old-fashioned Okinawa soba. The broth is a clear golden color, bonito-based🐟 It's pretty ordinary.
Soki soba, large ¥800

The noodles are medium-thick and gently wavy. Cooked on the soft side. Personally I like a bit more firmness, but this too gives a feeling of old-fashioned Okinawa soba🍜 However, even though I ordered a large, the amount of noodles felt small compared to other Okinawa soba shops🤔

The soki topping has a light seasoning and is understated. But when I ate it, it was quite sinewy, and my impression was it was mostly bone with little meat to eat🥩 I'd have been happier if it were simmered until falling-apart tender.

The chili heat hits harder than regular kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori), and the vinegar's sourness is strong too🌶️ Adding them to the broth gives it a punchy flavor, so opinions may be divided, but I recommend them to people who like spicy food.
The shop was bustling with customers, and I could tell it's a popular diner👪

The broth and noodles in particular are excellent, and I think it's an irresistible bowl for Okinawa soba lovers. The location is convenient too, so please stop by when you visit Urasoe. You can enjoy authentic Okinawa soba in a lively atmosphere, mingling with the locals. Okinawa soba lovers, Soba Senmon Tedako is a shop you should check out! Next time, please visit it yourselves. I'm sure you'll discover a new side of Okinawa soba's appeal 😉

そば屋よしこ.name: Sobaya Yoshiko
そば屋よしこ.desc: A long-established shop with a yellow sign standing at the gateway to Soba Road (Prefectural Route 84). Featured on Horiemon's Teriyaki app, its specialty is a hearty pig's feet soba with three big pieces of pig's feet (tebichi) topped with lettuce.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and partly edited by me lol 🍜✨

I ate here in November 2024 😄 This time I'd like to introduce "Sobaya Yoshiko" in Izumi, Motobu Town. This shop was featured on Horiemon's Teriyaki app, and it's a place I'd been curious about for a while 🔍
It's featured on Horiemon's Teriyaki app 😆
Sobaya Yoshiko
Sobaya Yoshiko
Shop entrance

Located along Prefectural Route 84, this is a long-established soba shop that has been loved by locals for many years. Its bright yellow sign is the landmark, and the noren (shop curtain) reading "Yoshiko Soba" flutters in the wind 🏮
Inside, there's an old-fashioned atmosphere, and many photos and autographs were posted on the walls. It was bustling with local customers and tourists, and lots of people came in that day too 😄
Inside the shop
Looking at the menu, it lists classic dishes like soki soba, pig's feet (tebichi) soba, and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba. The menu has photos, so it's easy to understand 👍
Menu
Menu
This time I ordered the "Pig's Feet Soba" that was featured on Horiemon's Teriyaki app. Tebichi means pig's feet; it's packed with collagen and is a popular topping among women too 🐷

After waiting a while, the "Pig's Feet Soba" was brought out. First, the visual impact! Like "Oshiro Soba" in Okita, Nago, which I introduce among my "Okinawa soba shops that don't fall short of my recommended shops," it's distinctive for being topped with lettuce 🥬
Pig's feet (tebichi) soba, large ¥850
As always, I start by tasting the broth. This shop's broth is a blended stock of pork bone, bonito, and kelp, with a gentle flavor where the bonito comes through a bit 😋
Pig's feet (tebichi) soba, large ¥850
Next, the noodles. The medium-thick, straight, softish noodles cling well to the broth and are decently tasty 🍜

And as for the pig's feet (tebichi) topping, there are three big pieces, making it very voluminous! They're slowly simmered, so the meat is meltingly soft and tender. Packed with collagen, it seems good for your skin too ✨
After finishing, I was left with a warm feeling of nostalgia. It was a bowl that made me understand why it's been loved for so long by locals and tourists alike 😌

By the way, on Horiemon's Teriyaki app this shop's pig's feet soba is introduced as a recommendation, and it is decently tasty, but I thought the pig's feet soba at "Nanbu Soba" in Shiozaki, Itoman, was tastier than this one 🎵
Rating (9/15): It's decently tasty. It's a shop popular with locals and tourists, so why not stop by when you head toward Motobu Town? 😊

そば＆酒膳処一本松.name: Soba & Shuzen-dokoro Ipponmatsu
そば＆酒膳処一本松.desc: An izakaya at night that serves Okinawa soba lunches during the day. It's a treasure trove of unusual dishes like taco soba, tomato sauce soba, and tropical soba, and its signature is the soupless dandan-noodle-style "Okinawan-Style Mapo Soba." The chewy fresh noodles are delicious.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 to Feb 29, 2024)," and I went here as my 12th of 34 shops 😊
Soba & Shuzen-dokoro Ipponmatsu. I thought it was just an izakaya (;^ω^)
I'd thought this shop was an ordinary izakaya, but thanks to this stamp rally I learned for the first time that they do Okinawa soba lunches at midday (;^ω^)
The interior does feel like an izakaya, but this time I decided to order the "Okinawan-Style Mapo Soba" that was featured in the stamp rally booklet.
This dish was also featured at the very beginning of the menu. Is it their top pick, I wonder?
It was featured at the very beginning of the menu: "Okinawan-Style Mapo Soba"
After ordering, as I flipped through the menu, I noticed that Ipponmatsu has quite an array of unusual Okinawa soba dishes 😁
This is "Tomato Sauce Soba," which I think was developed for the Okinawa soba stamp rally two years ago. I'm curious what it tastes like lol
A pasta-style (vongole?) Okinawa soba, and a pork-and-egg Okinawa soba lol. Quirky.
The pig's feet (tebichi) soba is normal, but the menu photo above is apparently "Taco Soba." I wonder what that's like (;^ω^)
Vegetable soba and squid ink soba. These are normal.
Dandan noodle soba and pork bone soba. These are fairly normal too.
Mapo tofu soba: this one looks soupier than what I ordered. "Braised Pork Belly Cheese Soba": this one's quirky too 😊
Curry soba and pork offal (nakami) soba. These are pretty common.
"Kake Soba" and "Grated Yam Soba." Unusual ones 🤗
Apparently this is "Tropical Soba." It seems to be topped with pineapple too (;^ω^)
While I was enjoying looking at all the quirky dishes, the "Okinawan-Style Mapo Soba" I ordered arrived.
Okinawan-style mapo soba ¥950
Usually I'd taste the broth, but this Okinawa soba is like soupless dandan noodles; instead of broth, it's mapo tofu sitting on top of Okinawa soba noodles.
So I decided to eat it by mixing the mapo tofu with the noodles 😊

The noodles seem to be fresh noodles, with a chewy texture, and they're delicious 😋 I'd imagined the mapo tofu would be a bit spicy, but it's not spicy at all; this is a flavor even kids would have no problem with 😁
The crunchy texture of the onions is a nice accent.

Rating (9.5/15): It was an Okinawa soba like a mapo tofu version of soupless dandan noodles 😊 The fresh noodles had a chewy texture and were delicious. Since it's mapo tofu, personally I'd have liked it a bit spicy.

たこ焼きちゃんぽん.name: Takoyaki Champon
たこ焼きちゃんぽん.desc: A shop with outstanding value for money in the characterful Chuo Ichibangai area of Okinawa City. Vegetable soba at an astonishing ¥400, with a gentle pork bone broth and plenty of vegetables. A welcome find in this era of rising prices.
t: I ate here in February 2024 😄
Takoyaki Champon (it's across from Densuke Shoten in Chuo Ichibangai, Okinawa City 😆)
Menu posted inside the shop (cheap, right 😄)
Menu posted inside the shop (cheap, right 😄)
Menu posted inside the shop (cheap, right 😄)

This is the menu posted inside the shop, and everything is at reasonable prices you won't find at other shops 😄 With so many products and shops raising prices due to soaring costs and wage increases, can they really make a profit at these prices? Maybe they have another source of income lol
From the menu I decided to order the super-reasonable "Vegetable Soba." ¥400, so cheap 😄
Vegetable soba ¥400
The vegetable soba arrived. It has a decent amount of volume 😄 First I taste the broth.
It's a gentle broth with a bit of a pork bone base coming through. Decently tasty.
Vegetable soba ¥400

The noodles are medium-thick, straight, and soft. For toppings, egg and pork luncheon meat (Spam) are cut into thin strips and added as accents. There's quite a lot of vegetables, and the seasoning is on the light side. I'm always eating Okinawa soba that's nothing but carbs and meat, so getting some vegetables in seems to make my nutritional balance a little better 😆
Rating (9/15): A great-value Okinawa soba in the characterful Chuo Ichibangai area of Okinawa City. The taste is decently good too, so why not give it a try at least once 😄

だるまそば（読谷村）.name: Daruma Soba (Yomitan Village)
だるまそば（読谷村）.desc: The second branch of "Daruma Soba" in Yamazato, Okinawa City, a hybrid shop combined with the charcoal-grill izakaya "Sumiya." Its pride is the soft-bone soba in a rich, hearty broth with plenty of bonito flavor, a deep taste only an izakaya could create, a bit different from the first shop. Relax in its tatami-seating style.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) and partly edited by me lol 🍜✨

I ate here in January 2025 😄 This time I visited "Daruma Soba" in Sobe, Yomitan Village. Actually, this shop is the second branch of "Daruma Soba" in Yamazato, Okinawa City. It's combined with an izakaya called "Sumiya," so I headed right over to see what kind of Okinawa soba they serve! 😄
Daruma Soba
Daruma Soba (shop entrance)
By the way, this is "Daruma Soba" in Yamazato, Okinawa City (the daruma logos really do look alike 😆)

The interior has a warm, wood-based design, and it's a tatami-seating style where you take off your shoes and step up. 🏮 It has a casual izakaya-like feel, and its charm is that you can enjoy Okinawa soba while relaxing at your leisure.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Ticket machine
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu (there's a dinner menu too)
The menu is extensive, so you can enjoy not just Okinawa soba but also lunch sets and all kinds of Okinawan dishes. Okinawa soba made by an izakaya, so my expectations rose a bit! ✨
This time, from the menu, I ordered the "Soft-Bone Soba (Medium)."
Soft-bone soba, medium ¥800

The broth has a rich flavor with plenty of bonito broth coming through. As you'd expect from an izakaya making it, you can really taste the depth. Its defining feature is a rich broth for which the word "hearty" is a perfect fit. It's a little different from the broth at a typical Okinawa soba shop; if anything, it's a somewhat distinctive flavor that feels packed with the izakaya's particular care. Maybe this is the reason the taste differs between the second and first shops.
Soft-bone soba, medium ¥800
The noodles are medium-thick wavy noodles, but they have a surprisingly soft texture 🍝

The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) 🍖 are well seasoned through and have a tender texture. However, they're not completely fall-apart tender; a bit of sinewy texture remains. The broth also has an oily quality, so I think it'll be irresistible for people who like rich, hearty flavors 🎉

Rating (10.5/15): Looking at it overall, I really feel this shop serves Okinawa soba with a good balance of noodles, broth, and toppings. They say it tastes different from the first shop in Yamazato, Okinawa City, and personally I found this second branch in Sobe, Yomitan Village, tastier. It's a bowl I can truly recommend to anyone who likes hearty flavors. Its unique depth and richness are something only an izakaya could deliver. If you ever head toward Yomitan Village, please do stop by at least once 😋

八重善.name: Yaezen
八重善.desc: A shop standing in the fiercely competitive stretch of the Okinawa Soba Highway (Prefectural Route 84). It offers good-value set menus that pair a gentle soup rich with bonito broth with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) and two small side dishes. Also known for its squid ink soba.
t: Prefectural Route 84, known as the "Okinawa Soba Highway," is a fiercely competitive area with lots of Okinawa soba shops, and in May 2023 I went to eat at one of them, "Yaezen" 😄
Yaezen

I went in at lunchtime on a weekday, but there weren't that many customers and I got in right away 😄　The staff bring the menu to your table and take it back right after you order, so it isn't left on the table, and I forgot to take a photo of it ^^;　Sorry m(_ _)m
The "recommended menu" items are all set meals, and this time I ordered the "Soki Soba Set (small)."
"Soki Soba Set (small)" ¥880

Along with a small soki soba, it came with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) (seasoned mixed rice), which in Okinawa is a standard at home for celebrations and as an offering at the family Buddhist altar, a small dish of nigana? (it looked something like that; I don't think it was nigana) dressed with canned tuna, a small dish of boiled spinach with dried baby sardines, pickled red ginger for the soba, and, though it's not in the photo, yellow fukujinzuke pickles behind the soba. A pretty decent amount of food 😆

The soki soba has a gentle flavor while the bonito broth comes through, and it's delicious 😋　The noodles were a medium-thin straight type and slightly on the soft side. The pork spare ribs (soki) had an ordinary seasoning, were tender, and had soaked up the flavor nicely; they were delicious.

Rating (9.5/15): The bonito broth soup is nice ✌. Overall it was solidly tasty too. There are still so many more Okinawa soba shops along the "Okinawa Soba Highway" on Route 84, and it really hit me that I've still got a long way to go before conquering them all ^^;　I'll keep making the rounds steadily while enjoying myself 😄

八重食堂.name: Yae Shokudo
八重食堂.desc: A long-established shop in downtown Nago, founded in 1973. Its famous signature is the unique style where you pour the soup yourself from a kettle into a bowl holding only noodles and toppings. A gentle, clear bonito broth with the flat noodles typical of Nago and tender pork spare ribs (soki). Reasonably priced, with soki soba at ¥500.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," so I ate here in July 2020 😄
Yae Soba (it's in downtown Nago, a fiercely competitive area for soba shops lol. It has character, doesn't it)
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Yae Shokudo" is featured as shop 3 of 41
I ordered the "Soki Soba," which was introduced with a photo in the map
Soki soba　¥500　Cheap ^^;

The special feature here is that a bowl with just the noodles (no soup) and the toppings is placed on the table, and the soup is brought in a kettle ^^;　This system is unique to Yae Shokudo 😁　The soup is a clear bonito broth with a gentle flavor. The noodles are the flat type. The pork spare ribs (soki) are tender and delicious too. Since the soup alone comes in a kettle, you can drink plenty of broth 😄
Rating (9/15): Yae Shokudo, with its style of bringing the soup in a kettle, is famous. Please give it a try at least once.
PS: There's no parking lot, so you'll have to use a nearby coin parking lot (¥200).

前田食堂（名護店）.name: Maeda Shokudo (Nago branch)
前田食堂（名護店）.desc: The second Nago branch of the famous "Maeda Shokudo" in Ogimi Village. Its signature "Beef Soba" has overwhelming volume with a towering mountain of bean sprouts, and a punchy, peppery soup. Take it on when you're hungry.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," and I ate here in December 2020 😄
Maeda Shokudo, Nago branch
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Maeda Shokudo, Nago branch" is featured as shop 38 of 41
Menu
When you say "Maeda Shokudo," the original is in Ogimi Village, but this shop is the second branch. I ordered the "Beef Soba," which is famous at the main shop too 😄
Beef soba　¥800　There it is! The impact is way too much lol

I went to the main shop in Ogimi Village quite a long time ago, and the second branch is the same: the portions are as generous as ever ^^;　A huge heap of bean sprouts, and the soup is peppery and has a punch 😄　You can't reach the noodles unless you eat the beef and bean sprouts first ^^;　If you're a light eater, the small size is better.
Rating (9/15): I think every menu item at Maeda Shokudo comes in a big portion, so when you visit, please come on an empty stomach ☺

千代.name: Chiyo
千代.desc: A shop in Kin Town, the spring training camp site of the Rakuten Eagles (Mendokoro Chiyo). Inside are tatami-mat seating areas, with rows of autographs from pro baseball players and celebrities such as HY. Its signature is Chiyo Soba, with a slightly rich pork bone-based soup and chewy medium-thin straight noodles. It also has a sister shop in Osaka.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) and partly added to by me lol 🍜✨
I ate here in October 2024 😊　This time I'm introducing "Chiyo Soba" in Kin Town 😊
Chiyo

This shop operates in Kin Town, known as the spring training camp site of the Tohoku Rakuten Golden Eagles. Lots of autograph boards from baseball players are displayed inside, giving it an atmosphere baseball fans will love 😆
Pro baseball players' autographs displayed inside the shop
Celebrities' autographs displayed inside the shop (there's HY's autograph 😄)
Inside the shop
Menu
Inside, tatami-mat seating areas spread out, and it has a calm atmosphere. Looking at the menu, "Chiyo Soba" is listed at the top as the signature item, so this time I decided to order it.
Chiyo Soba (large)　¥950
First, a sip of the soup. The pork bone-based soup has a firm saltiness and is seasoned on the rich side. This might be a matter of personal preference 🤔
Chiyo Soba (large)　¥950

Next, the noodles. They're a medium-thin straight type, and although the shop doesn't advertise it, they might be homemade fresh noodles. They have a chewy texture and moderate firmness, and my impression was that they're quite tasty 😋

The kelp topping is shredded and makes a nice accent. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) had a firm texture, and I was bothered that a bit of sinewy texture remained. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), by contrast, were stewed until meltingly tender, but these also seemed to have a slight sinewy texture left.
As it turns out, this shop also has a sister shop in Osaka. It's great that you can enjoy the taste of Okinawa on the mainland too 😄

Rating (9/15): When you come to Kin Town, why not stop by between watching the baseball camp? Especially for baseball fans, I think it'll be a rare spot where you can enjoy a meal while gazing at the players' autographs 😊

南乃畑.name: Minami no Hata
南乃畑.desc: An Okinawan restaurant with an attached farmers' market inside "Wansaka Oura Park" on Nago's east coast. It's particular about fresh local ingredients such as meat and vegetables, and its signature is the "Minami no Hata Soba," topped with everything—pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and pork spare ribs (soki)—plus fuchiba (mugwort). There are outdoor tables too.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," and I ate here in February 2021 😄
Minami no Hata (inside Wansaka Oura Park)
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Minami no Hata" is featured as shop 21 of 41
Minami no Hata is apparently particular about fresh ingredients, using local meat and vegetables. This time I ordered the "Minami no Hata Soba," which was introduced in the soba map 😄
Minami no Hata Soba　¥800
A soup with bonito flavor and rich broth, topped with everything—jiggly pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and pork spare ribs (soki)—plus fuchiba (mugwort). Solidly tasty 😁

Rating (9/15): It's also fairly close to "Kanucha Bay Resort" from here, so how about it when you're staying there, or driving or sightseeing along the east coast of northern Okinawa Island? It's a quiet place, so on a nice day, how about a leisurely meal at the outdoor tables? ✌

南部そば.name: Nanbu Soba
南部そば.desc: Provisional #7 (13.5/15). A popular shop on the Itoman Road where the parking lot is full even before opening. Its selling point is the "Nanbu Soba," with two large, jiggly pig's feet (tebichi) stewed in black vinegar and ginger. Bonito-based soup with homemade medium-thin wavy noodles. Rated No.1 in the southern area.
t: In November 2022, on my way back from surfing at Suicide Cliff Point in Itoman, I tried eating here lol　It's along the National Route 331 bypass (Itoman Road), so it's easy to find.
It had only just opened (from 11:00), but the parking lot was already full lol
It had only just opened (from 11:00), but the parking lot in front of the shop was already full

I arrived right around the opening time of 11:00, but the parking lot in front of the shop already looked full. I thought it might be tough to eat here, but they also have a second? third? parking lot a little way off behind the shop, and after lining up for a bit, I made it inside safely ☺
When I went inside and looked at the menu, the "Nanbu Soba," which has the same name as the shop, caught my eye, so I ordered it.

Maybe pig's feet (tebichi) (stewed pig's trotters) are this shop's selling point as a topping, because two large pieces of pig's feet (tebichi) were sitting on top of the soba 😁　It was explained that the pig's feet (tebichi) are slowly stewed in a secret sauce with black vinegar and ginger until they're jiggly and soft, and packed with flavor and natural collagen. Looks delicious 🤤
Menu (Nanbu Soba = with two pig's feet/tebichi. Also bone-in pork rib soba (hon-soki), yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) soba, and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba)

This time I ordered the "Nanbu Soba (with two pieces of pig's feet/tebichi)," which shares the shop's name and seems to be its selling point. Some people from the mainland may not like pig's feet (tebichi), but there's also "bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) (Okinawan-style spare ribs, the area around the pork rib bones)" and "yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) (oboro tofu) soba," so I think those would be delicious too.

By the way, in Okinawa a (beef) steak to finish off a night of drinking is also famous, but basically I think pork is the main meat used in Okinawan cuisine. People eat every part of the pig, so much so that it's said "they eat everything except the oink," so pig's feet are delicious too ✌
I ordered the Nanbu Soba (large)　¥970

First, a sip of the soup. The bonito-based soup has a strong flavor, and the noodles are the homemade noodles also advertised on the outside of the building—medium-thin and wavy. They're smooth and chewy, and with the way the soup clings to the noodles, I felt it was delicious and in a higher class than the other shops I've eaten at ☺
This time I felt that, to some extent, "a shop popular enough to have a line = basically delicious" really does hold true. (*There are exceptions, so please be careful)

Rating (13.5/15): At this point (March 2023), I think it's the most delicious Okinawa soba shop in the southern area of Okinawa Island. It's relatively close to Naha Airport too, so how about it for tourists' last meal lol

幸っちゃんそば.name: Sacchan Soba
幸っちゃんそば.desc: Near Nago City Hall, a shop recommended by locals. The straight noodles kneaded with mozuku seaweed have a personality you won't find elsewhere. You can enjoy braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), pork spare ribs (soki) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) all at once. Also featured on "Bananaman Sekkaku Gourmet".
t: It isn't listed in the "Nago City Soba Map" that got me started on my Okinawa soba tour, but locals recommended it to me, so I went to eat there in July 2022😄
Sacchan Soba (located near Nago City Hall)
I ordered the "Sacchan Soba," which has the same name as the shop
Sacchan Soba　¥800

The straight noodles kneaded with mozuku seaweed are something no other shop has☺　The soup was a light bonito broth. For meat, you get to enjoy all sorts of kinds: braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), pork spare ribs (soki) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and it's delicious😋　Most of the customers are locals, and you can tell it's loved by the community.

Rating (9/15): Thanks to the locals' recommendation, it was delicious. What's more, by coincidence, after I ate here it was featured on "Bananaman Sekkaku Gourmet (Nago City edition)" on 2022.8.28, so I could see it's popular. The TV show may have brought in more tourists too, but please give it a try.

御殿（うどぅん）.name: Udun
御殿（うどぅん）.desc: An Okinawan restaurant on the Soba Kaido (Prefectural Route 84), across from Okashi Goten. Dishes include the signature "Udun Soba" and sea lettuce (āsa) soba served with jushi. A bonito-based broth with roundish thick noodles.
t: In July 2023 I went to eat at "Udun", across from Okashi Goten in Nago City, along Prefectural Route 84, which is known as the "Okinawa Soba Kaido (Okinawa Soba Road)"😄
"Okashi Goten" along Prefectural Route 84　"Udun" is behind where I took this photo😊
Entrance of the Okinawan restaurant "Udun"
Menu
The menu said the "Udun Soba," which shares the shop's name, was the No.1 recommendation, but I didn't feel like eating anything too heavy, so I ordered the "Āsa Soba"😄
Sea lettuce (āsa) soba (with jushi) ¥836
Every soba on the menu came with "jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice)"😄

First, as is my custom, I take a sip of the soup to taste it😁　It's a bonito-based broth, and it's perfectly tasty. Next I try the noodles together with the āsa (seaweed)😄　The āsa has a nice briny aroma of the sea, and the noodles are roundish, thick and soft, unlike anything at other shops. The noodles feel a little on the soft side.
The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and the pork spare ribs (soki) are also tender and well-seasoned, and perfectly tasty.

Rating (9/15): I think it's perfectly tasty, but what was disappointing was that when I walked in, the place wasn't full, just a fair number of customers, yet nobody showed me to a table. All the staff were in the kitchen and no one guided me like at other shops, so I was a bit at a loss (^_^;)　I just sat down at an empty seat and waited a while, but even when they brought food to other customers' tables, they didn't notice at all that I had just come in (^_^;)
After delivering the other customers' food they hurried back into the kitchen; maybe they're short-handed, as there seemed to be few staff.

Unable to wait any longer, I peeked into the kitchen and ordered, and they said, "Oh, you hadn't ordered yet?" They hadn't noticed at all that I was a new arrival (^_^;)　I couldn't help feeling that they might not be able to compete on Prefectural Route 84, known as the "Okinawa Soba Kaido." I came away with a disappointing impression lol

恩納そば.name: Onna Soba
恩納そば.desc: A long-established shop in the resort area along Route 58, close to Moon Beach and Tiger Beach. A homestyle taste with a strong bonito broth, and reasonable prices such as the ¥660 sea lettuce (āsa) soba with its aroma of the sea are part of its appeal. A shop bustling with tourists.
t: I ate here in June 2022😄
Onna Soba (along Route 58)
Since it's a tourist area, I was the only local customer lol
Tiger Beach is nearby
This time I ordered the sea lettuce (āsa) soba.
Sea lettuce (āsa) soba　¥660

The price is more reasonable than at other shops. The soup has a strong bonito broth, and the noodles are the straight type. The taste is homestyle😁　The āsa topping has the aroma of the sea and is delicious. In the latter half I added kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) to change up the flavor, so it was delicious twice over😄

Rating (9/15): Personally I recommend the Okinawa soba shops in Onna Village "Nakamura Soba" and "Kinchichi Soba Onna branch," but this one is also perfectly tasty, so if those are too crowded to get in, please try "Onna Soba."

だるまそば.name: Daruma Soba
だるまそば.desc: A locally popular shop in Yamazato, Okinawa City. The signature dish is the Daruma soba with everything on top: bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), pig's feet (tebichi), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), in a gentle bonito broth soup. The specialty “bone soup” is popular too, and it fills up at lunchtime.
t: I ate here in November 2022.
Daruma Soba
You buy with meal tickets, and I ordered the “Daruma soba,” which shares the shop's name and is sold as “meal ticket No. 1” 😊
Daruma soba　¥900

The soup has the gentle taste of bonito broth 😊　The toppings are everything: bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), pig's feet (tebichi), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) 🤤　The noodles are medium-thick and there's plenty of volume too 😆
Rating (9/15): Just plain delicious. It's loved by local customers, and at lunchtime it fills up with customers. Daruma Soba's “bone soup” is delicious too, so please give it a try once.

上間沖縄天ぷら店.name: Uema Okinawa Tempura-ten
上間沖縄天ぷら店.desc: A shop with a long display of tempura, a “tempura shop where you can also eat soba.” The Uema way is to top the soupy ¥590 braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba with fish tempura and sausage tempura. The free tempura bits are a nice touch too, a shop rooted in the local community.
t: *This article was created with “Chat gpt 5.2 (Thinking)” and partially edited by me. I went to eat here in February 2025 😄

On my Okinawa soba tour, this time I went to “Uema Okinawa Tempura-ten” in Minami-Tōbaru, Okinawa City~ 😊　As the name says, the “tempura-first” vibe is already coming out from outside, and there are banners up too, so it's a perfect landmark. There were a lot of customers coming and going, and even before going in I felt, “Ah, this is the kind of place rooted in the local community” 🍤
Uema Okinawa Tempura-ten
Inside the shop
There's even a menu of Okinawan memorial service dishes 😆
Inside the shop

When you enter the shop, the first thing you see is the tempura display. It's lined up in a long row, and honestly it gets me excited ✨　There's fish tempura, sausage tempura, and vegetable ones too; it feels like Okinawa's “tempura culture” turned straight into a shelf. The interior is bright and clean, and I also like how casual it is, where you can eat quickly and leave quickly. In fact, customers never stopped coming, and seeing what looked like regulars buying with practiced ease, I thought, shops like this are strong~ 😌

My order this time was the “braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba” topped with fish tempura and sausage tempura. Rather than an Okinawa soba shop, the feeling of “a tempura shop where you can also eat soba” might fit better. It was served fairly quickly, and the moment I received it, it was the kind where you go, “Oh, it's soupy.” The visual volume was pretty impressive, and the sense of satisfaction comes first, as soon as it's set on the table 😂
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba　¥590
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba　¥590 + (fish, sausage tempura) ¥250

The soup is a combined broth with a light touch of pork bone. It has richness, but the overall impression is that the saltiness is a bit strong. Opinions may be divided, but on days when you've sweated or days when you want something strong, it seems like it would hit the spot for a lot of people 👍
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba　¥590 + (fish, sausage tempura) ¥250
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba　¥590

The noodles are medium-thick flat noodles with a loose wave. The texture is on the soft side. Personally, my honest feeling is that I'd be happy if they had just one more level of springiness~ 😅　However, the soupy broth clings to them well. I think people who like soft noodles can get hooked without worry.

And the tempura toppings. The fish tempura has a fluffy batter, and when you dip it in the soup a little, the batter gets moist and becomes a different kind of delicious. The sausage tempura has a junky feel that needs no explanation, and when something like this goes in, the “Uema-ness” comes out all at once 😋　Being able to add tempura bits for free is a quietly nice touch too.

Rating (9/15): Honestly, my overall verdict lands on “Yeah, it's ordinary.” There's no sharp edge like “Super moving!” or “One of a kind!”, but precisely because of that, there's a stability that makes it usable every day. It makes sense that there are so many customers, and I think the “convenient strength” of being able to enjoy tempura along with it is this shop's appeal 😊　Next time I'd like to go after other tempura and have fun from the tempura side 🍤✨

Mendokoro Tiandā
Mendokoro Tiandā

When you enter the shop, wood-grain interior and a homey atmosphere spread out before you; it's a shop that somehow makes you feel nostalgic. Autograph boards displayed on the walls caught my eye, and I really felt that this is a shop loved by locals.
Inside the shop

From the menu, I ordered the “soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba with fuchiba noodles” 😋. The words “house-made fresh noodles” on the entrance door caught my eye, raising my expectations. I waited excitedly, wondering what the combination of noodles kneaded with fuchiba (mugwort) and the uniquely Okinawan soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) would taste like.
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba (fuchiba noodles) ¥990

The soba that came out was beautiful from the look of it to begin with ✨. The greenish flat (thick?) fuchiba noodles float in a clear, light bonito broth soup, and ginger and mitsuba are gently placed on top. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), simmered until melt-in-your-mouth tender and served on a separate plate, really whet the appetite too 🍖.

First, a sip of the soup… Ooh! The bonito broth spreads slowly, a gentle taste that isn't heavy 😌. It's light, yet you can properly feel the umami, so it's a taste that makes you feel more relieved with every sip.
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba (fuchiba noodles) ¥990

And the flat (thick?) noodles! These are firm and really satisfying to eat 💪. The springiness you feel the moment you put them in your mouth is irresistible. It's a texture that reminds me a bit of the noodles at “Ishigufu,” and personally I like it a lot 😊.

The noodles kneaded with fuchiba (mugwort) have a faint grassy aroma too, and you can feel the Okinawan character. They're full of flavor, and I felt they add an accent to the taste of Okinawa soba, which can tend to be monotonous 🌿.

Next, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). They're served on a separate plate, a trick to keep their flavor from transferring to the soup. The soki itself is tender enough to fall apart in your mouth ✨ However, a little sinew remains, giving a balance with some chewiness / bite. You can eat them down to the bone, so it's a dish where you can fully enjoy traditional Okinawan cuisine 😋.

And this time the “kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori)” was a bit unique. Generally the liquid type is common, but here a granular solid type is provided 🧂. Both the look and the taste are a little different, and this was a little surprise. The heat isn't that strong, so I enjoyed changing up the flavor while dissolving it bit by bit into the soup 👍.

Rating (9/15): It was a reassuring Okinawa soba that tasted just plain delicious. The firmness of the flat noodles and the flavor of the fuchiba were especially memorable, but some people might feel the noodles are on the hard side. The soup and the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) also came together in an ordinary, well-balanced way 😌.

識名そば.name: Shikina Soba
識名そば.desc: A popular shop near the World Heritage site Shikina-en. The selling points are a deep soup with a good balance of bonito and pork bone, and chewy house-made thin noodles. The extra-large braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba, limited to 3 servings on weekends, is first come, first served.
t: *I also had AI (Claude 3.5 sonnet) make this article, and I've edited and updated part of it myself lol

I'm Anji, an Okinawa soba blogger 😊 This time I went to “Shikina Soba” in Shikina, Naha City! On my Okinawa soba tour, I wonder how many shops this makes~ 🤔 I haven't counted, but I'm still nowhere near conquering them all, sa~ (Note: the AI is lying, so here's a correction. I've been to about 177 shops 😆). But I want to keep touring while enjoying each and every shop!

Well now, “Shikina Soba,” which I visited this time, has a conspicuous sign, so it was easy to find 😄 Looking at the exterior of the shop, it feels like a typical Okinawan shokudo, with a somehow nostalgic atmosphere 🏠
Shikina Soba
Shikina Soba

When you enter the shop, a meal ticket machine greets you. It's a shame it doesn't support cashless payment 👍 Looking at the menu, there's a wide variety of Okinawa soba! It's hard to decide. But this time I ordered the classic “soki soba” 😋

Actually I wanted to have the meal ticket machine's recommended top-left button, “extra-large braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba, limited to 3 servings on weekends,” but it was already sold out (^0^;) Too bad lol
The meal ticket machine installed near the shop entrance

The inside of the shop was bustling with customers. I went in right after opening, but the parking lot was full too, and I just barely got in (^0^;)　It feels like there are more tourists than locals. This raises my expectations~ 🔥
Menu (the words “house-made noodles” make me hopeful 😄)
Menu
Menu
Now, here comes the long-awaited “soki soba”! It looks delicious from the appearance alone 😍 Clear soup, plenty of green onions, and a big piece of soki on top.
Soki soba, large　¥850

As always, let's start by tasting the soup 🥄 Huh? Unexpected! I thought the bonito broth would hit hard at first, but I can clearly taste the pork bone flavor too. The balance of bonito and pork bone is exquisite, and if anything it's slightly bonito-based? The faint bonito flavor comes through, making it a deep taste. It's just plain delicious, but I don't think it has a standout characteristic~.
Soki soba, large　¥850

Next, let's go for the noodles! 🍜 They seem to use house-made noodles, a thin type. The chewy texture is nice~. They cling well to the soup too, and you can slurp them down smoothly~. I quite liked these! The house-made noodles are delicious 😋

And the toppings I was curious about, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki)~ 🍖 They look melt-in-your-mouth tender, but when I ate them they felt a bit dry. The sweet seasoning gives an Okinawan feel, but there are sinewy parts here and there, so the texture is uneven. Hmm, it might have been the best if they'd simmered them a bit more tender 😅

Looking at it overall, “Shikina Soba's” Okinawa soba is, I'd say, fairly delicious. There's no particularly surprising point, but it feels like an Okinawa soba with a stable taste. I think I understand why it's been loved by locals for a long time.
Now, let's do my usual Anji-style rating!
Rating (9.5/15): The noodles were the biggest selling point! The chewiness of the house-made noodles is irresistible for Okinawa soba lovers 😋

“Shikina Soba” is a little away from the tourist spots, but it was a lively shop bustling with tourists and locals. It's recommended for people sightseeing in Naha City or who want to get a little taste of the local atmosphere~.

However, it's a popular shop, so it may be crowded at lunchtime. When I went, I somehow just barely managed to park in the parking lot, but depending on the timing you might have to wait, so it might be good to visit with plenty of time to spare 😉

Finally, a little tip! Near “Shikina Soba” there's Shikina-en. It's a Ryukyu garden registered as a World Heritage site, a place where you can feel Okinawa's history and culture. It might be nice to take a little stroll after eating soba 🏯

Well, that's it for this Okinawa soba tour! Where should I go next~ 🤔 There must still be lots of delicious Okinawa soba shops in Okinawa. I'll keep bringing you the charm of Okinawa soba from here on!
Well then, see you next time! Have a good Okinawa soba life~ 🍜✨

沖縄そば 楚辺.name: Okinawa Soba Sobe
沖縄そば 楚辺.desc: A hugely popular shop with a striking old-folk-house-style building surrounded by trees. In the spacious interior lined with surfboards and celebrity autographs, the specialty is the “Three-Star Makanai Soba Set Meal” (with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki)), limited to 30 servings a day.
t: I went to eat here in March 2025 😄 This time my Okinawa soba tour brings me to “Okinawa Soba Sobe” in Sobe, Naha City. The moment I arrived in front of the shop, my first impression was “Whoa, this place has a strong vibe.”
Okinawa Soba Sobe's parking lot
Okinawa Soba Sobe

An entrance like an old folk house surrounded by trees, and a sign full of character. Even though it's in town, the air feels a little more relaxed just there, and I totally get why people who come sightseeing get excited. In fact, the guide signs were conspicuous too, and even before going inside, there was a clear sense of “this must be a popular shop.”
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

Inside, the spacious interior had surfboards on display and lots of celebrity autographs, and it was a very memorable space where Okinawan clutter mixed with touristy glamour 😊
Menu
