What I had this time was the “Three-Star Makanai Soba Set Meal,” limited to 30 servings a day. The name alone has a bit of a special feel, and since it's topped with three kinds, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), it's visually very satisfying. In fact, when it was brought out the bowl was quite luxurious, and I thought, “This is the kind that gets my hopes up.” The set meal comes with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice), a small side dish, and even mozuku in vinegar, so I think it's a welcome lineup for tourists in terms of volume too. You can taste various aspects of Okinawa soba in one set meal, so it's an easy-to-understand set for first-timers.
Three-Star Makanai Soba Set Meal　¥1,550

First, the soup: among combined broths, it's a type where the pork bone's presence comes a bit to the front. It's just plain delicious, but it doesn't quite reach a personality that sticks strongly in your memory; that was my impression.
Three-Star Makanai Soba Set Meal　¥1,550
The noodles are thin, straight, and on the soft side. People who want to enjoy solid firmness and a wheaty feel might find them a bit lacking.

The toppings are braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), a lineup that gets you pretty excited just looking at the names. It had volume visually too, and a glamour worthy of the name “Three-Star.” But when I ate it, overall it leaned light, and I was bothered that each had a little sinewy texture remaining. If you're going to enjoy three kinds of meat, I'd have been happy if they were a bit more melt-in-your-mouth, or if the differences between each cut came through more clearly.

On the other hand, what was good were the small side dishes rounding out the set meal. The mozuku in vinegar was refreshing and felt great for resetting my palate. The bean sprout namul quietly did a good job too, and when small dishes like these are properly delicious, the satisfaction of the whole set meal goes up. The jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) was also on the light side, a balance that doesn't get in the way of the soba's taste. This might be why it's supported by tourists and a wide range of ages.
The table

However, I want to be honest here. The shop's atmosphere, its size, the building with a sense of history, the number of autographs, the number of tourists, even the special feel of the limited menu, all of it was there, so my expectations had gone up quite a bit. But when I actually finished eating, “just plain delicious” was my most honest impression 😅 It's not bad at all, and it's properly delicious. But it's also a fact that in Naha and Okinawa there are shops that grab you more with “the power of the soba itself.” That's exactly why I thought the reason so many people gather at this shop isn't just the taste, but must largely be its appeal including the strength of word of mouth, the shop's history, its location that's easy to visit while sightseeing, and that atmosphere.

Rating (9/15): I think it suits people who want to enjoy Okinawa soba leisurely in a spacious interior while feeling the Okinawan atmosphere on their trip. On the other hand, for people who “just want to be wowed by the taste of the soba alone,” I felt there's a chance it might be a bit of a letdown. It's worth going once including the atmosphere, but it wasn't a bowl that made me strongly feel I absolutely want to eat it again when I revisit. Still, actually going to a popular shop like this and confirming with my own tongue “so this is the type it is” is also part of the fun of an Okinawa soba tour 🌺

りんくる食堂.name: Rinkuru Shokudo
りんくる食堂.desc: A café-like Okinawa soba shop in a renovated former foreigners' house. The signature "Rinkuru soba" is an everything-on-top style bowl with additive-free bonito broth, topped with sea lettuce, sweet chicken, mozuku, and more. Unusual items like mushroom soba and clam soba too.
t: I went to eat here in December 2023 😊 It was during the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", so I wanted to eat at a participating shop, but there weren't any nearby, so I decided to eat at this shop, which isn't part of the stamp rally but which I'd been curious about for a while.
Rinkuru Shokudo — it seems to be an Okinawa soba shop in a renovated foreigners' house 😄
Rinkuru Shokudo entrance

If you go a little into the seaward blocks off Route 58 in Chatan Town, there's a neighborhood of foreigners' houses, and this shop has renovated a former foreigners' house into a café-like atmosphere 😁
I went inside and checked the menu.
Menu
Menu
There are lots of kinds of Okinawa soba 😄 "Mushroom soba" and "clam soba" are menu items I'm seeing for the first time, ones other shops don't have.
Menu — this seems to be the side menu for the Okinawa soba 😆
This time I ordered the "Rinkuru soba", which shares the shop's name, sits at the top of the menu, and seems to be the recommendation lol
Rinkuru soba ¥950

The "Rinkuru soba" has arrived 😁 My eyes went to the toppings first. Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), thinly sliced omelet, mozuku, green onion, sea lettuce (āsa), and chicken — I thought it was like an "everything-on-top" Okinawa soba of the items this shop handles. It reminded me of Futami Soba in Nago City (introduced as a shop that holds its own against the recommended ones) lol

But first, as usual, the soup 😆 Mm, it's a bonito broth soup with a strong bonito flavor. As explained on the menu, they advertise no chemical seasonings, no colorings, and no preservatives, so they seem particular about their ingredients.

However, it reminded me of a recent national news story where a shop selling muffins at some event, with a similar organic mindset, sold them as kid-friendly muffins with no preservatives and half the sugar, but the people who ate them got food poisoning (^0^;)
Scientifically, chemical seasonings have the same components as natural ingredients, so I think you don't really need to worry about them, and extreme, excessive organic thinking calls for caution.
That said, this shop's soup is gentle with no problems at all, so rest assured 😄
Rinkuru soba ¥950
Next I try the noodles. The medium-thick straight noodles are a bit on the soft side.
As for the toppings, first, the sea lettuce has a briny aroma of the sea and is delicious 😆 It reminded me of the "āsa soba" at "Nakamura Soba" in Onna Village lol

I couldn't really tell whether the chicken was chicken tempura, fried chicken, or chicken nanban, but it had a sweetish seasoning and I thought it was very delicious. I thought this topping was a nice new one I'd never seen at other shops 😄 The braised pork belly, however, had a bit of a sinewy texture, which was a shame.

Rating (9.5/15): Simply tasty. The sea lettuce and chicken (tempura? fried? nanban?) toppings in particular were delicious, and I thought they were new toppings. The shop is in a foreigners' house, so I thought tourists can enjoy Okinawa soba in a nice atmosphere too — how about trying it once?

わぁ～家～.name: Waa-ya
わぁ～家～.desc: A diner on the grounds of Roadside Station Yui Yui Kunigami. In a nostalgic interior with checkered tablecloths, enjoy soki soba in an amber-colored soup. Perfect for a break while sightseeing in Yanbaru.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet), with some parts added by me lol 🍜✨
I ate here in October 2024 😄

This time I went to "Waa-ya" on the grounds of Roadside Station Yui Yui Kunigami in Okuma, Kunigami Village. Kunigami Village is a nature-rich area at the northern tip of Okinawa's main island, surrounded by the Yanbaru forest and beautiful seas, and it's popular as a sightseeing spot too 🌳🌊
Waa-ya

Roadside Station Yui Yui Kunigami is full of local specialties and tourist information, and it's a perfect spot for a break on a drive. "Waa-ya", on its grounds, is a popular shop not only with locals but with tourists too 😄
Inside the shop

When you go inside, the atmosphere feels somehow nostalgic. The tropical-style checkered tablecloths give it warmth. Looking at the menu, there were several Okinawan local dishes, starting with Okinawa soba. This time I decided to order the classic "soki soba" 🍜
Soki soba ¥850
After waiting a while, the "soki soba" was brought out. Medium-thick straight noodles in a clear amber soup, with the soki meat carefully arranged on top. First, as usual, I taste the soup.
Taking a sip of the soup, the pork bone broth had a slight kick, and the saltiness felt somewhat strong.
Next I have the noodles. Medium-thin straight noodles with a somewhat soft texture. They cling well to the soup, but personally I felt they could have a bit more bite.

The soki meat had a light seasoning and was simply tasty, but some parts still had quite a sinewy texture and were hard to eat. From what I heard before, this shop used to use inobuta (wild boar–pig hybrid) meat, but apparently it became hard to source and now it's regular pork. I wanted to try inobuta soki soba for the first time, so that was a little disappointing 😢

There were also several groups of what looked like tourists in the shop, and I could see them enjoying Okinawan food culture. When you make the trip to Kunigami Village, it's a spot where you can enjoy this Okinawa soba along with the nature of Yanbaru 🚗

Rating (9/15): The soup is pork-bone based with a salty kick and simply tasty. The noodles are on the soft side and easy to eat, but the soki meat was a bit sinewy, so it felt like it needed just a little more. If you stop by while sightseeing in Kunigami Village, I think it's worth trying once as a local flavor 😊

わざ家.area: Jitchaku, Urasoe (inside the National Theatre Okinawa)
わざ家.desc: A one-of-a-kind shop inside the National Theatre Okinawa. While flying a banner for "the original Ryukyu suba", it offers soy sauce ramen made with medium-thick fresh Okinawa soba noodles, Taiwanese ramen, and even lu rou fan — a shop of "ramen made with Okinawa soba noodles".
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude Haiku 4.5), with some parts added and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in January 2025 😁😊
The National Theatre Okinawa in Jitchaku, Urasoe City. Inside this facility, where you can fully enjoy Okinawa's traditional culture, there's a slightly unusual Okinawa soba shop. That's "Waza-ya".
Waza-ya (located inside the National Theatre Okinawa)
Waza-ya (located inside the National Theatre Okinawa)
Waza-ya (located inside the National Theatre Okinawa)
Meal ticket machine
🎭This time I got the "soy sauce ramen with lu rou fan" set. The banner proudly says "Ryukyu suba", so this definitely counts toward my Okinawa soba tour 😄
Inside the shop

When you enter the National Theatre Okinawa building, you see, a more modern and refined space than you'd imagine opens up. The thick bare-concrete pillars are striking, the ceilings are high, and the atmosphere is open. Like a café — no, even more contemporary, yet a mysterious space with a faint scent of the Ryukyus. 🪟Through the big windows you can see Okinawa's nature. Waza-ya, you see, has set up shop in a corner of this space. In front, a banner reading "The Original Ryukyu Suba Waza-ya" flutters prominently. Ordering is by ticket machine, and there's a really extensive lineup, from Okinawa soba–related items to Taiwanese ramen, and even gyoza and rice dishes.
Soy sauce ramen with lu rou fan ¥1,030

Well, here comes the "soy sauce ramen". 😍The soup seems to be based on rich pork bone, kombu, and bonito broth. But I couldn't even tell if it was soy sauce flavored — it's somehow complex, with a pretty rich, heavy taste. 🍲What I'm most curious about, you see, is this soup. Is it an Okinawa soba–style broth, or authentic ramen? The line between them is blurry. It's distinctive, but feels like something different from regular Okinawa soba.
Soy sauce ramen with lu rou fan ¥1,030

The biggest highlight, you see, is these noodles! 🤩They use medium-thick Okinawa soba noodles. Just from looking at them, you see, you can tell they're chewy. When you actually eat them, you see, they have the springy texture of fresh noodles. The noodles alone are completely Okinawa soba. This part is really well done. The toppings are basically ramen 😅 A big slice of chashu sits there prominently, and there's a soft-boiled egg on top too.

The lu rou fan, in the tradition of Taiwanese ramen, is pork simmered down in a miso flavor, piled generously over white rice. There's mitsuba on top too. This lu rou fan also has a pretty robust seasoning, and eating it together with the ramen boosts the satisfaction in one go. Overall the volume is more than enough. There's so much that I got a little worried whether I could finish it all by myself.

If I were to describe Waza-ya in one phrase, you see, it'd be "ramen made with Okinawa soba noodles". It's not completely Okinawa soba, but it's not completely ramen either. If anything, maybe it's more like "Okinawa soba in the shape of ramen". The banner saying "Ryukyu suba" also conveys that spirit of challenge. 😄It's precisely because the location, you see, is inside a cultural facility called the National Theatre Okinawa that a concept like this "fusion of tradition and novelty" might be so naturally accepted. It has an atmosphere where not only tourists but locals too can drop by casually.
Rating (9/15): It's ramen with Okinawa soba noodles (^0^;) Simply tasty.

アグーそば処 ひかり食堂.name: Agu Soba-dokoro Hikari Shokudo
アグーそば処 ひかり食堂.desc: A two-in-one shop: Hikari Shokudo by day and Shokuraku Shubo Juria by night. Its feature is that you can choose the soup, rich with Agu pork broth, from three types: rich, light, or blend. The signature Agu Hikari soba is topped with both braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs.
t: I went to eat here in March 2025 😄
This time I'm introducing "-Agu Soba-dokoro- Hikari Shokudo" in Meido, Okinawa City 😊
-Agu Soba-dokoro- Hikari Shokudo

The exterior has a calm design based on black, and at the entrance a lantern reading "Juria" catches the eye. In fact, this is a two-in-one shop that serves Okinawa soba as "Hikari Shokudo" during the day and transforms into an izakaya called "Shokuraku Shubo Juria" at night 🍺 It's open across a wide range of hours: 10:00 AM–2:00 PM for lunch and 5:00 PM–1:00 AM at night. It seems they're on Uber Eats too.
Meal ticket machine near the entrance
Menu posted on the wall

Ordering is by ticket machine. Looking at the menu, there's a full lineup of Agu soba items 😆 This time I ordered the shop's top recommendation, the "Agu Hikari soba (¥950)". It's a hearty bowl with both braised pork belly and soft-bone ribs. The interesting point of this soba is that you can choose the soup from three types: rich, light, or blend 🐷 When I asked the staff for a recommendation, they said "The blend is recommended", so I chose the blend without hesitation!
Agu Hikari soba (blend soup) ¥950

The "Agu Hikari soba" that appeared after a short wait is served in a black bowl and looks pretty good ✨ First, a sip of the soup. The Agu pork broth comes through firmly — full-bodied yet not heavy. I could also sense what seemed to be a bonito broth flavor, giving it a taste unique to the blend. The best of both rich and light, I guess? 😋
Agu Hikari soba (blend soup) ¥950
Next I try the noodles 🙏 The noodles are medium-thin and straight, with a softish texture.

The toppings — braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) — come in big, hearty chunks, and it's quite filling 😄 The seasoning is on the light side, perhaps to make the most of the Agu pork's own umami. The soft-bone pork ribs are tender, but some parts still had a bit of a sinewy texture. The braised pork belly has a strong sinewy texture with real chew, a properly meaty texture that's very filling 🐷
Right inside the entrance it's suddenly private rooms (^0^;)

The interior has a private-room layout, built to suit the nighttime izakaya business. But because right inside the entrance is the wall of a private room, you can't really see the staff... At first I was a little confused about who to call out to (lol) 😂 But once you've ordered at the ticket machine, all that's left is to wait leisurely, so no problem. On the wall there was something like a certificate for Okinawa-produced Agu pork, which shows their commitment to ingredients.

I've been around a fair number of shops that feature Agu pork, but being able to choose the soup style from three types, so you can customize it to your taste, is a nice point 😊 It was a simply tasty bowl!
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty Agu soba. Being able to choose the soup style is its distinctive feature 😊

アワセそば食堂.name: Awase Soba Shokudo
アワセそば食堂.desc: A long-established popular shop whose signature is a perfectly balanced soup where you can taste both bonito and pork bone at the same time. You can choose homemade flat or thin noodles, and the No. 1 most popular item is the sanmai-niku soba. The parking lot fills up at Sunday lunchtime.
t: I ate here in May 2023 😄
I came at lunchtime on a Sunday, but the parking lot was full (・・) After waiting a little, one space opened up, so I managed to get in 😊
Menu (their commitments are explained 😊)
Menu (the No. 1 to No. 3 most popular items are explained 😄)

Looking at the menu, I ordered the No. 1 most popular "sanmai-niku soba". You can choose flat or thin noodles, and when I asked the staff, they recommended the flat noodles, saying "the old-fashioned flat noodles are ordered a lot", so I ordered with flat noodles.
Sanmai-niku soba (large) ¥880
As always, I go around to shops that catch my interest with no prior information, so I took a first sip of the soup wondering, "Bonito broth?" "Pork bone broth?" 😄

The moment I drank it: "?" I couldn't immediately tell the base flavor of the soup, so I took another sip to check. I can taste bonito broth, and I can also taste pork bone broth — a soup flavor unlike any I've had so far.

At Okinawa soba shops up to now, even with a bonito-and-pork blended broth, it's usual for one flavor to be stronger, but at Awase Soba Shokudo you can taste both flavors, and I thought it was a perfect balance.
The homemade flat noodles have a soft bite. The braised pork belly topping is also tender and delicious 😄

Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. The soup lets you taste both bonito and pork bone, something other shops don't have. A long-established popular shop bustling with local customers. They also accept PayPay, and it was the first Okinawa soba shop where I got a receipt, so I plan to turn it into money using the method in another article ("[Points hacking] How to turn receipts into money (small change) (super steady-effort type)") 😄

シラノ.name: Shirano
シラノ.desc: A stylish, Western-style "Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop" run by an owner with a French cooking background. Starting with an appetizer of garlic toast, its soki soba in bonito soup is distinctive, letting you change the flavor with citrus condiments made from shikuwasa and tankan.
t: I ate here in March 2024 😄 I learned about this shop from the newspaper lol
Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop Shirano
Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop Shirano
Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop Shirano
What country's architecture does this look like? It's Western-style 😄 Different from the Okinawa soba shops I usually go to 😄
Near the entrance in front of the shop (it's in a peaceful, rural kind of place)
The entrance in front of the shop (it's on slightly elevated ground)

According to the newspaper article, it had only just opened in November 2023. The owner seems to be a chef with a French cooking background. That's why the building is Western-style like this — because of the French background 😁
When I went inside, since it was lunchtime, there were quite a lot of customers. The interior is Western-style, but the moment I entered there was a lovely smell of bonito broth 🤤
It seems to be based on a bonito and pork bone broth, but from the smell drifting through the shop, I thought the bonito was dominant lol
The counter seats inside (Western-style, isn't it)

I forgot to take a photo of the menu, but I ordered the "soki soba". Among the other items there was also "clam-broth Okinawa soba", which I thought looked delicious, but I was told it was "sold out" (^0^;) There was also a menu item called "spice curry soba", which also looked delicious and I hesitated, but I thought I should order the classic here after all, so I went with the "soki soba" 😁
Appetizer garlic toast
Before the Okinawa soba, garlic toast came out with "Here's your appetizer". Other shops don't have this style — just as the sign says, it really is an "Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop" 😁
The crispy toasted bread has a good garlic kick and is simply tasty.
Soki soba ¥850 (other shops don't have citrus condiments)

First I taste the soup. It's mainly bonito, combined with pork bone broth, and the soup seems to take cues from French technique. It's a soup that fills the shop with a lovely aroma, so I took a sip with high expectations.
As expected, the bonito comes through, and it's a simply tasty soup.
Soki soba ¥850
Next I have the noodles. They're homemade aged noodles, apparently rested for five days after being made before they're finished. Thin noodles, and I thought these were also just ordinary.
While enjoying the soup, noodles, and soki, in the second half I changed the flavor with condiments made from shikuwasa and tankan (Okinawan citrus), something other shops don't have.
A citrusy freshness gets added to the bonito broth soup, and I thought it was a new flavor, but they go well together — delicious.

Rating (9/15): A shop with a stylish Western-style exterior and interior. How about trying Okinawa soba made by an owner with a French cooking background at least once 😁 The citrus condiments go well with the bonito-forward soup, so why not try them? The location is peaceful and quiet, so you can enjoy your meal at a relaxed pace.

あがり家+.name: Agariya+
あがり家+.desc: A locally rooted shop on the grounds of MaxValu. The signature is the "Agariya Special", topped with fragrant charcoal-seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and a whole boiled egg. It's also fun that you can change up the flavor with wasabi as a condiment.
t: *This article was created based on AI (ChatGPT-4o) with some additions by me 😁
This time, in August 2024, I went to "Agariya+" in Iso, Urasoe City! The shop's atmosphere has a very local feel, with a scattering of customers who seemed to be regulars.
Agariya+ (it's on the grounds of MaxValu)
Agariya+ (it's on the grounds of MaxValu)
Menu
Menu (the creative soba look delicious too 😄)
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Inside the shop (a big stock of island liquor too 😆)
From the menu, what I had this time was the manager's recommendation, the "Agariya Special". Just from the name, it has a special feel, right ✨
Agariya Special　¥1,250

The first thing that caught my attention was the broth's unique flavor. It's a blended stock of pork bone and bonito, but the pork bone comes forward gently, and it has more depth than I expected. You can taste the bonito flavor too, with the pork bone base gently working: that's the balance. It's a solid flavor, but the way it isn't too heavy is nice, and it feels ordinary 😊.
Agariya Special　¥1,250

The noodles are medium-thin, finished on the soft side. I think I prefer a bit more chewiness. But the pairing of soft noodles and this broth is surprisingly good, and the way it spreads softly in your mouth feels nice. And something you don't see much at other shops is the boiled egg. A boiled egg on Okinawa soba was a bit of a surprise, but it works as an accent in its own way, and I thought it was interesting.
Agariya Special　¥1,250 (a whole boiled egg is unusual 😆)

The seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), which you could call the star this time, give off the fragrant aroma of charcoal, and you can enjoy the aroma with every bite. The cartilage part is jiggly, soft and easy to eat. However, the meat part had a bit of a sinewy texture, and honestly I'd have liked it a bit more melt-in-your-mouth 😅. But people who like this level of searing will surely find it irresistible!
Wasabi and salt as condiments.

On top of that, the wasabi that came as a condiment was a slightly surprising accent. Wasabi on Okinawa soba…? I thought, but it goes surprisingly well! When you put a little dab of wasabi on the soki and eat it, the flavor changes to something refreshing, and it's delicious in its own way. It reminded me of "Ishigufu" and "Su~gi~ji", which has now moved to Onna Village and changed its name to "Sakihama Seimen". There was a nostalgic feeling, along with new discoveries, and it was a happy time 😌.

Overall, the Agariya Special at "Agariya+" is a well-balanced bowl throughout. But if you ask whether it has a standout point that makes it particularly special, maybe not really. Still, it's plenty for enjoying local Okinawa soba, and I felt it has a stability that makes you want to come back again and again. If I get the chance, I'd like to try other menu items too 🍜.

Rating (9/15): Everything is average and plain tasty. I have no complaints, but honestly I'd have liked a little more impact. This shop on the grounds of MaxValu has an unusual paid parking lot with no gate bar (cameras at the entrance/exit). The payment machine is on the shop side, so be careful. (You can get a free ticket from the shop, so parking is effectively free.)

いしぐふー やんばる店.name: Ishigufu Yanbaru branch
いしぐふー やんばる店.desc: The Yanbaru branch of Ishigufu, the "First Okinawa Soba King". On Nago City's east coast along National Route 331, near Kanucha Bay Resort. A clear agu pork broth, firm handmade noodles, and melt-in-your-mouth seared soki served with wasabi and mustard.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map", and I ate here in March 2021 😄
"Ishigufu Yanbaru branch" along National Route 331 in the northern part of Nago City's east coast
Introduced as shop 19 of 41 in the "Nago Soba Map"

"Ishigufu" is the shop of the "First Okinawa Soba King" and has branches in various areas. This time I ordered the "Ishigufu Special Selection Soba (with both bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) and seared soki)".
Menu (this time I ordered the special selection soba)
Ishigufu Special Selection Soba (with bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) and seared soki) ¥1,000
In the clear agu pork broth, the handmade noodles are smooth and firm and tasty 😄　The seared soki is melt-in-your-mouth, and the wasabi and mustard are an accent not found at other shops, nice 😄
Rating (9/15): "Kanucha Bay Resort" is also nearby, so how about it when you're staying there, driving along the east coast of northern Okinawa Island, or sightseeing?
PS: The handmade noodles are very firm, so depending on personal taste, some people may find them on the hard side.

いしぐふー（浦添大公園）.name: Ishigufu (Urasoe Daikoen)
いしぐふー（浦添大公園）.desc: The Urasoe Daikoen branch of Ishigufu, the "First Okinawa Soba King". A bowl with a light agu pork broth, chewy medium-thick noodles, and seared soki accented with wasabi and mustard.
t: "Ishigufu (Ishikufu)" is the shop of the "First Okinawa Soba King" and has branches in various areas. This time I ordered the "Seared Soki Soba" at the "Urasoe Daikoen branch" (March 2019).
Ishigufu (Urasoe Daikoen branch)
Seared Soki Soba　¥700

It seems that even under the same shop name, "Ishigufu" tastes a little different at each branch. Here it's a light agu pork broth with chewy, firm medium-thick noodles 😄 The seared soki is tender too, and the wasabi and mustard are an accent unique to Ishigufu, nice 😄
Rating (9/15): Plain tasty.
PS: Ishigufu's noodles are on the firm side, so some people may find them hard.

いちの屋.name: Ichinoya
いちの屋.desc: A shop in Isagawa, Nago City, along National Route 58. A broth with a strong bonito flavor, regular straight noodles and tender seared soki. There's also the big-volume specialty "Dekadeka Soba". Changing up the flavor with kōrēgūsu is recommended too.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map", and I ate here in October 2020 😄
Ichinoya (along National Route 58)
"Ichinoya" introduced as shop 36 of 41 in the "Nago Soba Map"

I ordered the "Seared Soki Soba". The bonito broth flavor is strong, and with the regular straight noodles, the seared soki was tender and tasty too 😋　Until then, I'd avoided kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori; an Okinawan seasoning of island chili peppers steeped in awamori) without ever trying it, but from around the time of this Ichinoya, I started to realize that adding it changes up the flavor of the broth so it's delicious twice over, and after that I began adding kōrēgūsu partway through 😄
Seared Soki Soba

Rating (9/15): I think it's plain tasty. In the soba map, a soba called "Dekadeka Soba" was described deliciously as "big volume with the aroma of pork bone and bonito stock", so if I get another chance I'd like to try it 😄　Also, I realized I'd been avoiding kōrēgūsu without trying it, and it changes up the flavor of the broth, so I recommend it, please give it a try.

いーばる家.name: Iibaru-ya
いーばる家.desc: A spacious shop marked by its roadside sign. A light broth with restrained pork bone and thin, slightly curly noodles. A community-rooted shop bustling with local customers.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions by me.
I ate here in June 2024 😄
This is Iibaru-ya's sign along the road.
Iibaru-ya
Inside the shop (it's quite spacious)
Inside the shop (near the entrance, someone's autograph is on display 😄)
I decided to order the "Soki Soba" from the meal ticket machine installed at the entrance.
Soki Soba (large)　¥900
Now, first, the broth. Taking a sip, you can tell the pork bone stock is working a little. However, it's restrained, and the impression is light.
Okinawa soba broth tends to show strong individuality from shop to shop, but "Iibaru-ya"'s broth falls into what you'd call the orthodox category.
There were no particularly standout features; it's an average finish as Okinawa soba broth, and I didn't find anything especially noteworthy. It feels plain tasty.
Soki Soba (large)　¥900
Next, the noodles. "Iibaru-ya"'s noodles are a thin, slightly curly straight type. They're boiled on the soft side.
The noodles are slightly on the thin side, but they cling to the broth well enough. However, if I state my personal preference, I felt they could have had a bit more firmness.
Finally, I'll touch on the toppings, especially the pork spare ribs (soki). Soki is one of the representative toppings of Okinawa soba, and the seasoning is the light type.
Also, it's a shame that the meat was a bit coarse and on the dry side.
I was also left dissatisfied with the volume of the soki. While the bones are quite large, the amount of meat is on the small side.
The other toppings (green onions, fish cake (kamaboko), etc.) were ordinary, with nothing especially noteworthy.

In summary, my overall impression of "Iibaru-ya"'s soki soba was "ordinary". It's not particularly bad, but it doesn't have features that leave a strong impression either. Certainly, when I visited it was bustling with local customers. There are many regulars too, and there's no doubt it's a popular shop rooted in the community. However, I didn't feel enough appeal to want to go out of my way to visit again.
Rating (9/15): It feels ordinary 😊　How about it for those who want to casually enjoy Okinawa soba when visiting Itoman City?

うかじそば.name: Ukaji Soba
うかじそば.desc: A shop convenient for sightseeing near Shuri Castle and Ryutan Pond. A light blended broth of pork, chicken and bonito, flat thin noodles, and melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). A gentle bowl for those who like it light.
t: I ate here in February 2023 😄
Ukaji Soba (near Ryutan Pond)
Since it's close to tourist spots like Shuri Castle, I thought it might be crowded with tourists, but I was able to park in the lot in front of the shop, and it was empty.
Menu
Soft-bone Soki Soba (medium)　¥800

I ordered the Soft-bone Soki Soba (medium). The broth is the light type, a blended stock of pork, chicken and bonito. The noodles are flat and thin. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are melt-in-your-mouth and delicious, but the broth was too light, and it felt weak in flavor.
Rating (8.5/15): According to the explanation on the menu, they seem to be particular about the broth, but I'm sorry, to me the flavor was too weak, and I felt it was too light.

名嘉地そば.name: Nakachi Soba
名嘉地そば.desc: Along the National Route 331 Oroku Bypass. A cloudy pork bone-based soup with medium-thin wavy noodles. A rare shop where the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are prepared suchika-style (salt-cured) rather than with soy sauce.
t: I went to eat here in April 2023 😁
Nakachi Soba (along the National Route 331 Oroku Bypass)
I ordered the "Nakachi Soba," which has the same name as the shop 😊
Menu
Nakachi Soba (regular) ¥880
The cloudy soup has a strong pork bone base 😊　The noodles are medium-thin and wavy.

Unlike at other shops, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) wasn't soy sauce-based but suchika (salt-cured pork belly), which was a first for me. In Okinawa, suchika sometimes appears as an offering at the Buddhist altar lol　It had been a while since I'd eaten it 😁　The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) also weren't given the usual soy sauce-based seasoning, but a seasoning that seemed to match the suchika.
It may also be unusual that there's no kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) seasoning on the tables.

Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty 😊　It's close to Naha Airport, so how about it while sightseeing? I'd also like to try their unusual Okinawa soba varieties like nakami soba, chicken soba, and mugwort soba 😊

名護曲.name: Nagumagai
名護曲.desc: A Ryukyuan cuisine and seafood restaurant along National Route 58. Its signature is the pitch-black squid ink soba: bonito broth-based, accented by squid and the bitterness of fuchiba (mugwort). The look is shocking, but the flavor is gentle.
t: I went to this shop in August 2020 after seeing the "Nago City Soba Map."
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Nagumagai" was featured as shop 17 of 41.

Looking back at my Twitter from that time (I'm writing this blog now in March 2023), it seems many shops were temporarily closed because of COVID, and it felt like that day I finally found a shop that was open.
"Nagumagai" along National Route 58
COVID has really hurt restaurants in Okinawa. I hope they hang in there.

Nago soba tour, part 6〜　Squid ink soba at "Nagumagai"〜 lol　A soup of squid ink and bonito broth, with plenty of seafood toppings—squid—and slightly bitter fuchiba (mugwort). The noodles were flat and delicious. I checked shops here and there, but many were temporarily closed due to COVID; the economy is tough. (— Anji, from a post on August 14, 2020)

This time I ordered the "Squid Ink Soba," which was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map." I'd never even had squid ink pasta or anything like that, so I was nervous about trying squid ink for the first time in my life 😁
Squid ink soba　¥990

With the pitch-black soup, it's hard to imagine how it tastes from the look of it, but it's bonito broth-based and solidly tasty ☺　As I tweeted, there are plenty of toppings—seafood in the form of squid—and the bitterness of the fuchiba (mugwort) is a nice accent; delicious 😁
The noodles are flat, which you occasionally see at soba shops in Nago.

Rating (9/15): The look is shocking lol, but when you eat it, it's surprisingly gentle, and I realized I'd been dismissing squid ink without ever trying it ☺　For people who are tired of regular Okinawa soba, I think it's a nice change of pace.

PS: It's fine while you're eating it, but in the following days, I think what comes out when you go to the bathroom (number two) will be pitch black. It's startling lol　So please keep that in mind lol

味ごのみ.name: Aji Gonomi
味ごのみ.area: Goya, Okinawa City (near the Okinawa Zoo & Museum)
味ごのみ.desc: A well-known Okinawa soba spot near the Okinawa Kodomo no Kuni (zoo). Pork bone-based soup with tender soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). A convenient stop to combine with a trip to the zoo.
t: I ate here in November 2022.
A famous Okinawa soba spot, "Aji Gonomi"　It's near the Okinawa Kodomo no Kuni (zoo)
I ordered the "Nankotsu Soba" 😊
Nankotsu soba　¥700? (Sorry, I'm not sure about the price ^^;)
The noodles are a medium-thick straight type, and the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are tender and well-seasoned; solidly tasty 😋　The soup is pork bone-based. The portion is decent too 😁

Rating (9/15): It's solidly tasty, but I'm sorry to say the pork bone-based soup doesn't seem to have the creamy mouthfeel and umami of "796 (Nankuru)," also in Okinawa City. I'd recommend "796 (Nankuru)" more. However, it's close to the Okinawa Kodomo no Kuni (zoo), so if you want to combine the zoo with a meal, this shop is near and convenient 😁

味千拉麺.name: Ajisen Ramen
味千拉麺.desc: A Kumamoto ramen shop at Nakagusuku SA (up line) on the Okinawa Expressway. Although it's a ramen shop, it serves authentic bonito-broth Okinawa soba, and the vegetable soba loaded with stir-fried vegetables is popular too. Good for a bowl during a drive.
t: ― 2nd visit (January 2025) ―

*This article was created with "ChatGPT 5.1 (Thinking)" and partly added to by me. I went to eat here in January 2025 😄　This time I stopped by "Ajisen Ramen" at Nakagusuku SA on the up line of the Okinawa Expressway〜🚗💨
Ajisen Ramen

With its red exterior, big "RAMEN" lettering, and a red-tiled roof standing proudly, it catches your eye right away even within the service area. It's a shop with a strong image as a ramen place originating in Kumamoto, Kyushu, but here at the Nakagusuku SA location they quietly serve authentic Okinawa soba too.
Meal ticket machine near the entrance

First, I started by buying a meal ticket at the ticket machine beside the entrance 🎫　The buttons are packed in rows, with everything from dandan noodles and spicy miso ramen to fried rice sets, so you could easily agonize over it, but of course this is my "Okinawa soba tour" (lol), so I pressed the "Vegetable Soba" button.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

I handed my meal ticket in at the counter, got a number tag, helped myself to water, and went to my seat. Inside, table seats and counter seats are nicely balanced, and the atmosphere is bright and clean ☀️　The walls are decorated with Okinawan photos and posters, making it a slightly relaxing space, just right for a rest stop during sightseeing. It was before noon on a weekday, so there weren't many customers, and time flowed at a leisurely pace.

After a while my number was called, and when I went to pick it up at the counter, I came face to face with a steaming "Vegetable Soba" ✨　The aroma rising from the dark bowl was a truly appetizing mix of savory stir-fried vegetables and bonito broth. On top was a heaping mound of stir-fried vegetables like cabbage, bean sprouts, and carrots, with bits of meat and fish cake (kamaboko) visible here and there. Bright red pickled red ginger sat neatly in the center, and the colors looked great too. Kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) was properly on standby at the side as well—a visual that says everything is ready.
Vegetable soba　¥870

First, a sip of the soup. The base is a solid bonito broth, with the umami and oil of the stir-fried vegetables melted into it, giving it a flavor with a slowly spreading richness. It's surprisingly light on the palate, but it's the type where the umami slowly follows afterward. Since "Ajisen Ramen" is known for its signature Kumamoto pork bone ramen, I'd assumed it would lean more toward ramen, but I was pleasantly surprised. Rather than a "fake Okinawa soba" made by a ramen shop, it felt like a properly authentic Okinawa soba soup paired with stir-fried vegetables, and I thought, "Oh, I might like this direction" 😊
Vegetable soba　¥870
The noodles are a thin straight type, boiled slightly on the soft side, with a squishy mouthfeel.

The stir-fried vegetables are cooked through, with a nice balance between the sweetness of the cabbage and the crunchiness of the bean sprouts. The meat mixed in here and there has just the right presence without being too assertive. Mixing in the pickled red ginger little by little tightens up the richness of the fat and changes the flavor, which is fun too. Partway through I tried adding a few drops of kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori), and with its tingling heat and aroma, the soup transformed into something with yet another face 🌶

The Okinawa soba I recently ate at "Wazaya" in the National Theatre, also run by a ramen shop, had a strong ramen-leaning arrangement, but the "Vegetable Soba" at Nakagusuku SA leans quite orthodox. I found it a bit interesting that even ramen shops can go in such different directions 😄　It's not the type that hits you hard with personality; it's in the position of "a solidly tasty bowl you can eat with peace of mind." I think it's perfect when you want to stop by quickly during a drive and fill your stomach.

Personally, I do feel I'd have liked it even more if the noodles were just a little firmer, but you can clearly taste the bonito aroma in the soup, and with plenty of vegetables it was satisfying too.

Rating (9/15): Just like last time, I thought it was solidly tasty. I thought the Okinawa soba made by a ramen shop holds its own against specialty Okinawa soba shops. How about it when you stop by on a sightseeing sightseeing drive 😄
― 1st visit (June 2023) ―
In June 2023 I found it at the Nakagusuku service area on the airport-bound (up) line of the Okinawa Expressway and tried eating here 😄

While driving on the expressway, with no research as usual, I was planning to have lunch at some Okinawa soba shop, and wondering "Is there an Okinawa soba shop at the service area?" I tried Nakagusuku SA.
Then the outdoor sign I found said "Ajisen Ramen." I thought, "Ah, a ramen shop," but I wondered "Maybe they serve Okinawa soba too?" and headed to the shop entrance anyway 😁
And sure enough, on the sign at the shop entrance, the main items were of course lots of ramen dishes, but there were a few soba items too 😄
I thought "Lucky," but the ramen menu looked delicious too 🤤

Since it's a ramen shop, I hesitated for a moment about getting ramen, but I remembered my resolve when I decided on my Okinawa soba tour (wanting to conquer every Okinawa soba shop on the main island), and chose "Okinawa Soba" (^_^;)
"Ajisen Ramen" in Nakagusuku SA (up line) on the Okinawa Expressway
Okinawa soba　¥700
First, my usual sip of the soup 😄　I thought it was delicious, with an authentic bonito broth base. The noodles are a thin straight type. Soft and solidly tasty.
The toppings are tender braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) that has soaked up the flavor, and fish cake (kamaboko). These too were solidly 😋

Rating (9.5/15): Solidly tasty. I thought the Okinawa soba made by a ramen shop holds its own against specialty Okinawa soba shops. When I googled this ramen shop, it seems to be Kumamoto pork bone ramen, but the Okinawa soba is bonito-based, not pork bone lol　It seems this is the only location in Okinawa, so how about it when you stop by on a drive 😄

和.name: Kazu
和.area: Gusuku, Nago (inside the Nago Public Market)
和.desc: "Shokuji no Mise Kazu" inside the Nago Public Market. Its signature is the "Miso Soba," which is like Okinawa soba in miso soup, with a light miso broth and softish flat noodles. A sweet coffee is served on the house after the meal too.
t: Relying on the "Nago City Soba Map," I found "Shokuji no Mise Kazu" (June 2020).
Kazu is inside the Nago Public Market
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Kazu" was featured as shop 11 of 41.
Here too, I ordered the "Miso Soba," which was introduced with a photo in the soba map
Miso soba　¥700
It looked like Okinawa soba in miso soup, but surprisingly the miso soup flavor was mild, and it was on the light side ^^;　The portion was very generous.
The noodles are softish flat noodles, and miso soup and Okinawa soba go together, but personally I wished the miso flavor were stronger, as the name suggests.
Just when I thought I'd finished, suddenly a sweet coffee with syrup was served on the house after the meal lol　It was my first experience of the Okinawa soba and sweet coffee combo lol
A sweet coffee is served on the house after the meal lol
Rating (9/15): It's solidly tasty, but I wanted more miso flavor in the soup.

PS: I thought the shop had no parking lot and ended up parking at a coin parking lot nearby, but there's a fair amount of free parking inside the Nago Public Market, so take note. First, check for open spaces in the parking lot on the premises.

和喜川屋.name: Wakigawaya
和喜川屋.desc: A diner in Chibana, Okinawa City, run by an owner who loves pottery (*closed November 22, 2024). A gentle soup with bonito broth and fall-apart soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). Shisa made by the owner lined the shop. I'm keeping this article as a record.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT-4o) and partly added to by me lol

I ate here in November 2024 😄🍜　I went to "Wakigawaya" in Chibana, Okinawa City! The exterior has a bit of a "Kitanashuran" (shabby-but-delicious) vibe, but it's exactly these kinds of shops where you can expect good food!
Wakigawaya
Wakigawaya
Wakigawaya
Wakigawaya

When you enter, the dishes made by the owner, a pottery enthusiast, catch your eye. Handwritten menus line the walls, written not only in Japanese but also in English. Perhaps because of the location, there were foreign customers too, and it left an impression how lively it was, with them mixed in among the locals.
Inside the shop
Menu posted inside the shop
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
On top of that, the savory smell of champuru (Okinawan stir-fry) drifted through the shop, whetting my appetite 🤤.
Soki soba　¥750

This time I ordered the "Soki Soba." The bowl brought before me was filled with a gentle soup rich with bonito broth. The soup is light, but you can clearly taste the bonito flavor, and it's a soothing taste with every sip.
Soki soba　¥750

The noodles are medium-thick wavy noodles, finished on the soft side. The noodle lengths seem uneven. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are lightly seasoned and stewed until tender. They're so soft they fall apart when you put them in your mouth, but a little sinewy texture remains in the cartilage part.
At this shop, a notice caught my eye: "We will close as of November 22, 2024."
Closing notice　What a shame.
It's sad that a shop loved by locals for many years is closing, but I'm glad I got to eat here at this timing.
Looking around the shop after the meal, there was a row of ceramic shisa pieces apparently made by the owner, and it was a space with a warmth that felt very Okinawan.
There were shisa that seemed to be the owner's work. They're well made.

Rating (9/15): Overall my impression was "solidly tasty Okinawa soba," but with the shop's atmosphere and local feel added in, it was a heartwarming bowl 😊. It was right before closing, but I'm glad I got to eat here.

ちだもと食堂.name: Chidamoto Shokudo
ちだもと食堂.desc: A down-to-earth diner in Okita, Nago, with the charming look of a renovated detached house. An old-fashioned space where the soki soba with plenty of bonito broth and the manga on the counter put you at ease.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) and partly edited by me lol 🍜✨
I ate here in October 2024 😄 This time I'd like to introduce "Chidamoto Shokudo" in Okita, Nago.
The building looks like a detached house from the outside, and a charming noren (shop curtain) hangs at the entrance. It has the look and feel of an old-fashioned Okinawan diner 😌
Chidamoto Shokudo
Ticket machine inside the shop (the menu is simple)

When you step inside, there's a ticket machine, and while looking at the menu I decided to order the "Soki Soba." The price was ¥850. There aren't that many menu options, but it gives the impression of a simple Okinawa soba specialty shop.
Menu posted on the wall
There's even manga at the counter inside 😆
Soki soba, large ¥850
After ordering, the "Soki Soba" was brought out after a little while. First I'll taste the broth. It's a broth with plenty of bonito broth coming through, with a nice aroma, and it's decently tasty 😋
Soki soba, large ¥850
Next, the noodles. They're medium-thick, straight noodles with a softish texture. Personally I felt they could have had a bit more firmness, but their compatibility with the broth is about average.

The toppings, soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), are well seasoned through, and the knotted kelp is a nice accent too. However, the meat had some slightly stringy parts, and I think it would have been better if it were a bit more tender 🤔

Rating (9.5/15): All in all, it was a decently tasty Okinawa soba. When you visit Nago, I think it could be one of your options as a down-to-earth Okinawa soba shop you can casually drop by 😊 Why not give it a try once?

ちばとぉーんどー.name: Chibatondo
ちばとぉーんどー.desc: The shop's name means "doing our best" in the Okinawan dialect. Its specialty is "Getto Soba," thin, green, wavy noodles kneaded with shell ginger (getto) powder, and paired with a light pork bone and bonito broth, it's a bowl you won't find at other shops.
t: I saw it featured in the local newspaper and went to eat there in September 2022 😄
The shop's name, "Chibatondo," means "doing our best" in the Okinawan dialect, and they really are doing their best 😊
Chibatondo
I ordered the "Getto Soba" that was featured in the newspaper.
Getto soba, large ¥720
If you google "getto," it says: "An evergreen perennial of the genus Alpinia in the ginger family. Its local names in Okinawa include sannin and sanin." 😊

In Okinawa its leaves are often used to wrap "muchi (rice cakes)," but here, getto powder is kneaded into the noodles, making them green, thin, and wavy. These are noodles you won't find at other shops.
According to the explanation in the shop, getto seems to have all sorts of health benefits. It's nice that it seems good for your body 😄 When you eat the noodles, there's a faint aroma of getto.
The broth is a light pork bone and bonito base with a gentle flavor. The toppings are braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), rolled omelet, fish cake (kamaboko), and fried tofu, and it's decently tasty.
Rating (9/15): It's decently tasty. Noodles kneaded with getto aren't found at other shops, so why not try them once? There are only a few parking spaces in front of the shop, so be careful.

ちゃるそば.name: Charu Soba
ちゃるそば.desc: A locally rooted shop in an alley of Sakaemachi Market. Soft-bone pork rib soba for ¥750, with medium-thin straight noodles in a gentle bonito broth. A bowl to enjoy together with the retro atmosphere of the quiet market at midday.
t: This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o), with some additions by me 😁

I went to eat here in October 2024 😄 I visited "Charu Soba" in Sakaemachi Market in Asato, Naha! ✨ It had been a while since I'd been to Sakaemachi Market, and the daytime quiet left an impression. When you picture the nighttime bustle, the daytime atmosphere feels like a completely different world. Enjoying Okinawa soba in such a calm atmosphere is a luxury in itself 🍜.
Charu Soba
Sakaemachi is a bar district that's lively at night, but it's quiet at midday 😄

As you walk down the narrow alleys inside the market, the "Charu Soba" noren (shop curtain) leaps into view. The exterior feels somehow nostalgic, and you get the sense that it's a shop rooted in the local community. The orange sign combined with the retro atmosphere of the market slowly builds your anticipation 🌟.

Inside, a warm space with a wood-based design opens up. The walls are decorated with menus and celebrity autographs, and you're enveloped in a homey, very Okinawan atmosphere. The tables and chairs have a design somehow reminiscent of a nostalgic school classroom, and when I sat down I felt I could take a breather 🍃.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Menu posted on the wall inside the shop (the TV show Age Age Meshi came to film here too 😆)
Menu posted on the wall inside the shop (the TV show Age Age Meshi came to film here too 😆)
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba ¥750

What I ordered this time was the "Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba" (¥750). It's one of the popular dishes among Okinawa soba, isn't it! The soba that was served was simple yet beautifully arranged, and it looked delicious.
When I took a sip of the broth, the gentle flavor of the bonito broth spread through my mouth.
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba ¥750

The noodles are medium-thin, straight, and finished on the soft side. They're not especially firm, but they cling well to the broth, and you can enjoy how they come together in your mouth. You could say this softness is typical of Okinawa soba, but I thought I'd be even happier if there were a little more variety in texture 🤔.

The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are tender, but in places some sinewy texture remains. Still, overall they're well seasoned, and they went well with the broth and noodles. The chopped green onions and kelp served alongside were also just the right accent.

Okinawa soba eaten inside a market really is something special. Eating soba among the locals while enveloped in the quiet midday atmosphere gives an indescribably special feeling. This combination of a retro market scene and Okinawa soba is an experience I can recommend to both tourists and locals 🌿.

Rating (9/15): Overall my impression was "decently tasty," but I think enjoying it together with the market atmosphere makes this bowl even more appealing 🎵. Its charm isn't special luxury, but a homey flavor that somehow puts you at ease 🌺

ちゅるげーそば具志川直営店.name: Churuge Soba Gushikawa Direct Store
ちゅるげーそば具志川直営店.desc: In Midori-machi, Uruma, a sister shop of Ginowan Soba. Its specialty is the "Nuchi Masu Salt Bonito Soba," where the noodles and toppings come in the bowl without broth and you pour the stock from a teapot yourself. You can adjust the saltiness with Nuchi Masu, a specialty salt of Uruma, and it's hearty with three big soft-bone pork ribs.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 to Feb 29, 2024)," and I went here as my 19th of 34 shops 😊
Okinawa soba specialty shop Churuge Soba Gushikawa Direct Store. It looks like an izakaya, so maybe they're open at night too?
Okinawa soba specialty shop Churuge Soba Gushikawa Direct Store. It looks like an izakaya, so maybe they're open at night too?
When you enter, there's a ticket machine near the entrance. This one also seems to be a cash-only ticket machine (;^ω^) I wish every Okinawa soba shop would go cashless soon.
This time I was after the "Nuchi Masu Salt Bonito Soba" featured in the stamp rally booklet 😊
Ticket machine (the "Nuchi Masu Salt Bonito Soba" is lined up 🤗 on the second row)
The shop's explanation of what they're particular about
"Huh?" I've seen this explanation of "rich" and "light" before lol. It's the same as at "Ginowan Soba," where I ate the other day.
Ginowan Soba's explanation 😁 It was similar to Churuge Soba's lol

Churuge Soba's explanation (light) says "chicken, pork, and bonito," so you can tell it's bonito-based. Ginowan Soba the other day says "three-stage preparation" yet only lists "chicken and pork," so the word "bonito" must have been left out (;^ω^) Because the taste definitely had a bonito base coming through lol
Churuge Soba's explanation of the noodles is also more detailed and thorough lol

However, for the "Nuchi Masu Salt Bonito Soba" I ordered this time, I wasn't asked which type of noodles or broth I wanted. Since the dish name includes "bonito," I assume the broth is the light stock.
Menu photos displayed in the shop 1
Menu photos displayed in the shop 2
While waiting for the "Nuchi Masu Salt Bonito Soba," I looked at the menu photos in the shop and saw a dish called "Gorogoro Soba," which I ate at Ginowan Soba the other day.

Between the explanations of the broth and noodle types, and, if you look closely, the back print on the staff's matching T-shirts, which reads "Okinawa soba specialty shops Ginowan Soba, Churuge Soba."

When I asked the staff after eating, it turned out it really is something like a sister shop of Ginowan Soba 😊 The dishes are almost the same as at Ginowan Soba too; the difference seems to be that Churuge Soba has a tofu shop in Uruma, so the "Yushi-dofu Soba" is what sets it apart from Ginowan Soba.
Nuchi Masu salt bonito soba ¥990
The "Nuchi Masu Salt Bonito Soba" arrived 😁 Surprisingly, the bowl had no broth in it. Apparently the stock is in a teapot.
Rather than the kettle at Yae Shokudo in Nago, this is the teapot version 😊
The staff asked me, "Is this your first time?" and explained how to eat it.
They said Uruma's specialty "Nuchi Masu" is mild, so it's fine to put it all in. However, they explained that I should first add about half and then adjust to my taste, so I ate it exactly that way.
The stock in the teapot (there was quite a lot of broth, enough that you could pour seconds and drink it lol)
Nuchi Masu salt bonito soba ¥990

As the staff explained, I added half the Nuchi Masu and then took a sip of the broth. As expected, it's a light, bonito-based broth. I tasted a little of the Nuchi Masu on its own, and it was just plain salty (;^ω^) But once it dissolves into the stock, it becomes a gentle, light flavor and is decently tasty. I thought it could be saltier without any problem, so I dropped in the remaining half of the Nuchi Masu.

The broth is a pretty high level. Next I decided to try the noodles hidden under the rolled omelet. These were wavy noodles. It seems the "Nuchi Masu Salt Bonito Soba" always comes with wavy noodles. These are also the same as the wavy noodles I ate at Ginowan Soba the other day.
The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are big, and there are three of them. It's nice that there's plenty of volume; the seasoning is gentle, and they're tender and decently tasty.

Rating (9.5/15): It's decently tasty. I thought the broth was a high level. This also seems to be a shop loved by locals; the parking lot in front of the shop fits a few cars, but it fills up quickly. Why not give this shop a try at least once too?

ちょーでーぐぁ.name: Chodegwa
ちょーでーぐぁ.desc: Its selling point is homemade fresh noodles (thick and thin), and the firm thick fresh noodles are recommended for those who like them on the harder side. The clear bonito broth has a gentle taste reminiscent of Kenpa no Subaya. Self-service mozuku seaweed from Tsuken Island is another feature.
t: ― 2nd Visit (November 2023) ―
I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 to Feb 29, 2024)," and I went here as my 24th of 34 shops 😊

I'd eaten at this shop a little over a year earlier, and since I want to conquer every Okinawa soba shop on the main island of Okinawa, I'd rather avoid second visits as much as possible, but this time I came back again to get the stamp for the stamp rally 😁
Okinawa Suba Chodegwa *First time in a little over a year 😁
This time I ordered the "Chodegwa Suba (Light)" featured in the stamp rally booklet. The ticket machine here is cash-only too, so I hope they go cashless soon 😄
Noodle explanation board next to the ticket machine

After buying the "Chodegwa Suba (Light)" at the ticket machine, there was a noodle explanation board next to it. Last time I had the "thick fresh noodles," so I wanted to choose a different type of noodle, but when I handed my ticket to the staff, they didn't ask me anything and the order went straight in (^0^;)
Apparently the "Chodegwa Suba (Light)" comes with a set type of noodle.
While I was waiting, the staff suggested I help myself to some "mozuku" seaweed.
This shop offered complimentary mozuku from Tsuken Island in Uruma 😁
Complimentary mozuku isn't something other shops offer, so it's a nice treat 😄
Chodegwa Suba (light, thick fresh noodles, self-service mozuku) ¥900
While I was eating several helpings of mozuku, the "Chodegwa Suba" arrived 😄 It was written on the ticket too, but the noodles were indeed the "thick fresh noodles" (^0^;)
First, a sip of the broth. The clear broth reminds me of "Kenpa no Subaya" in Naha 😁
The broth is finished with a gentle flavor with plenty of bonito broth coming through. Decently tasty.
Chodegwa Suba (light, thick fresh noodles, self-service mozuku) ¥900
Next, the noodles. As I wrote in my first article, the thick fresh noodles have some chewiness but are quite firm and on the hard side. I feel these noodles may come down to personal preference.

The toppings, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), are seasoned on the light side. They're tender, but have a bit of sinewy texture.

Rating (9.5/15): It's decently tasty, but the noodles are a bit hard, so opinions may be divided. The broth has a gentle flavor with plenty of bonito broth and is delicious, but the toppings are on the light side and have a bit of sinewy texture.
― 1st Visit (July 2022) ―
I went to eat here in July 2022 😊 From the sign, it seemed their selling point is homemade fresh noodles.
Chodegwa
Menu (there's a lot. The photo is cut off, but the cold Okinawa soba is unusual)
Soft-bone pork rib suba (thick fresh noodles) ¥700
I ordered the "Soft-Bone Pork Rib Suba." For the fresh noodles you can choose between thick and thin, and I chose the "thick noodles," which were described as having a "chewy texture."
I was told they're less firm than the thin noodles, but even the thick noodles are pretty firm 😁
They go with the clear bonito broth, but I think some people might find the noodles a bit hard. The complimentary mozuku from Tsuken Island is a distinctive touch 😊

Rating (9/15): It's decently tasty, but even the thick fresh noodles described as having a "chewy texture" were pretty firm with a hard bite, so I imagine the thin fresh noodles, described as being firm, are even harder. If you like your noodles on the firm side, why not give it a try?

つきしろそば.name: Tsukishiro Soba
つきしろそば.desc: A shop of real ability, with a salty broth of vegetable stock and pork bone at recommended-shop level. Its specialty is the black laver seaweed soba piled high with black bara-nori, and changing up the flavor with shikuwasa pepper is delicious too. The Kimutaku figurine at the counter is a hidden highlight.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 to Feb 29, 2024)," and I went here as my 18th of 34 shops 😊
"Tsukishiro Soba" The parking lot is a few dozen meters away on the same side, with a few spaces (about 8?).

Menu set up at the entrance (this time I came for the "Black Laver Seaweed Soba" featured in the stamp rally, but I also thought I'd like to try the "Nirai Kanai (= Okinawan word for paradise) Soba" 🤗.
Menu set up at the entrance (I'm curious about the "Special Soba of the Month" item; are they developing a new Okinawa soba every month? 😬)
Menu set up at the entrance (there seem to be side dishes besides Okinawa soba too)
A Kimutaku figurine (;^ω^)
When I went inside, it was quite busy with local customers. At the ticket machine near the entrance inside, I bought the "Black Laver Seaweed Soba" featured in the stamp rally.

I sat at the counter, and right in front of me was the Kimutaku ornament from the photo above 😁 I knew Kimutaku is a longboarder, but he's holding it super close to the nose (the tip), huh. That would drag the board (surfboard), so this style only works at beach-break spots on the mainland lol. I surf too (shortboard), but in Okinawa the spots are reefs (dead coral), so if you carried it that way your board would get wrecked (;^ω^)
The "Black Laver Seaweed Soba" featured in the stamp rally booklet. I'm looking forward to the broth, described as "made with vegetable stock and pork bone."
Tsukishiro Soba's condiments (shikuwasa pepper) look delicious 😋
Explanation of the shikuwasa pepper. I decided to change up the flavor with this condiment partway through (lol)
Black laver seaweed soba ¥900

I was observing all sorts of things around me between ordering and the food coming out, and after a while the "Black Laver Seaweed Soba" arrived 🤗 It's piled insanely high with black laver seaweed and looks delicious 😁
First, as always, a sip of the broth alone. I wanted to taste just the broth, and since there was so much black laver, I was careful not to mix it in (;^ω^)
As described in the stamp rally booklet, the broth with its "vegetable stock and pork bone" base is really tasty 😋 I thought it was a high level. It has a solid saltiness too and is delicious.

Next I mixed the broth with the laver and took a sip 🤗 On top of the delicious broth, you can taste the flavor of the seaweed too, making it even tastier 😋 As expected, I thought the broth was a high-level taste even compared to other shops.
Black laver seaweed soba ¥900
Next, the noodles. They're thin, straight noodles. Slurping them, they're soft, ordinary noodles lol. These are decently tasty.

The black laver topping is generous, which is good. The egg is a thick rolled omelet and pretty tasty. However, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) was on the small side and a bit sinewy. Since I thought the broth was quite high level, I wished the noodles and braised pork belly had been better.
Stamp rally progress (this was my 18th shop. I've finally passed the halfway point (;^ω^))

Rating (10.5/15): I thought the salty broth made with vegetable stock and pork bone was delicious, at recommended-shop level. Changing up the flavor with the shikuwasa pepper was a nice accent and delicious too. However, I thought the noodles were just average, and while the laver and thick rolled omelet toppings were delicious, the braised pork belly still had a bit of sinewy texture, so I felt it was one step short. Still, I think the broth is a high level, so why not give it a try at least once? 😁

石川さん家.name: Ishikawa-san Chi
石川さん家.desc: An open-air diner loved by students, near Meio University and a nursing school. Tacos and taco rice are the main draw, but there's also "nankotsu soba," topped with hefty soft-bone pork ribs in a rich, sweetish seasoning. A community-rooted shop where the proprietress runs everything solo.
t: This time I'm introducing "Shokuji-dokoro Ishikawa-san Chi" in Biimata, Nago🏠 I ate here in March 2025😄
Ishikawa-san Chi
It's right in front of the nursing school in Nago, and Meio University is nearby too, so the shop is in an area bustling with students and young people.

As for the exterior, a signboard with an eye-catching yellow band is mounted on the ground floor of a mostly white building, with the words "Shokuji-dokoro - Tacos, Taco Rice, Soba - Ishikawa-san Chi" written big and bold inside an orange round logo.
Menu posted outside the shop

It feels less like an Okinawa soba shop and more like a diner where tacos and taco rice are the main thing, and sure enough, looking at the menu, there's a rich variety of dishes besides Okinawa soba, like taco rice, taco rice sets, cheese curry rice, salted beef tongue set meals, and pig's feet (tebichi) set meals😄
Near the entrance of the shop

Rather than an interior, it's more like tables and chairs lined up in a semi-outdoor open space with a roof over the parking area; a so-called open-air diner style. Menus with photos are posted all along the wall, and it's fun just to look at them. There's an unpretentious, very Okinawan local feel, and it has the atmosphere of a truly community-rooted diner🌺

When I visited at lunchtime, there were lots of young students, probably from the nearby schools. The proprietress running the place solo looked extremely busy handling the customers who kept coming one after another. It took a while from ordering until the food came out, so I waited😅
What I ordered this time was the "nankotsu soba (large)" for ¥900🍜
Nankotsu soba, large ¥900

First, a sip of the broth. It's a combined pork bone and bonito broth, with the pork bone flavor coming clearly to the front. It doesn't have any especially standout character, but it's just plain tasty😋
Nankotsu soba, large ¥900

Next, the noodles. They're medium-thick and straight, with an overall softish texture. Personally I'd be happier with a bit more firmness and springiness, but they blended well with the broth and were easy to eat.

And the highlight this time, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki)!🥩 Big chunky pieces were piled in generously, and visually the volume is quite something. The sweetish, rich flavor had soaked in thoroughly, and in that respect they were satisfying. However, some sinewy texture remained, and rather than being finished meltingly tender, they were finished with a chew. My impression was I'd appreciate it if they were simmered a bit longer🤔

Rating (9/15): It was a bowl that felt like "just plain tasty~." Given its location near the nursing school and Meio University, I could really see that it's loved as an everyday eatery for students. I was also curious about the other dishes like tacos and taco rice, so it might be fun to come back for those. Please consider it as one option when you're looking for an Okinawa soba shop in the Nago area😊

具志川そば 愛ちゃん.name: Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan
具志川そば 愛ちゃん.desc: An Okinawa soba specialty shop in Ota, Uruma, marked by a big red-and-yellow sign. A two-in-one shop that's a soba shop by day and a place for drinks and karaoke by night; its signature is Gushikawa soba in a light broth with plenty of bonito. Autographed cards line the walls, and it's loved by locals for everyday meals.
t: I ate here in March 2025😄 This time I went to "Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan" in Ota, Uruma😊✨
Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan
Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan
Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan

A conspicuous red-and-yellow sign sits boldly on top of a big building, so you can spot the shop right away even from a distance. It's along the road, and you can see a gas station and a convenience store across the street, so it was an easy place to find even while driving🚗 The parking is under and beside the shop, so it's quite easy to pull into. When you're making the rounds of Okinawa soba shops, places that still have this old-fashioned diner feel always catch your interest.

Near the shop entrance is a big yellow banner reading "Okinawa Soba Specialty Shop," along with a hand-drawn-style illustration of soba, giving it plenty of local feel🌺 The sign reads "Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan" in big letters, and the name alone feels friendly somehow.
Meal ticket machine

When you enter the shop, it's a style where you first buy a ticket at the meal ticket machine. Gushikawa soba, braised pork belly soba, soft-bone soba, pork offal (nakami) soba, yushi-dofu soba, soki soba, and more are lined up, and the menu was bigger than I expected🍜 This time I ordered the "Gushikawa soba, large" from among them.

Inside there are counter seats, table seats, and what look like tatami seats in the back, so it's an easy atmosphere to walk into whether you're alone or with family😊 The wooden counter is fairly wide, and it was nice to be able to eat leisurely.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Autographs of celebrities posted on the shop wall

Lots of autographed cards decorate the walls, and there was an air of "lots of different people have visited here." There are also Okinawan fabrics, awamori bottles, and drum and ship's-wheel decorations; it's an interior that isn't too flashy but properly has an Okinawan feel🌴 Rather than something elaborately built for tourists, my impression was of a relaxed soba shop where locals come to eat on a regular basis.

The "Gushikawa soba, large" that was brought out after a while looked like classic Okinawa soba🍜 A clear broth topped with braised pork belly, soft-bone-type meat, fish cake, and green onion; not flashy, but a reassuring bowl😋
Gushikawa soba, large ¥950
When I first took a sip of the broth, the bonito broth really comes through.
Gushikawa soba, large ¥950

The noodles are about medium-thin, loosely wavy noodles, and the texture was on the soft side🍜 They have the rustic simplicity of Okinawa soba, but rather than the type where you really enjoy the firmness, they're the type that slurps down easily. I felt they were a little soft here😅

The meat topping had moderate seasoning, with a balance where the sweet-savory flavor isn't too strong🥩 The soft-bone-type meat had a bit of sinewy texture, and rather than meltingly tender, it was the type that keeps a meaty texture.

Rating (9/15): Overall, the Gushikawa soba (large) at "Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan" left the impression of plainly tasty Okinawa soba that's easy for locals to have as an everyday meal, rather than a highly distinctive, memorable bowl🍜✨ With its combination of a light broth with plenty of bonito, softish medium-thin wavy noodles, and moderately seasoned meat, it has few quirks, in a good way. Personally, I have no major complaints about any of the noodles, broth, or toppings, but I think it would have been more memorable with one more step of strength that makes you go "oh!"😊

本部そば.name: Motobu Soba
本部そば.desc: On National Route 449, marked by a yellow exterior and black 3D lettering. The famous "three-kind platter" is a meat trio of bone-in pork ribs, braised pork belly, and soft-bone pork ribs. There are also edgy dishes like Motobu-raised goat soup and goat soba. Covered terrace seating available.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5), with some additions of my own lol I went to eat here in December 2024😄
It was a day when rain clouds made the color of the sea look just a little heavy, on the way from Nago toward Motobu. I stopped by "Motobu Soba," a shop whose yellow exterior jumps right out at you.
Motobu Soba
As you can see in the photo, the exterior displaying "Motobu Soba" in black 3D lettering really stands out, and the little shisa by the entrance seems to greet you with a "welcome!", which is cute🦁✨.
Menu posted on the building's exterior wall
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Menu posted in the shop

Inside the shop there are seashells, woodwork objects, and even houseplants; it has a relaxed atmosphere, as if a tourist-spot vibe and local everyday life were mixed exactly half and half. The wooden-placard menus lined up high on the wall are very Okinawan too, and just looking at them gets me excited.
Menu posted in the shop
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

That day I had the "Motobu soba three-kind platter," listed first on the menu and seemingly their selling point, in regular size. As shown in the menu photo, it's ¥900 including tax, a really good value. Outside there's also a covered terrace, and raindrops were wetting the wooden floor, but I couldn't help imagining how pleasant a space it would be on a sunny day🌺.
There's outdoor seating, but unfortunately it was raining (^0^;)
Motobu soba three-kind platter (regular) ¥900

Now, the bowl arrives. Beyond the rising steam, a clear pork-bone-based broth glistens. As in the photo, green onion and fish cake are modestly placed on top, and the star meat trio is bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki)🍖. First, a sip of the broth. The aroma leads with the fullness of pork bone, but the flavor is surprisingly restrained; neither the salt nor the fat is pushy, and I think "a classic, ordinary pork bone broth" describes it perfectly.
Motobu soba three-kind platter (regular) ¥900

The noodles are medium-thin and straight. As in the noodle lift shot, they have a hint of squared edges, but they're cooked on the soft side. Rather than a springy bounce when you bite, they're the type that hugs the broth and slips down smoothly. Personally I'd like them with just half a step more firmness.
The seasoning is light overall. On the other hand, the bone-in pork ribs and braised pork belly retain a noticeable sinewiness, the kind where you enjoy the chewiness.

As shown in the photos, the menu is wide-ranging too; besides soba, it's interesting that there's taco rice, seafood rice bowls, a "greedy set," and even "tsukemen (hot/cold)." They've also got supporting dishes like mozuku seaweed in vinegar, sea grapes, and jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) well covered, which gives the reassurance of being able to tell tourists, "you can sample all the flavors of Okinawa here." The "Motobu-raised goat soup (with offal)" and "goat soba" pushed on the posters are surely things fans would make a special trip for. This sense of balance, offering edgy dishes like these while keeping the everyday soba basic, may be the reason for this shop's popularity👍.

When I finished eating and glanced outside, the rain was still falling finely, but the yellow exterior and green awning looked lovely in the wet, and somehow I felt a little lucky, thinking a rainy day in Okinawa isn't so bad after all.

Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty. All in all, the "Motobu soba three-kind platter" was "right-down-the-middle Okinawa soba" that tourists and locals alike can reach for with confidence: a clear pork-bone-based broth, softish medium-thin straight noodles, and three kinds of lightly seasoned meat. The meltingness of the soft-bone pork ribs earns high marks, while the two sinewy meats may divide opinion. Next time I'd like to have it with jushi on the side and plenty of kōrēgūsu🍜.

我那覇そば.name: Ganaha Soba
