t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT-4o), with some additions of my own lol
I went to eat here in November 2024😄

Today I stopped by "Haneji no Eki" in Makiya, Nago, and had Okinawa soba at "Ganaha Soba" inside it~. The sign says in big letters "Original Soki Soba Shop," which shows quite a bit of confidence✨ But "Marutaka Soba" in Nago also called itself the "original," and "Gabusoka Shokudo" writes "the true-lineage soki soba"... Nago is right in the middle of a "soki soba originator war"😂 (in a good way!)
Ganaha Soba inside Haneji no Eki
Ganaha Soba
Ganaha Soba
This is "Marutaka Soba," which also claims to be the original soki soba😄
This is the "true-lineage soki soba" (Gabusoka Shokudo main shop)
Well then, let me tell you about the all-important soba experience.
Inside, an old-fashioned diner feel coexists with the relaxed feel of a tourist facility, and it's quite comfortable ◎.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Menu posted on the shop wall
Menu set up inside and outside the shop
Menu set up inside and outside the shop
Ticket machine set up in the shop

You order by ticket machine. There were so many menu items that I hesitated a bit, but this time I chose the signature dish, the "original soki soba (¥900)"! When they call it the "original," you just can't not order it~😆

After sitting down and waiting a while, a bowl appeared with just the right amount of steam. Ooh, there are three chunky soki rolling around on top! That's impactful. Kelp and green onion add color too, and it looks really appetizing. Itadakimasu🙏
Original soki soba ¥900

First, a sip of the broth. Yep, it's a combined pork and bonito broth. But rather than one of them coming to the front, it's a balanced broth where neither stands out. No strong personality, but it was an ordinary kind of taste that would probably appeal to everyone😊
Original soki soba ¥900

The noodles are thick, flat, and straight. On the soft side. The look of it with kelp as a topping reminds me of "Miyazato Soba"😄 The kelp topping is very Nago-like too, and nice! I think people who like the Miyazato Soba style will love it👍

And the soki. Three large cuts, with a perfect presence✨ They don't quite fall apart when you put them in your mouth... some sinewy texture remains, so they're satisfying to chew. The seasoning is on the light side. But honestly, I can't deny the impression that it's a little understated in terms of feeling special~😅
Overall, it's a gentle Okinawa soba of the kind locals would want to eat every day. Rather than being aimed at tourists, it feels close to everyday life, and I had a good impression.
Rating (9/15): All in all, it was plainly tasty Okinawa soba. When you visit Haneji no Eki, why not give it a try?😊

t: ― 2nd visit (November 2024) ―
This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet), with some additions of my own lol🍜✨ I ate here in November 2024😄
I'm introducing "Sakura Shokudo" in the municipal market in Gusuku, Nago😊 It's been quite a long time since I last ate here😆

Soba menu

Looking at the menu, the words "stamina bean sprout soba," the house specialty, jumped out at me. This is the dish I'd been thinking "next time" about ever since I ate here last time, so I had no choice but to order it🔥
After a while the "stamina bean sprout soba" appeared! What first catches the eye is the amount of bean sprouts and chopped meat heaped on top of the noodles😳 That's hugely filling!
Stamina bean sprout soba, large ¥980
First, as usual, a gulp of the broth. Is it a combined bonito and pork broth? Or maybe it's agu broth. It's a delicious broth with plenty of umami😋
Stamina bean sprout soba, large ¥980
Next, the noodles. They're medium-thin and straight with a softish texture, but they suit this dish! Just plain tasty.

And what's distinctive is the toppings. The heap of bean sprouts and chopped meat is seasoned with garlic and doubanjiang, and the spicy flavor is irresistible! Eating it makes your body heat up and you start sweating💦 This is truly the stamina type! A powerful bowl, just as the name says.
I ordered the large size, but the volume was more than I imagined, and I almost gave up partway through😅 Next time I think a small size will be plenty. Even so, it'll surely be quite satisfying.

うっちや～.name: Utchiya~
うっちや～.desc: A precious shop on the Motobu Peninsula where you can eat morning soba from 7 a.m. A rich bonito broth with chewy, medium-thick, flat fresh noodles. There's also a fun custom of ringing a bell on your way out.
t: *This article was created by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5), with parts added to and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in January 2025 😁😊
This time I visited "Utchiya~" in Nakaoshi, Nakijin Village. This shop actually opens from 7 a.m., so a big feature is that you can eat morning soba.
Utchiya~

Shops in the Motobu Peninsula area where you can enjoy Okinawa soba from the morning are surprisingly rare. The exterior is a cute, very Okinawan building based on white, marked by a wooden noren (shop curtain). I visited just past noon, and there was a good mix of local customers and tourists, with a lively atmosphere in the air.
Meal ticket machine
They do morning soba too 😆
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

The interior is a traditional Okinawan construction using lots of wood, with counter seats and tatami seating too, a well-prepared environment for enjoying Okinawa soba calmly. It's an ordering system using the ticket machine, so it keeps the atmosphere of a local shop while letting you order smoothly, which left a good impression ✨　What I had this time was the "Utchiya~ Soba".
Utchiya~ Soba (large)　¥980

When I'm actually in front of the bowl, the aroma of the broth with its bonito stock spreads pleasantly. You can taste the saltiness properly too; it's by no means bland, but rather has a moderate richness. It's finished as a well-balanced, delicious broth 🎯
Utchiya~ Soba (large)　¥980
Apparently they use carefully made fresh noodles

The noodles are carefully made fresh noodles, with a distinctive shape that's medium-thick and flat. The chewy texture is pleasant, and they cling to the broth outstandingly. There's solid chewiness left too, and rather than smooth, the unique springy texture is what leaves an impression. The texture of these noodles certainly has a personality different from other shops, and it feels nice 👍

Looking at the toppings, there are soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), a soft-boiled egg, green onions, and a small amount of sea lettuce (āsa) (seaweed). The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are well soaked with a soy-sauce-based flavor, and you can taste sweetness too. However, a fair amount of sinewy texture remains, so while they're satisfying to eat, the slightly fibrous parts are a bit noticeable. The soft-boiled egg is a style you don't see much at other shops, and the small amount of sea lettuce (āsa) is also a nice, very Okinawa-soba-like touch.

The fact that many local customers visit speaks to the high quality of this shop. There are a fair number of tourists too, and there's a nice atmosphere with a good balance of locals and tourists. And what's interesting is that there's a custom of ringing the bell in the shop when you leave, to convey that "it was delicious" 😅
It seems you ring the bell when you leave the shop? lol

This is an unusual touch, and I think it's a lovely system for expressing your satisfaction after eating. Above all, being open from 7 a.m. is a big point. For people who want to be active from early morning on their trip, being able to eat morning soba loved by local customers is an advantage not found at other shops. If you build it into your sightseeing route in the Motobu Peninsula area, you'll have an even more fulfilling Okinawa soba tour.

Rating (10/15): I thought it's a shop that lets you taste top-level deliciousness for the Motobu Peninsula area. With the unusual feature of serving morning soba too, I felt it's a shop worth visiting at least once. Those who want to immerse themselves in the charm of Okinawa soba from the morning, please do pay it a visit 🍜

I ate here in June 2024. This seems to be a long-established shop, but I learned it would close on June 20, 2024, so I came for the last chance! 😄　It's sad that an Okinawa soba shop loved by locals is closing.
Mutsumibashi Kadoya (it was packed with customers trying to taste it one last time since it's closing)
Mutsumibashi Kadoya (it was packed with customers trying to taste it one last time since it's closing)
Mutsumibashi Kadoya (it was packed with customers trying to taste it one last time since it's closing)
Maybe because it's closing, there was a very long line. As expected of a long-established shop that's continued to be loved! But turnover was good, and I was able to eat sooner than I expected.
It closes on June 20, 2024, but it's amazing that it lasted for 72 years. A long-established shop. Thank you for all your hard work.
It closes on June 20, 2024, but it's amazing that it lasted for 72 years. A long-established shop. Thank you for all your hard work.

I'm glad I was able to eat at Kadoya before it closed 😄
The menu posted inside the shop
This time, from the menu, I decided to order the “pork loin soba.”
The condiments on the counter (there was also the pepper-flavored pipātsu that I'd seen at the Yaeyama soba shop “Shima Soba Ichibanchi” where I ate before)
Pork loin soba　¥600
First, the soup. It's characterized by a gentle pork-bone-based taste, not too rich, a light flavor. This is the long-standing taste that customers have loved for so long 😄
Pork loin soba　¥600
The noodles are a medium-thick straight type. They have a soft texture and cling well to the soup. They taste just plain delicious.
The main topping, the pork loin, has a light flavor. It has little fat and a refreshing texture.
“Mutsumibashi Kadoya's” Okinawa soba is truly the most classic of the classic. There's no flashiness, but with one bite it feels like “Ah, this is Okinawa soba!”
Long-time love — it makes sense that it's widely loved by both tourists and locals.

Since its closing has been decided, I'm really glad I was able to eat it one last time. There's no doubt that this shop, bringing down the curtain on more than 70 years of history, has adorned an important page in the world of Okinawa soba.
On top of that, I even got a closing commemorative card lol　Maybe it's a bit of a rare item? I found myself thinking, I wonder if it would sell for a high price on Mercari (lol)
I received a closing commemorative card
Rating (9/15): It tasted just plain delicious, but I'm glad I was able to eat at Kadoya before it closed. Thank you very much.

うちなあ家.name: Uchinaa-ya
うちなあ家.desc: A chain with shops all over Okinawa, marked by a red sign. A combined broth with slightly strong pork bone and melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). They also offer limited-quantity meat-heaped menu items and “Tōjin soba,” the roots of Okinawa soba.

I ate here in August 2024 😆

Actually, this day was the opening day of Costco's Nanjo City store, and when I headed there casually without thinking, I got caught in a huge traffic jam starting on the surrounding roads along the way (^0^;)💦 On top of that, it was pouring rain (^0^;)　In the middle of all that, I decided to make the best of it, made a sudden change of plans, and went into this Okinawa soba shop that I spotted on the way (lol). And so, I decided to visit “Uchinaa-ya” in Tamagusuku, Nanjo City.
Uchinaa-ya (shot from inside the car in the pouring rain (^0^;))

When you arrive at the shop, the first thing that jumps out at you is the bright red sign! It says “Okinawa Soba Shop Uchinaa-ya,” and it somehow gets me excited 😆 When I googled it later, it turns out this shop is actually a chain with locations all over Okinawa. I guess it's loved by both locals and tourists?
Inside the shop
When you go inside, there's a calm atmosphere where you can feel the warmth of wood. There are counter seats and table seats, and it's a relaxed space.
Menu

Menu (there are set meal menus too)

Menu (there's also “Tōjin soba,” the roots of Okinawa soba, which I had at “Miyo-ya” in Kadena Town.)
Looking at the menu, there are lots of kinds of Okinawa soba, but this time I tried ordering the “soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba.”
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba, large　¥900
And then, at last, the “soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba” appeared! It looks voluminous from the appearance alone, and this raises my expectations 😋
First, the soup. When I take a sip, phew~, the balance of pork bone and bonito feels good. But the pork bone flavor comes across as a bit strong. It tastes just plain delicious.

I chose thick noodles, and they were quite soft. They slide down smoothly, but I thought they could have a little more firmness.

Rating (9/15): Honestly, “Uchinaa-ya's” Okinawa soba wasn't a particularly surprising taste, but it's just plain delicious. It's near the Costco that opened on August 24, 2024, so how about trying it once for a meal on your way back from Costco 😄

沖縄そば専門 しまぶく家.name: Okinawa Soba Senmon Shimabuku-ya
沖縄そば専門 しまぶく家.desc: A specialty shop in the style of an old-fashioned shokudo with the warmth of wood. An authentic combined broth of bonito and pork bone with plenty of bonito, and smooth thin noodles. The thoughtful side of shima rakkyo (island shallots) is a nice touch too.
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude Haiku 4.5), with parts edited and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in February 2025 😁😊
I discovered a lovely Okinawa soba shop in the Tomori area of Yaese Town. I visited “Okinawa Soba Senmon Shimabuku-ya” 🍜
Okinawa Soba Senmon　Shimabuku-ya

The exterior is a warm, wood-based structure, and the sign says “Okinawa Soba Senmon Shimabuku-ya” in big letters. When you step inside the shop, it has the atmosphere of an old-fashioned shokudo, and a calm space where you can feel the warmth of wood spreads out before you.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
The walls are covered all over with Okinawa soba menus, and with counter seats and table seats, it has an atmosphere that's easy to enter whether you're alone or with family.
The menu posted on the wall

Looking over the menu, the wide selection makes it hard to choose. From the classic soki soba to yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) soba and pig's feet (tebichi) soba, there are all sorts of variations. This time I chose soki soba without hesitation. My expectations rise, wondering what it will taste like 😄

What arrived was a soki soba topped with two impressive pieces of soki. The sight of it in a black ceramic bowl really whets the appetite. On top of the noodles are pork soki and green onions, and a side of shima rakkyo (island shallots) comes in a white dish.
Soki soba, large　¥830
The side of shima rakkyo (island shallots)

Well then, let's start by tasting the soup. When I take a sip, the combined broth of bonito and pork bone spreads pleasantly in my mouth. What's especially striking is that the bonito broth really comes through, and the balance with the deep richness of the pork bone is exquisite. At first glance I thought it might be an ordinary shokudo-style taste, but I could feel an unexpectedly authentic harmony of broth 😋
Soki soba, large　¥830
Next, let's try the noodles. A thin, straight type, with a pleasant smooth texture 🍜
And the topping, the soki. For its size, it's finished in a way that has plenty of chewiness / bite. It has a sinewy texture and is finished with a light flavor 😄
And not to be forgotten is the side of shima rakkyo (island shallots). The color of the yellow shima rakkyo in the white dish brings a refreshing accent to the table.

Rating (9/15): What I felt overall is that “Okinawa Soba Senmon Shimabuku-ya” may look like an ordinary shokudo-style shop at first glance, but it's actually a shop serving quite authentic Okinawa soba. From the harmony of the bonito and pork bone combined broth, to the wonderful texture of the thin noodles, to the quality of the toppings, everything comes together at a high level. The side of shima rakkyo (island shallots) is lovely too, showing a thoughtful attention to detail. If you love Okinawa soba, I think it's a shop worth visiting at least once.

沖縄そば処 みなみ.name: Okinawa Soba-dokoro Minami
沖縄そば処 みなみ.desc: A new shop that opened in November 2022 in a renovated detached house. A combined broth where the pork bone slightly wins, and the meal ticket machine that accepts cashless payment is convenient. Close to Okinawa Arena and the expressway IC, so it's handy on the way back from events too.
t: I ate here in August 2023 😊
“Minami” near the Okinawa Expressway (Okinawa-Minami IC)
The entrance of Okinawa Soba-dokoro “Minami.” It seems they renovated an ordinary detached house into the shop.
Meal ticket machine

First, when you go into the shop, the meal ticket machine in the photo is installed right in front. The inside seems newly renovated, and when I googled it later, it seems it had just opened in November 2022.

The meal ticket machine supports cashless payment, so I could pay quickly. Convenient 😊　There are Okinawa soba shops that support cashless payment, but there are still many old-fashioned “cash only” shops, so I hope they progress soon lol
This time I ordered the “soki soba (large),” located in the upper row on the right side of the meal ticket machine and which seemed to be the recommendation.
Soki soba　large　¥850
To enjoy the soba's aroma, I checked the flavor 😊　From the smell, I thought the soup was “bonito broth?” and took a sip.
However, it wasn't bonito; if anything, I tasted a bit of a pork-bone-based flavor. I think it's a combined broth of pork and bonito, but maybe the pork bone slightly wins?

The aftertaste after drinking the soup had something like an acidity; just very slightly, but I could also feel a sour sensation. It's just plain delicious, but other shops don't have an aftertaste like this.
The noodles are a thin, wavy type. The texture is on the soft side 😊
The soki is tender too and just plain delicious, but the taste feels a little restrained. The meat's texture is sinewy in places too, and after eating I needed a toothpick to clean between my teeth 😊

Rating (9/15): It's just plain delicious, but the soup's aftertaste bothered me somehow. It seemed to be bustling with local customers. It supports cashless payment (this time I paid with QUICPay), and unusually for an Okinawa soba shop, I could get a receipt issued from the meal ticket machine, so I'd like to turn it into money too using the method in my other article (“[Points hacking] How to turn receipts into money (small change) (super steady type)”) 😄　This shop is close to the expressway IC, the venue for the basketball World Cup being held this month (August 2023) (Okinawa Arena), and the ground where a professional baseball team (Hiroshima Carp) holds its winter camp (also used for the high school baseball prefectural qualifiers), so how about stopping by once when you attend a sports event 😄

帆掛（ふーか）きそば.name: Fūkaki Soba
帆掛（ふーか）きそば.desc: A specialty Okinawa soba shop with no chemical seasonings, along the Tengan River in Uken, Uruma City. The signature dish is the umikaji soba with a seafood broth of clams, bonito flakes, kombu, and the fresh fish of the day (no meat used at all), prepared by an owner who loves fishing. You can choose the noodles from special fresh noodles (Shimamugi Kanasan) or Terukina Seimenjo's wavy noodles.
t: I ate here in February 2024 😄
Fūkaki Soba (I thought it was the entrance, but it seemed to be the back door)

This time, from the 2 soba menu items, I ordered the “umikaji (sea breeze) soba.” According to the menu, it's “a broth of concentrated umami from clams, bonito flakes, kombu, and the fresh fish of the day. *No meat used at all.”

You can also choose the noodles from 2 kinds, the shop's special fresh noodles (Shimamugi Kanasan) or Terukina Seimenjo's wavy noodles, and this time I chose the special fresh noodles (Shimamugi Kanasan) 😄
Looks delicious 😁

Umikaji soba, regular　¥1,000
The umikaji soba has arrived. It's full of things from the sea, clams and sea lettuce (āsa), and looks delicious. First, I taste the soup.
The seafood broth, with no meat used at all, tasted lighter than I expected, and I could taste some saltiness. It's basically lightly seasoned.
There are plenty of clams in it, but I can't taste much seafood flavor in the soup.
Umikaji soba, regular　¥1,000

うみちか食堂.name: Umichika Shokudo
うみちか食堂.desc: A local diner in Mashiki, Ginowan City. Reasonably priced, like the Umichika Soba with gentle bonito broth (medium ¥700), with unique menu items such as squid ink soba and bean sprout and garlic chive stir-fry soba. Finishing with zenzai is recommended too.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions by me.
I ate here in October 2024 😄　This time I'm introducing "Umichika Shokudo" in Mashiki, Ginowan City.
Umichika Shokudo
The exterior is a cream-colored building, marked by a blue sign. Entering the shop, it was bustling with local customers and tourists 😄
Umichika Shokudo's parking lot
Menu
Menu
Menu (set meals are plentiful too)
Menu (there are rice bowls too)

Looking at the menu, starting with the basic "Umichika Soba", there's a rich lineup ranging from standard dishes like soft-bone soki soba and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba to unique items you don't see much at other shops, like squid ink soba and bean sprout and garlic chive stir-fry soba. In terms of price range, you can enjoy Okinawa soba reasonably 😆
This time I decided to order the signature "Umichika Soba (medium)" (¥700).
Umichika Suba (medium)　¥700
The "Umichika Soba" was brought out. First, the clear broth. The gently flavored bonito-stock-based broth comes through.
Umichika Suba (medium)　¥700
The noodles used are a thin straight type. Though the texture is on the soft side, they pair outstandingly with the broth 😋

The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) topping is slowly simmered to a melt-in-your-mouth texture. The fat has melted out just right and it's delicious, but a little sinewy texture remaining bothered me. The fish cake (kamaboko) has a moist texture, and the aroma of chopped green onions accents the whole thing.

The side menu is also plentiful, and you can enjoy standard Okinawan meals like jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) and champon too. For dessert there's also "zenzai", unique to Okinawa, which I recommend to finish off 🍨

Rating (9/15): A gently flavored Okinawa soba with a well-balanced broth, plain tasty. The prices are reasonable too, and it's a shop you can drop into casually. When you come to Ginowan City, why not pay it a visit? It was a simple, warm Okinawa soba shop 😊

うむさんの庭.name: Umusan no Niwa
うむさんの庭.desc: An Okinawan charcoal-grill restaurant near Kafuu Resort Fuchaku. The specialty "Charcoal-Seared Thick-Cut Braised Pork Belly Soba" features braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) so tender you can cut it with chopsticks and so fragrant it's No.1 class among all toppings I've had. The lemon-water hospitality is stylish too.
t: I ate here in April 2024 😄
The sign along National Route 58 (turn right at this sign)

"Umusan no Niwa" is near a hotel (Kafuu Resort Fuchaku)

Entering the shop, I went to the seat the staff guided me to (you're assigned a shoe locker and take your shoes off). There seemed to be a few customers, and it didn't feel crowded. It's a quiet atmosphere inside.
Menu (the touch panel system is nice)
Menu (the touch panel system is nice)

It's a stylish, creative menu of Okinawa soba. All of them look delicious, but I figured the item shown at the very top was probably the recommendation, so I decided to order the "Charcoal-Seared Thick-Cut Braised Pork Belly Soba".
Inside the shop (there were other customers, so sorry, I couldn't photograph the left side, but the shop is spacious)

While waiting, I drank the water in my cup and thought, "? This tastes good somehow." I drank it all and went for a refill from the self-service? water pitcher away from my seat. Then the staff brought a pitcher to my seat, and inside it was lemon 😁
I see, that's why it has a refreshing taste; the lemon flavor is nice too. Stylish right down to the water.
Lemon in the pitcher. Refreshing lemon water, delicious
Charcoal-Seared Thick-Cut Braised Pork Belly Soba　¥1,200
The soba came. First, the broth of course. It's a broth where the bonito stock really comes through, delicious.
Charcoal-Seared Thick-Cut Braised Pork Belly Soba　¥1,200
Next I have the noodles. Apparently they're homemade fresh noodles, and these too are chewy and delicious. Next, the thick-cut braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). And charcoal-seared, no less.

It's a big piece of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), but when I lift it with my chopsticks, it breaks apart (°°)　It's very tender 😁　And since it's seared over charcoal, it's fragrant and very tasty 😋
I thought it was the most delicious braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at so far. I recommend it.

Rating (12/15): This shop is in a sightseeing spot in Onna Village. The charcoal-seared thick-cut braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is superb. I thought it was the best of all the Okinawa soba toppings I've eaten so far (as of February 2024). Even the water is lemon water, stylish in a way not found at other shops, so how about trying it once? I recommend it 😄

うるかそば.name: Uruka Soba

うるくそば.name: Uruku Soba
うるくそば.desc: The TOMITON branch, inside the "Okinawa Soba Expo" food court at Toyosaki's TOMITON. Its feature is that you can choose the broth from pork bone or bonito, and the No.1 most popular dish is the sweet-savory soft-bone soki soba. A casual bowl while you're out shopping.
t: This time I went to "Uruku Soba TOMITON branch" inside TOMITON in Toyosaki, Tomigusuku City 😊 I ate here in April 2025 😆
Uruku Soba TOMITON branch
Since it's inside TOMITON, the parking lot is large too, and it's an easy shop to drop into while shopping or out and about.
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall

At the shop front, food samples and menus are lined up in a row, and besides Okinawa soba, the menu is quite extensive with set meals, curry, taco rice and more ✨ Families can each order what they like, so my impression was that it seems easy to use.
Looking at the showcase, the one introduced as "Popularity Ranking No.1" was the soft-bone soki soba. Since I was there anyway, this time I tried ordering the popular dish!
This shop's feature is that you can choose the broth from pork bone flavor or bonito flavor. This time, since I like bonito broth, I chose the bonito flavor without hesitation 😊
Soft-bone Soki Soba (bonito broth)　¥700

The soft-bone soki soba that was brought out is a simple bowl with two large soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) on a clear broth. Starting with the broth, the bonito stock comes through more strongly than I expected. The moment it hits your mouth the bonito aroma spreads, and while it's light, I could fully feel the presence of the stock.
Soft-bone Soki Soba (bonito broth)　¥700

The noodles are medium-thick curly noodles. They're boiled on the soft side, with an old-fashioned Okinawa-soba-like texture. Rather than the type where you enjoy firmness, my impression was of gentle noodles you can slurp down smoothly together with the broth.

And the star, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), are well soaked with a sweet seasoning. They're not the fall-apart type, and some parts had a bit of sinewy texture remaining, but when you chew, you can fully taste the savoriness of the pork. With the sweet-savory seasoning, they'd probably go well with rice too 🍖
Overall, it was a well-balanced bowl and plain tasty 😊
However, my honest impression is, "It's tasty, but I think there are other Okinawa soba shops that would move me more~" 😂

Rating (9/15): Plain tasty. The shop is easy to walk into, and being inside a shopping mall, the ease of using it casually is a big draw. I felt it's just the right shop for when you "want to have a quick Okinawa soba" on your way home from shopping or in the middle of sightseeing ✨

t: I ate here in January 2023 😄
Wachichi (near Okinawa Prefectural Comprehensive Athletic Park)

Menu
Wachichi Soba (medium) ¥800

おおしろそば.name: Oshiro Soba

It competes with just large, medium and small, with a lettuce topping not found at other shops and a bonito broth, and you can choose flat noodles too. The first shop I visited on my Nago Soba Map tour.
t: It's a shop that people around me call "the most delicious", and it's one of my favorite soba shops too ☺　It's the first shop I visited after deciding to go on a soba tour with the "Nago City Soba Map" lol
It was originally in Gusuku, Nago City, but on November 24, 2022 it moved and reopened in Okita, Nago City, so I went for the first time in a while (December 2022).
"Oshiro Soba", moved and reopened. Apparently it has parking for 9 cars
