Rating (12/15): Bonito-based broth is the standard at soba shops in Nago City, but I think Oshiro Soba is delicious, so please give it a try. Before the move it was street parking or a nearby coin parking lot, but now a certain amount of parking (9 cars) is secured, so I think it's easier to drop in than before.

おかあさん.name: Okaasan
おかあさん.desc: A locally popular diner marked by its red sign. A gentle pork-bone-based broth, medium-thick loosely curly noodles, and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) with a sweetish soy sauce flavor. A shop featured on Age-Age Meshi, bustling with regulars.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions by me.
I ate here in September 2024 😄
This time I'm introducing "Okaasan" in Zaha, Itoman City. It seems to be a popular shop loved by locals 🏃‍♂️💨
Okaasan
"Okaasan" is characterized by a simple exterior marked by its red sign. Entering the shop, a warm atmosphere spreads out 😌
Inside the shop
It seems it was featured on a local TV program (Age-Age Meshi)
Menu posted inside the shop
Menu posted inside the shop

Looking at the menu, the standard Okinawa soba dishes are lined up. This time I tried ordering the "Soft-bone Soki Soba". While waiting, seeing it bustling with local customers, I felt firsthand how popular this shop is 👀
Soft-bone Soki Soba　¥900

After a while, the long-awaited "Soft-bone Soki Soba" makes its appearance! 🍜 First, let's taste the broth. The gentle pork-bone-based broth has a flavor that somehow feels nostalgic. It feels plain tasty.
Soft-bone Soki Soba　¥900
Next I have the noodles. The medium-thick loosely curly noodles have a soft-ish texture.

And then the main topping, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). The soy sauce flavor is on the strong side, and a slightly sweet seasoning is characteristic. They're simmered until melt-in-your-mouth, but a little sinewy texture remains.
Looking around the shop, there are many people who seem to be regulars, and the atmosphere is lively. You can really see how it's loved by locals 😊
"Okaasan"'s Okinawa soba doesn't have any particularly unusual features, but its simple, warm flavor is its charm. I feel like I understand why it continues to be loved by locals.
However, if I give my personal impression, the taste struck me as ordinary. It wasn't surprisingly delicious, but there's no doubt it delivers stable deliciousness.
When you visit Itoman City, why not try the Okinawa soba at "Okaasan", loved by locals, at least once? 😉 You're sure to enjoy the simple flavor and warm atmosphere!

Rating (9/15): It feels ordinary 😊　Overall, "Okaasan" delivers stable deliciousness. It's not a surprising taste, but it was a simple, warm Okinawa soba that lets you understand why it continues to be loved by locals. Everyone, please do pay it a visit! 🚶‍♂️🏃‍♀️

大城そば家.name: Oshiro Soba-ya
大城そば家.desc: An Okinawa soba specialty shop in Miyazato, Nago, marked by its salmon-pink building. The signature "Oshiro soba," where you can choose thin or flat noodles, is a very Nago-style bowl: a broth with plenty of pork bone, topped with knotted kelp.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), with some additions of my own lol🍜✨ This time I'm introducing "Oshiro Soba-ya" in Miyazato, Nago.

I ate here in August 2024. This shop is close in location to "Oshiro Soba," which I introduced in "Okinawa soba shops every bit as good as my recommended shops," and the names are similar too (^0^;) I entered excitedly this time as well😊
Oshiro Soba-ya
Oshiro Soba-ya

"Oshiro Soba-ya" has the air of a place loved by locals, just from its exterior. The salmon-pink building catches the eye. At the entrance, there's an "Okinawa Soba Specialty Shop" sign and a row of wooden menu placards, which is exciting🎉

When I entered, perhaps because it was lunchtime, it was bustling with local customers. Lively voices were flying around, and you could feel the atmosphere of a popular shop. There are counter seats and table seats, and I sat at a table. (It was busy with customers, so sorry I couldn't take photos inside🙏)

Looking at the menu, the signature "Oshiro soba" jumps right out at you. Can't skip this one😆 When ordering, I was told you can choose between thin noodles and flat noodles. I tried the flat noodles, which are very Nago-like.
Meal ticket machine (at the top left is "Oshiro soba," which seems to be the recommendation)
After a while, the long-awaited "Oshiro soba" makes its appearance!🎊
Oshiro soba, large ¥900

First, the looks. Chunky toppings peek out of a broth gleaming golden. What's distinctive is the knotted kelp on top. This reminds me of "Miyazato Soba" in Nago, which I went to before. Maybe it's a characteristic of Nago's Okinawa soba😄
Now, as usual, I start by tasting the broth. Hm? An unexpected flavor. At first I thought it was bonito-based, but surprisingly the pork bone comes through. Just plain tasty👍
Oshiro soba, large ¥900
Next, the noodles. The flat noodles I chose are soft. They have a smooth, slippery texture and go fine with the broth. But personally I think I prefer a bit more bite😊

Turning to the toppings, a hefty soki sits enthroned. It's meltingly soft. When you put it in your mouth, it's soft as expected and the umami of the meat spreads gently. The seasoning is on the light side, a balanced finish that doesn't interfere with the taste of the broth.
And the knotted kelp I mentioned earlier. This makes a nice accent too. The umami of the kelp dissolves into the broth, making the overall flavor deeper.
My overall impression after eating... hmm, I'd say just plain tasty🤔 There's no particularly surprising originality, but it's reliably delicious.

Rating (9/15): It was plainly tasty, reliable Okinawa soba. It's not especially surprising like "Oshiro Soba" from "Okinawa soba shops every bit as good as my recommended shops," but I think it's a bowl you can fully enjoy as a local Nago taste. If you have a chance to come to Nago, please stop by "Oshiro Soba-ya." You're sure to spend a heartwarming time while soaking up the local atmosphere🏖️

チキンの丸焼きこっころこ.name: Chikin no Maruyaki Kokkoroko
チキンの丸焼きこっころこ.desc: A one-of-a-kind chicken soba made by a whole-roast-chicken specialty shop. Garlicky roast chicken sits boldly on top, and the soup, infused with the fat and aroma of the roast, has a character no other shop has. Keihan (chicken rice) and takeout whole roast chicken too.
t: This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5 Thinking), with some parts added by me 😁
I ate here in December 2024 😄 Today I visited "Chikin no Maruyaki Kokkoroko" in Awase, Okinawa City.
Chikin no Maruyaki Kokkoroko
Banners outside the shop
The sign and exterior are cute, with wood-grain accents standing out on the white building along the road 🏠 There's a ramp in front of the shop, too, giving it an easy-to-enter feel.
Inside the shop (there's a guitar on display (^0^;))
Inside the shop

When you go inside, the first thing that jumps out at you is the wall of autograph boards above the counter 📸 You can feel how loved it is by locals. When you sit down, the savory smell of roast chicken is already gently tickling your nose, and your appetite switch turns on naturally 😄
Price revision notice
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

Flip through the menu and, as expected, the star is chicken. A whole roast is ¥2,000, the "tori-zara (half)" to enjoy in the shop is ¥1,200, and the quarter (Kokkoroko Special) is ¥1,000 — a solid lineup. For takeout fans there's also the "Chicken L pack (1/2) ¥1,200" and "S pack (1/4) ¥850", so munching on it at home while watching a movie sounds nice too 🚗 I also discovered a new menu item, "keihan (chicken rice) ¥800". It seems to be an arrangement of the Amami Oshima local dish using their roast chicken, so it's decided as homework for next time 🍗✨
That said, today I came to eat Okinawa soba, so I ordered the "chicken soba" in "large".
Chicken soba (large) ¥880

The bowl that arrived has, as in the photo, roast chicken sitting boldly on top of the soup. The skin is nicely browned, and from the first bite the garlic in the seasoning comes through strongly, with an impact that makes you go "Oh!" 🧄🍜 The clear golden soup is less the sharp, "straight-up clear chicken broth" type and more the type where the fat and aroma of the roast have slowly melted in. Rather than competing on the outline of the broth alone, it pushes forward with the savoriness only a chicken specialty shop can offer. A flavor you can only find here — I kept nodding and my spoon wouldn't stop 😋
Chicken soba (large) ¥880

The noodles are medium-thick and gently wavy. Pale and smooth, cooked on the soft side. Rather than pulling you along with chewiness, they're designed to coat themselves in soup as you slurp. Personally I'd like a bit more bite, but they have a "good receiving quality" that catches the punch of the star chicken and garlic, so the overall flow isn't bad. When you lift the noodles, the aroma spreads softly with the steam, and adding a little green onion lightens the aftertaste. Adding pickled red ginger midway tightens everything up at once, and the heaviness of the second half disappears — that's nice too 🥢

And then the chicken topping. When you put your chopsticks in, it comes apart tenderly along the fibers. The skin is savory, and the inside is moist. As the garlic seasoning blends into the soup, its sharp edges soften and layers of umami build up, which is fun. It's nice that you can reset your palate with the namasu-style side dish and go back to the soup in a loop. Since I went with "large", it's more filling than it looks, and my stomach was well satisfied 🐔

I think what makes this bowl interesting is that it's complete not through "purity of broth" but through "the shop's character". The worldview is clear with three points: the roast aroma, the garlic flavor, and the soft noodles, and if you come expecting the classic pork-bone or bonito-forward Okinawa soba, you'll be betrayed in a good way. Opinions may be divided, but if asked "Can you only eat this here?", I'd proudly answer yes. It hits the spot on days when you want to eat heartily or recharge your stamina after work. If you go along mixing in flavor changes with the pickled red ginger and green onion on the table, you can enjoy it without getting bored until the end. For those who like spicy food, next time I'm curious about the chili sauce suggestion for the "keihan" too 🌶️
A price revision notice was posted in the shop, but I felt a determination of "we'll satisfy you with the volume on the plate" to make up for it.

They also offer takeout and vacuum packs, so it seems handy for family gatherings and as a treat to bring to people 📝 Making "our own chicken soba" at home by preparing a hot soup and topping it with a quarter sounds fun too. There are days for tackling the classic tourist spots, and days like this for dropping casually by a distinctive local shop, and I reflected that both are good ✨

Rating (9/15): All in all, the chicken soba at "Chikin no Maruyaki Kokkoroko" was a bowl that "pulls you along with the deliciousness of the meat", lightly leaping beyond the framework of Okinawa soba. The direction of the soup isn't the easy-to-grasp type, but the savoriness of the roast and the punch of garlic keep you eating right to the end. If you're looking for something distinctive, or it's a day you want to eat well, please give it a try 🍜

ナナチ.name: Nanachi
ナナチ.desc: A new shop whose selling points are Daito soba and Daito sushi. The glossy, chewy, thick wavy aged fresh noodles are delicious in a way no other shop offers. Touch-panel ordering and smartphone payment, and the Daito sushi made with fish shipped straight from the Daito Islands looks tempting too.
t: I went to eat here in May 2023. It recently opened along Prefectural Route 7, which I take to and from my surf point (Itoman City, Suicide Cliff point), so I'd been curious about it 😄
Nanachi, along Prefectural Route 7
The moment I parked in the lot, someone from the shop noticed and even came outside to greet me ^^; Kind of embarrassing ^^;
Looking at the banners outside, maybe they're from Higashi? Minamidaito Island — they seem to be featuring "Daito soba" and "Daito sushi".
Menu (I ate on the terrace seats, where you can feel the outdoor air 😄)

Right when you enter, there's a touch-panel machine, and it's prepay. My impression is that many Okinawa soba shops are still cash-only, but since this one opened recently, I could pay by smartphone 😊 Nice. I wish restaurants would go cashless soon.
This time I ordered the "Nanachi Special (¥1,100)" recommended by the staff, with a large portion of noodles (+¥100).
Nanachi Special (large noodles) ¥1,200

The banner said "aged fresh noodles", and in the soup with a strong pork bone broth, the noodles are thick and wavy — glossy, chewy, and satisfying. Noodles unlike other shops', and delicious 😋 The toppings — pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), fish cake (kamaboko), pickled red ginger, and green onion — were chosen on the touch panel.

Rating (10/15): The thick wavy aged fresh noodles were delicious even compared to other shops. The toppings and soup are simply tasty. However, I paid +¥100 for large noodles, but the amount didn't really feel like a large portion, and the price may be a bit high compared to other shops. (Then again, maybe other shops are too cheap ^^;)
The cute ball-shaped(?) Daito sushi apparently uses fish shipped directly from the Daito Islands, and the photo on the menu looked delicious 🤤

パパイヤとスブイ.name: Papaya to Subui
パパイヤとスブイ.desc: Creative Okinawa soba with distinctive shiitake broth and papaya and subui (winter melon) toppings. After Ishikawa in Uruma City and Matsuo in Naha City, it now operates inside Ginowan Yui Marche. The Lemosco condiment is something other shops don't have.
t: ― 3rd visit (May 2025, Ginowan Yui Marche) ―
I ate here in May 2025 😆 This time on my Okinawa soba tour, I went to "Ginowan Yui Marche" in Oyama, Ginowan City.
Ginowan Yui Marche
Papaya to Subui (inside Ginowan Yui Marche)
Papaya to Subui

Inside the marche, lined with local vegetables and souvenirs, is "Papaya to Subui no Okinawa Soba". From outside, the bright yellow-green sign catches your eye, and it has a somewhat quirky atmosphere — you'd never think there was an Okinawa soba shop inside a marche.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

I'd eaten at Papasubu before at the Uruma City location and the location in front of the Prefectural Office, but this was my first visit in quite a long time. There's a ticket machine at the front, and it's lined with Okinawa soba you rarely see elsewhere, starting with Papasubu soba, plus sunui shiitake soba, shikuwasa wasabi soba, ume and ginger soba, squid ink soba, and more. A lineup that's exciting for anyone who wants to enjoy creative Okinawa soba, different from the standard sanmai-niku soba or soki soba.
Meal ticket machine
Meal ticket machine
That day, the blackboard in the shop said "¥200 cashback for customers ordering vegetable soba", so I ordered the limited-time recommendation, "vegetable soba", without hesitation.
The vegetable soba was a good deal today 😆

Looking at the photo, it's piled high with leafy green stems, eggplant, green pepper, bell pepper, kombu, and more, and it looks quite hearty. On top of that there's chopped meat and bonito flakes too, so the bowl is lively 😊
Vegetable soba ¥1,050 (*¥850 with the ¥200 cashback)

When I first drank the soup, the flavor was quite different from the usual Okinawa soba pork bone or bonito broth. Maybe it's shiitake broth — a soup with a distinctive aroma and umami, light but with a strong character. If you're expecting the bonito aroma typical of Okinawa soba, you might be a little surprised. Perhaps the moisture from the vegetables was added too, but overall it was a gentle flavor, and I found it a bit lacking.

The vegetables are also quite different from a typical vegetable soba. The main ones were summer vegetables like leafy green stems, eggplant, green pepper, and bell pepper. The seasoning is very restrained — the type where you enjoy the vegetables' own aroma and texture. I think it's a bowl vegetable lovers will enjoy.
Vegetable soba ¥1,050 (*¥850 with the ¥200 cashback)
The noodles are said to be homemade hand-kneaded noodles — medium-thin and wavy. A bit on the thin side for Okinawa soba noodles.

The chopped meat on top was also something quite different from the usual Okinawa soba braised pork belly or pork spare ribs. Maybe a five-spice-like aroma — a distinctive seasoning that also felt a bit herbal, another flavor you rarely encounter at other shops. Both the soup and the toppings gave the impression of being finished as tropical-style creative cuisine rather than leaning toward the Okinawa soba standard. When I added a harissa-like condiment midway, a curry-like spiciness came out, and it changed into an even more ethnic-leaning bowl 🌶️

Honestly, in terms of my personal taste, the flavor didn't really click for me. Overall it was lightly seasoned, and quite different in direction from the powerful pork bone or bonito I look for in Okinawa soba. However, there really are a lot of vegetables, and by the time you finish you'll be quite full. I think it's an interesting shop for people who want to eat plenty of vegetables, people looking for an unusual variety different from the usual Okinawa soba, and people who like spicy or creative flavors.

Rating (9.5/15): Being inside Ginowan Yui Marche, it's easy to drop by while shopping, which is nice. If you want to feel the breadth of Okinawa soba, I'd really like you to try Papasubu's one-of-a-kind Okinawa soba at least once ✨
― 2nd visit (October 2024, Matsuo, Naha City) ―

I ate here in October 2024 😆 This time I visited "Okinawa Soba Papaya to Subui" in Matsuo, Naha City. I'd been once before when it was in Ishikawa, Uruma City, but this is my first visit since it moved to Naha City.
Okinawa Soba Papaya to Subui

The shop is on the 1st floor of an old building, and when you go inside, a calm space with lots of houseplants spreads out, with an atmosphere just like a café 😊 Elementary school tables and chairs are used, which I felt helped create a cozy feel.
Inside the shop (recycled elementary school tables and chairs 😄)
Inside the shop (recycled elementary school tables and chairs 😄)
A whole "subui (winter melon)", from the shop's name, is placed as interior decor 😆

When I checked the menu on the meal ticket machine near the entrance, there was a range of creative Okinawa soba. Among them, the signature "Papasubu soba" caught my interest. I bought a ticket and waited at a table surrounded by plants. There were several other customers in the shop besides me, and everyone seemed to be spending a leisurely time.
Meal ticket machine near the entrance

While waiting in the shop, I looked out the window and it was raining. But somehow the atmosphere of this rainy day felt pleasant. The green of the houseplants, the old-fashioned furniture, and the natural light coming through the windows blend together in perfect balance 😌
After a while, the "Papasubu soba" was brought out in a yellow bowl.
Papasubu soba ¥900

First, as usual, I start with the soup. One sip, and a deep flavor unlike the Okinawa soba shops so far spreads out. In addition to pork, chicken, and bonito, the broth made from plenty of shiitake is its distinctive feature.

Actually, I felt this soup was delicious enough to work as a ramen soup rather than an Okinawa soba one. The strong shiitake flavor was especially memorable, a deep taste where you can also sense elements of Japanese dashi. This is a unique worldview you can hardly find at other shops 😋
Papasubu soba ¥900

The noodles are homemade hand-kneaded noodles with a gentle wave, and they have a moderate chewiness. They cling well to the soup, and eating them together seems to bring out the soup's umami even more. The thickness is about medium-thin, I'd say. The firmness is just right, and they kept a good texture right to the end.

The toppings, shibui and braised pork belly, are slowly simmered until melt-in-your-mouth tender. However, the braised pork belly still had a slightly sinewy quality, which bothered me a little. There's plenty of green onion on top, and eating it mixed with the soup adds a nice accent.
Papasubu soba ¥900

What was interesting was the condiment on the table. Instead of kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori), the usual Okinawa soba condiment, there was "Lemosco". It's a spicy condiment made with Setouchi lemons, and when I tried adding it to the soup, a nice sourness and heat were added, changing it into a completely new flavor! I was impressed by what a novel idea this is 😆
Lemosco (a condiment other shops don't have)

The way the atmosphere is created is distinctive too — the wooden tables like old school desks and the arrangement of houseplants seem to deliberately create a nostalgic space. A big houseplant is placed by the window, and beyond it you can see the kitchen. Every so often a lovely aroma of broth being made drifted from the kitchen, which whetted my appetite.

Rating (10.5/15): As a creative Okinawa soba, I felt it was a bowl with its own unique worldview. The distinctive soup with a strong shiitake flavor in particular is an appeal other shops don't have. It's wonderful that they've kept the same flavor even after moving to Naha City. Including the atmosphere of the shop, I think it's a valuable place where you can enjoy Okinawa soba at a relaxed pace.
― 1st visit (March 2023, Ishikawa, Uruma City) ―
*The following is an article from when it operated in Ishikawa, Uruma City. It has now moved to Ginowan City.
In March 2023 I went to "Papaya to Subui", located pretty much along Route 329.
Papaya to Subui — a stylish exterior, isn't it

This shop, which opened on April 11, 2022 in a renovated former ramen shop — I learned from TV or somewhere that they use papaya and subui, and shiitake for the soup broth, so I'd been curious about it.

"Papaya" seems to be a tropical fruit native to tropical America, but in Okinawa the green unripe fruit (green papaya) is eaten as a vegetable. In Okinawan cuisine it's often eaten as papaya champuru ☺ It's delicious.
"Subui" is winter melon (togan), a vegetable native to tropical Asia and a staple of Okinawan cuisine. This is delicious too.
From the meal ticket machine, I ordered the "Papasubu soba", whose name suggests these are used as toppings.
Papasubu soba ¥830 — the bowls and everything are stylish too.

In a very stylish atmosphere inside the shop, first I took a sip of the soup 😀 Mmm, as expected it's different from the soups at other shops so far, and refreshing. Apparently, in addition to bonito, kombu, pork, and chicken broth, the soup is made from a large amount of shiitake and seasoned with Okinawan salt and sukugarasu. The homemade hand-kneaded noodles cling to the soup and are delicious 😋

The toppings are tender pork and, though it's hidden in the photo, melt-in-your-mouth subui (winter melon) soaked with flavor. There's also bonito flakes, papaya, julienned kombu, and shiitake, unique toppings you can't find at other shops, which is refreshing too. Healthy, isn't it.

Rating (10.5/15): The exterior and interior are very stylish, and the woman of the young tourist couple at the table next to me was really delighted 😀 Like, coming here was the right call lol. The hand-kneaded wavy noodles are delicious, and the toppings really are different from other shops, so it's refreshing. How about it, for those who are tired of regular Okinawa soba?

PS: However, I'm sorry to say, even though they went to the trouble of stylishly renovating the building and interior, the toilet in the separate building was old inside and not very clean, which I thought was a shame.

沖縄そば屋FLOG（ふろっぐ）.name: Okinawa Sobaya FLOG (Furoggu)
沖縄そば屋FLOG（ふろっぐ）.desc: A shop in Ohigashi, Nago City, also featured on the TV program "Uchiran". An all-too-unique style with a golf simulator inside and daytime drinking OK. The Okinawa soba is an orthodox bonito broth.
t: This time I'm introducing "Okinawa Sobaya FLOG (Furoggu)" in Ohigashi, Nago City! I went to eat here in February 2025 😄
FLOG (Furoggu)
FLOG (Furoggu)
FLOG (Furoggu)
This shop was actually featured on the TV program "Uchiran" ✨ Since it had been featured, I got curious and went~!

The shop's exterior is a building with a striking red awning, and "Okinawa soba" banners are put up along the road, so it's easy to spot even while driving. Near the entrance there's a blackboard sign, handwritten with "Okinawa soba — open now", and also "Daytime drinking available 🍺". An Okinawa soba shop where you can drink from noon is pretty rare, isn't it 😄
Inside the shop (you can play golf (^0^;))
Inside the shop (you can play golf (^0^;))

When you go inside... the first thing that jumps out at you is a golf simulator 😅 No, really, it's a space where you can actually play golf inside the shop. There were golf bags, and simulator footage was being projected by a projector. Golf while eating Okinawa soba!? That's quite a unique combination lol. There are also TV screens and counter seats in the shop, and there's a somewhat bar-like atmosphere too. The direction of enjoying drinks from lunchtime came through clearly 😊
Menu
Menu

The menu is simple: sanmai-niku soba (medium ¥800 / large ¥880), nankotsu soki soba (medium ¥800 / large ¥880), mixed soba (large ¥950), and jushi (small ¥200 / large ¥300). For drinks, they have everything from sanpin tea, cola, and iced coffee (¥300) to beer and highballs (¥600) — well stocked to suit the daytime drinking style 🍺
This time I ordered the "mixed soba (large) (¥950)". A greedy bowl where you can enjoy both braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs!
Mixed soba (large) ¥950

Looking at the soba brought out after a while, it's piled with plenty of green onion, with braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs lined up beneath. It looks quite hearty 😋 First, a sip of the soup. An orthodox soup with a solid bonito broth.
Mixed soba (large) ¥950

Next I have the noodles. Medium-thick and straight, with a softish texture. Both toppings, the braised pork belly and the soft-bone pork ribs, are moderately infused with flavor, and still have a bit of a sinewy texture.

By the way, as for the customers other than me... everyone was eating set meals with grilled fish! The aroma of grill-roasted fish drifted through the shop, and it looked so delicious, yassa 🐟 Maybe grilled fish is their signature dish. Maybe the grilled fish set meal is more popular than the Okinawa soba? lol. I thought next time I come I'd like to try the grilled fish set meal.
Ume-flavored pickles were served on the table, and they were delicious as a palate cleanser 😄 The refreshing ume flavor was a welcome touch between bites of soba.

Rating (9/15): All in all, the Okinawa soba is orthodox and simply tasty. It's a unique shop with the surprising character of an interior where you can play golf, and you can drink during the day too. When you stop by the Nago area, why not visit once, combined with an unusual experience 😊

ブラジル食堂.name: Burajiru Shokudo
ブラジル食堂.desc: A shop along Prefectural Route 84 near Nago Pineapple Park. The menu is unique, like an "Okinawa soba VS Brazilian cuisine" showdown. You can enjoy light pork-bone soki soba as well as Brazilian-style roast pork, pastel, and more.
t: It was featured on the "Nago City Soba Map", and I ate here in October 2020 😄
Burajiru Shokudo (pretty much along Prefectural Route 84)
"Burajiru Shokudo" is featured as shop 33 of 41 on the "Nago Soba Map"
I ordered the "soki soba" featured on the map. The menu layout is unique, like an "Okinawa soba VS Brazilian cuisine" showdown lol
The unique menu (Okinawa soba VS Brazilian cuisine) 😄
Soki soba (large) ¥700
The soup is a light, pork-bone-based type. The noodles are regular noodles. The soki is also simply tasty.

Rating (9/15): I think it's simply tasty. The location is near tourist spots like "Nago Pineapple Park", so how about it when sightseeing? I didn't take a photo, but inside, someone's soccer uniform was on display 😀

三丁目そば.name: Sanchome Soba
三丁目そば.desc: A shop full of local customers that I happened upon on a back street off Kokusai-dori. Pork bone × bonito blended soup with jiggly soft-bone pork ribs, and amazingly jushi included, all for ¥650 — great value. A pretty high-level bowl.
t: I ate here in June 2023 😄
"Sanchome Soba" — I happened upon it while walking off Kokusai-dori 😊

I had an errand at "Pallet Kumoji", at the end of Kokusai-dori, so I parked in a paid parking lot in a nearby building and walked toward Asato looking for a soba shop, and when I searched the streets behind Kokusai-dori, I found this shop by chance 😄
It's nice, kind of a once-in-a-lifetime encounter (^_^;)

Okinawa had entered the rainy season, but this time there was little rain, and that day was super hot too, and since I'd walked a bit from Pallet Kumoji, I went into the shop drenched in sweat. The shop was cooled pretty strongly, which was the best 😁
Menu posted on the wall
Looking at the menu, I thought that apart from the "Sanchome soba", things were relatively reasonable compared to other shops. The clientele also seems to be mostly locals.
I ordered the "nankotsu soki soba".
Nankotsu soki soba ¥650
Looking at the menu, I thought it was just the soba, but amazingly it also came with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) — a happy surprise 😆

I felt like starting with the rice, but first, the ritual sip of the soup. The soup looks a bit cloudy, but it's a delicious soup that seems to be a blend with pork bone broth, with a bonito base coming through a little 😋

The noodles are thin and straight, on the soft side. The soft-bone pork ribs are jiggly and infused with flavor — can't go wrong. Delicious 😄 I put them on top of the jushi like a pork bowl and ate it that way, and it was the best lol

Rating (10/15): Simply tasty. I thought it was a pretty high level 😄 It's close to Kokusai-dori, so how about it when you come shopping or sightseeing? I think it's reasonable and delicious Okinawa soba.
*The shop has no parking lot, so you'll need to park at a coin parking lot in the area.

守礼.name: Shurei
守礼.desc: A long-established diner in Isagawa, Nago. Its old-fashioned tiled roof has a lot of character. A gentle bonito-based soup with flat noodles, topped with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), rolled omelet, and fried tofu, for an outstanding value of ¥500. It also serves Nago's specialty, hitō (dolphin) dishes.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," and I ate here in March 2021 😄
Shokudo Shurei (the old-style tiled roof has a lot of character lol)
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Shurei" is featured as shop 41 of 41
I ordered the "Soba" that was introduced in the map.
Soba　¥500
A gentle bonito-based soup with flat noodles. The toppings are plentiful too—braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), rolled omelet, and fried tofu—yet it's ¥500 😁　More reasonable than other shops.

Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty and reasonable. The set meals apparently come with free rice refills, which is also good value 😁　Nago is famous for hitō (dolphin), and it was on the menu. Next time I'd like to try a dolphin dish too.

守良屋（すろーやー）.name: Suroya
守良屋（すろーやー）.desc: A popular handmade Okinawa soba shop tucked away deep in the Kyoda village. Committed to using no chemical seasonings, with glossy homemade wavy flat noodles and a light, gentle bonito broth. A natural style with windows wide open and only electric fans.
t: Driving along National Route 58 in Kyoda, Nago, I'd been curious about a handmade sign reading "Handmade Okinawa Soba Suroya," and I finally went to eat here in July 2023 😊
The turnoff from National Route 58 in Kyoda, Nago, to "Suroya"
A handmade sign with character 😄
Going deep along the narrow village road, "Suroya" was at the dead end 😁
There was no menu; the soba menu was posted on the wall of the building.
Since you access it from the national highway via a narrow road through the village, it's a quiet, tucked-away place, but inside it was packed with locals and tourists (・・)
As usual, I went in without any research, but I think it's a popular shop.

I ordered the "Suroya Soba," which has the same name as the shop. Because I hadn't done any research, I didn't know how to read the kanji, and when ordering I ended up saying "Moriyoshi-ya soba, please," but my order went through just fine (^_^;)　When I googled it after eating, I learned it's read "Suroya" (^_^;)
"Suroya Soba" ¥950
On the wall inside was a notice saying "No chemical seasonings used." I got the impression they're quite particular about making things with natural ingredients.

First, a sip of the soup. A gentle flavor with a light bonito broth coming through; solidly tasty 😋　The noodles are homemade, handmade wavy flat noodles. They look glossy and delicious. When you eat them they have a bit of firmness, and these are solidly tasty too 😋

The toppings are soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), both jiggly and tender 😄　The seasoning is gentle and light, which felt different from the type at other shops where the flavor has thoroughly soaked in.
Rating (9.5/15): It's a shop particular about its ingredients, with "no chemical seasonings used" 😄　How about it for those who like healthy Okinawa soba?

When I ate here it was a super-hot lunchtime right after the rainy season had ended, but maybe because their concept is enjoying food naturally in an old house, the shop's windows were wide open with only electric fans, and no air conditioning was on (^_^;)　Everyone was eating while sweating, which in a sense was healthy too 😁

宜野湾そば.name: Ginowan Soba
宜野湾そば.desc: A famous shop also introduced in Horiemon's email newsletter. A customizable style with 3 kinds of noodles × 2 kinds of soup; the Gorogoro Soba loaded with chopped meat and the salt soft-bone pork rib soba are popular. Its sister shop is Churuge Soba in Uruma City.
t: ― 2nd visit (November 2023) ―
I ate here in November 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 – Feb 29, 2024)," and I went as my 17th of 34 shops 😊
Ginowan Soba (it's on the way toward the University of the Ryukyus from the Ganeko intersection on National Route 330)
I learned about this soba shop from Horiemon's email newsletter and ate here before, and this is my second time in a while 😁
Celebrity autographs displayed inside the shop
Lots of celebrity autographs are displayed inside. It's a famous shop loved by the locals 😊
Inside the shop

Last time there were customers, so I couldn't take photos of the inside, but this time it was past lunchtime and no one was there, so I took some photos. The parking lot fits several cars, and the inside is spacious too.
You can choose from 3 kinds of noodles and 2 kinds of soup.

This time I had decided to order the "Gorogoro Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet, and I chose the "light" soup. When I asked the staff about the noodles, they recommended the "wavy noodles," so I ordered it with "wavy noodles."

However, when I checked my previous blog after eating, I'd been recommended the same thing by the staff that time too and chosen "light soup" with "wavy noodles," so I thought I should have ordered something different this time (;^ω^)
Gorogoro soba　¥800 (light soup, wavy noodles)

Partly because there were no other customers, it came out quickly after I ordered. When it's this fast, you can grab a meal easily, which is nice. When I went to taste the soup first, I thought the soup's color was dark and it looked strong-flavored as I took a sip.
Sure enough, it's the "light" type as I ordered, but it still has a solid flavor and is delicious 😋

As for this soup, this time the wall inside said "Prepared in three stages with prefecture-raised chicken and pork. The classic light soup," so it seems to be a chicken and pork broth soup, but the menu in my previous blog said "bonito flakes, combined with the saltiness of soy sauce and seasonings," so maybe the broth base changed?
Gorogoro soba (medium)　¥800 (light soup, wavy noodles)

The wavy noodles have just the right firmness too; solidly tasty 😋　The meat in the toppings (braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), lean meat?) is chopped into small pieces, and though it was a medium size, it had quite a lot of volume.
Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty. I thought it was a fair bit higher level than when I ate here before. This is also a shop loved by the locals, so how about it when you're nearby.
― 1st visit (September 2021) ―
I ate here in September 2021. I learned about this place because it was introduced in Horiemon's email newsletter 😄
Ginowan Soba (it's on the way toward the University of the Ryukyus from the Ganeko intersection on National Route 330)
Menu

Horiemon had eaten the "Salt Soft-Bone Soki Soba" in his email newsletter, so I ordered the same item. It's the type where you can choose the soup and noodles, and this time I went with the "light bonito soup" and "wavy noodles" the staff recommended 😄
Salt soft-bone soki soba (large)　¥1,000
The soup clings well to the smooth wavy noodles; delicious 😋　There were lots of pork spare ribs (soki) too, and I got full.

Rating (9/15): It's solidly tasty, but since it was recommended by the gourmet Horiemon, my expectations were too high and I set the bar too high ^^;　I felt it didn't have the impact of my provisional #1 recommendation, EIBUN. However, this is also a shop loved by the locals, so how about it when you're nearby.

宮古そば ひらら.name: Miyako Soba Hirara
宮古そば ひらら.desc: An unusual Miyako soba shop inside a golf driving range. Its selling point is the traditional-style, un-Instagrammable "Soba" with the toppings hidden under the noodles. A blended broth of pork bone and bonito, with the pork bone coming through strongly.
t: I ate here in May 2024 😁 I learned about this shop because it was introduced in a local newspaper 😁　But this road is one I often take to the surf point I go to every weekend (Suicide Cliff Point) (^0^;)
I had absolutely no idea there was an Okinawa soba shop at a golf driving range (^0^;)
The "Miyako Soba Hirara" sign (the sign at the access road to the golf driving range along Prefectural Route 7)
The other side of the "Miyako Soba Hirara" sign. It's inside the golf driving range.
"Miyako Soba Hirara" is there when you head down the golf driving range access road.
Miyako Soba Hirara (it's inside the golf driving range)
Menu
From the menu, I somewhat randomly ordered the "Nankotsu Soba (regular)."
However, after I finished eating, I looked back at the newspaper article again and regretted it (^0^;)
It seems this shop's selling point was the "Soba" listed at the top of the menu.
Traditional Miyako soba is apparently characterized by the toppings being hidden at the bottom under the noodles, and the "Soba" at the top of the menu seems to be that.
At a glance it looks like just green onions and noodles; it makes "not Instagrammable" its selling point and seems to stick firmly to the old-fashioned traditional Miyako soba style.
This is my first Miyako soba since "Miyako Soba Ai" in Okinawa City, which I visited during the stamp rally, but Ai didn't have that style.
Since it just said "Soba," I mistakenly assumed it was simply plain soba (no toppings) (^0^;)　I should have ordered the "Soba."
Inside the shop (it's beside the golf driving range)
Inside the shop (it's beside the golf driving range)
Nankotsu soba (regular)　¥780
This one has the toppings sitting on top of the noodles as usual (^0^;)
The soup is a blended broth of pork bone and bonito, with the pork bone coming through.
It's solidly tasty.
Nankotsu soba (regular)　¥780
Next, the noodles. Medium-thin, roundish, and straight. A soft type. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are meltingly tender too, but there are spots where some sinewy texture remains.

Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty. I recommend the un-Instagrammable "Soba" with the toppings hidden under the noodles, which seems to be traditional for Miyako soba 😄　If you play golf, how about this driving range?

宮古そば愛.name: Miyako Soba Ai
宮古そば愛.desc: A night-owl Miyako soba shop open from 6 p.m. to 5 a.m. in the Nakanomachi nightlife district. A reassuring flavor with solid bonito broth, perfect for filling up before drinking or for finishing the night. It's nice that it accepts PayPay too.
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 – Feb 29, 2024)," and I went as my 9th of 34 shops 😊
Miyako Soba Ai　It's got great character 😁

This shop's business hours are 18:00–5:00, so it's open at night 🤗　It's in an area of Okinawa City with lots of bars called "Nakanomachi," so it's an Okinawa soba shop for filling up before drinking or for finishing off the night after drinking (lol)
The nightlife district (Nakanomachi) where Miyako Soba Ai is. Since it was the weekend, there were lots of touts out on the street lol
Miyako soba (small) ¥750

Since it was nighttime, this time I ordered a smaller Okinawa soba, the "Miyako Soba (small)." There was a meal ticket machine, but it also supports cashless payment, and I was able to pay with PayPay. It's nice to be able to pay quickly 😁
First, a sip of the soup. The bonito broth base comes through solidly, a reassuring flavor 😊　Solidly tasty.
Miyako soba (small) ¥750
Next, the noodles. The noodles are a thin straight type. These also have a reassuring flavor. You can't go wrong lol

Near the downtown area where this shop is (Nakanomachi (Koza)) is the road to the US military base (Kadena Air Base) (commonly known as Gate Street or Airport Road), and nearby is the street that used to bustle with American servicemen as customers.
When I walked along this road for the first time in a while, hip-hop music was blasting from bars catering to foreigners, and the street felt like a club 🤗　It makes you want to dance (lol)

Rating (9/15): The soup has solid bonito broth and a can't-go-wrong, reassuring flavor. How about it at least once to finish off a night of drinking in Koza (Nakanomachi), Okinawa City 😁　If you head out to Gate Street, you can enjoy an atmosphere like being abroad too.

沖韓亭.name: Okikantei
沖韓亭.desc: An unusual shop that, despite being a Korean restaurant, for some reason also serves Okinawa soba. A gentle broth made by simmering pork, chicken and vegetables for 10 hours, with medium-thick wavy noodles, topped with melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki).
t: I ate here in December 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1 to 2024.2.29)," and I went as my 28th of 34 shops😊
Okikantei
As the shop name and sign say, this place is a Korean restaurant, yet for some reason it also has Okinawa soba (^0^;)　It's my first time experiencing a shop like this😁
Inside the shop　The bottles on the wall on the left side of the photo seem to be Korean liquor lol
Menu
Menu
As expected, the menu is mostly Korean food, but then suddenly, for some reason, there's an Okinawa soba menu😄
This time I ordered the "nankotsu soki soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) soba large　¥780

First, the soup. I was savoring it thinking it was a gentle broth with a strong bonito base?, but when I later looked at the stamp rally description, it said "Please savor our broth made by simmering pork, chicken and vegetables for 10 hours" (^0^;).

"Was it chicken broth?" I lost confidence (^0^;)　Sorry for my clueless taste buds (^0^;)　But when I was drinking the soup I thought it was bonito, so maybe there's bonito broth in it too. Sorry, I'm not confident (^0^;)
Soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) soba large　¥780
Next, the noodles. Medium-thick wavy noodles. They're on the soft side.
The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) topping is fairly large and simmered until melt-in-your-mouth.
Perfectly tasty😆

Rating (9/15): Perfectly tasty. The light, gentle broth and the melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are delicious. Also, the parking lot was behind the shop, but it seemed to have only a few spaces. When I googled it, there was information that parking at a nearby paid lot would be free, but I couldn't figure out where a coin parking lot was in the area.

浜屋そば.name: Hamaya Soba
浜屋そば.desc: A shop popular on social media with lines out the door, near Miyagi Coast (a surfing and diving spot). A light salt-based soup with bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) and seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). It also runs the food truck "Tomoyan-kun."
t: This shop is popular on social media and elsewhere😊　I ate here for the first time in quite a while (May 2023)
"Hamaya" is a popular shop, and there's always a line at lunchtime lol
Menu
I ordered the "Hamaya Soba," which has the same name as the shop
Hamaya soba large　¥850

First, a sip of the soup. It's a light flavor with just a touch of pork bone, different from other shops' soups😊　The noodles are medium-thick, and the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) and seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) toppings also seem to be seasoned with salt, so it's on the light side.

Rating (9/15): Perfectly tasty. It's a popular shop with lines even on weekdays, but turnover is decent, so I think you'll get in after a short wait. There seem to be 2 parking spaces beside the shop and 7 a little way away, but this time I parked far down along the seawall on the coastal road^^;　This sea (Miyagi Coast) is popular for diving on days with no waves and as a surf point when there are waves, so there's a lot of street parking along the seawall too. They also seem to run a food truck, so you could probably eat there without lining up😊
I parked far away on the road along the seawall and walked to Hamaya^^;　It's one of the prefecture's top diving and surf spots😊
There's also the food truck "Tomoyan-kun"😊
Recently the food truck has been in the parking lot of a commercial facility in Okinawa City😊

浦添そば.name: Urasoe Soba
浦添そば.desc: A locally popular shop along Route 330. Its soki soba with a strong bonito broth is distinctive for the fuchiba (mugwort) scattered over it, and the self-service mini sata andagi after your meal is a nice touch.
t: I ate here in March 2023😊
Urasoe Soba (along Route 330)
I had the "soki soba"😊
Soki soba　¥800
The soup has a strong bonito broth, and the noodles are the thin type. It's soki soba, but it had fuchiba (mugwort) scattered over it, which no other shop has😁
Eaten together with the noodles, the mugwort flavor is really nice and delicious. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are melt-in-your-mouth and tasty too😋
What's more, mini sata andagi (Okinawan doughnuts) are set out self-service for after your meal, which is great service😄

Rating (9/15): Perfectly tasty. It's close to the spring training ballpark of the pro baseball team Yakult Swallows, so why not visit while sightseeing? I went in at lunchtime, and it was bustling with local customers.

浮島ＢＡＳＥ.name: Ukishima BASE
浮島ＢＡＳＥ.desc: A stylish new shop near Kokusai-dori. Its signature is the nankotsu soba with a pork bone-based soup, where you can choose between fresh noodles (chewy) and regular noodles. The menu is extensive, from champuru and pork bone soup to desserts.
t: I ate here in March 2024😄
Ukishima BASE (so stylish😁)
Ukishima BASE (so stylish😁)
It was lunchtime, and the shop was full of customers, but after waiting a while I was told "Please come in" and shown to a counter seat😄
Menu
Menu (besides Okinawa soba dishes, there's champuru too)
Menu (miso soup loaded with ingredients and pork bone soup too lol)
Menu (there are all sorts of things besides Okinawa soba dishes)
Menu (there are desserts too)

This time I ordered the "nankotsu soba." You can choose between two kinds of noodles, "fresh noodles (chewy texture)" and "regular noodles (noodles that cling to the soup)," and I chose the "fresh noodles."
Nankotsu soba　¥800
The "nankotsu soba" is here. Judging from the color, I wondered if the soup was pork bone-based as I took a sip.
As expected, it was pork bone-based😁　It's perfectly tasty.
Nankotsu soba　¥800
Next, the noodles. Medium-thin noodles with fairly good firmness.
The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are jiggly and tender, and the seasoning is on the light side.
Rating (9/15): Perfectly tasty. It's close to Kokusai-dori, so why not try it when you're nearby while sightseeing? The inside of the shop felt new and stylish, perhaps because it had just opened.

海老そばとwine PARMI.name: Ebi Soba to wine PARMI
海老そばとwine PARMI.desc: Shrimp soba by day and a wine bar by night, a double act. Its signature is the limited 5-servings-a-day "Ebi Zanmai -Kiwami-" with a rich, creamy soup made from a pork bone base and 20 shrimp. Luxurious toppings including two head-on shrimp and chashu.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o), with some additions of my own😁
I ate here in November 2024😆 This time I visited "Ebi Soba to wine PARMI" in Omoromachi, Naha City.
Ebi Soba to wine PARMI
Ebi Soba to wine PARMI
As the name says, this shop serves soba featuring shrimp, and it's a soba shop with a unique style where you can also enjoy wine, especially at night.
The lunch menu is shrimp soba, and the dinner menu is a wine bar😆
The inside has a calm atmosphere, a space like a stylish bar, with wine bottles lined up on the counter. Being able to enjoy wine at an Okinawa soba shop is quite a rare concept🍷✨.
The mini bottles of liquor on the counter are cute😆
There are lots of wine bottles too
Menu (the limited 5-servings-a-day "Ebi Zanmai -Kiwami-"😆)
Menu (an explanation of the difference between Ebi Zanmai and shrimp soba. Ebi Zanmai is the top one👍)
Menu (the "Rich Shrimp Miso Soba" looks delicious too😄)
Menu
Menu (besides shrimp broth, there's also shellfish broth and bonito broth)
Menu (side dishes. Dangerous for calories (^0^;))
An explanation of the parking
A panel explaining their commitment to the shrimp soba
Ebi Zanmai -Kiwami-　¥1,600

What I had this time was the limited 5-servings-a-day "Ebi Zanmai -Kiwami-" for ¥1,600😄. As the name suggests, it was a bowl that lets you enjoy shrimp to the fullest. The soup is made from a pork bone base with broth drawn from 20 shrimp, giving it a very creamy, rich finish🦐. It's packed with the umami of shrimp, and I could also taste a spicy accent🔥. The soup is frothy😆
Ebi Zanmai -Kiwami-　¥1,600

The noodles are medium-thick, gently wavy fresh noodles🍜. They have a chewy texture, and with every bite you can faintly taste the flavor of the wheat and a hint of salt. They cling well to the soup, picking up the rich shrimp soup nicely. Unlike traditional Okinawa soba noodles, they're closer to a ramen style.

The toppings were very luxurious too✨. Two large head-on shrimp, a seasoned egg, four slices of chashu, plus two pieces of melt-in-your-mouth braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and small shrimp scattered over it, a volume truly worthy of the name "Ebi Zanmai (shrimp galore)"🦐🍖. However, what was disappointing was the seasoned egg and the chashu🥚. They were cold, as if just taken out of the fridge, and the gap with the temperature of the soup bothered me a bit❄️. If they'd taken the extra step of warming them, it might have been a more unified bowl.

Rating (9/15): I got the impression the menu was a little similar to that of "Kaidashi Okinawa Soba Kiseki.", which I visited the other day during my stamp rally rounds🤔. Both are seafood-style Okinawa soba, characterized by a creamy soup. However, personally I felt Kiseki's soup was better put together and more polished. PARMI's shrimp soba is delicious too, but the cold toppings ended up being a bit of a letdown. I'm sorry, but I ended up thinking "Kaidashi Okinawa Soba Kiseki." was tastier🙏

玉屋そば jr 名護店.name: Tamaya Soba jr Nago Branch
玉屋そば jr 名護店.desc: The Nago branch (along Route 449) that calls itself the "Second-Generation Okinawa Soba King." A light, clear soup with a choice of flat or thin noodles, and the all-you-can-take fuchiba (mugwort) is its specialty. Try the mixed soba with tender simmered pork spare ribs (soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku).
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," so I ate here in January 2021😄
Tamaya Soba jr Nago Branch (along Route 449)
"Tamaya Soba jr Nago Branch" is introduced as shop 35 of 41 in the "Nago Soba Map"
I ordered the "mixed soba" introduced on the map. According to the map, it's the "Second-Generation Okinawa Soba King" and its selling point seems to be fuchiba (mugwort).
Mixed soba　¥700

A light, clear soup, and you can choose flat or thin noodles; this time I went with the thin noodles, which are the popular choice😄　The pork spare ribs (soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) toppings are simmered tender too😋　Just what you'd expect from the 2nd-generation Okinawa Soba King lol　The all-you-can-take fuchiba (mugwort) is also a great accent and the best. I feel like it instantly makes it zero calories and healthy😁
Rating (9/15): As the "Second-Generation Okinawa Soba King," it's a shop you'll want to check out😁　It's perfectly tasty, so please do give it a try.

あじゃず.name: Ajazu
あじゃず.desc: A stylish popular shop with jazz playing inside (is the name from Aja × jazz?). The entrance covered in greenery is the landmark, and the signature dish is the soki soba with three large pieces of soki on a light pork bone soup.
t: *I also had AI (Claude 3.5 sonnet) make this article, and I've edited and updated part of it myself lol
On my Okinawa soba tour, this time I'll introduce “Ajazu” in Akebono, Naha City! 😄 I ate here in September 2024 😄
I went to “Ajazu” in Akebono, Naha City. It's located heading toward the port from the Aja intersection on National Route 58.
The shop's exterior is really stylish! The sign reading “Okinawa Soba Ajazu” on the white wall catches the eye. There are lots of green plants around the entrance, full of tropical vibes 😊
Ajazu (the entrance is covered in green, so at a glance you can't tell (^0^;))
The sign for Ajazu's on-site parking lot
Ajazu entrance
When I entered the on-site parking lot, it was actually full (^0^;)
It was lunchtime, but I thought it must be a popular shop.
However, since it's Okinawa soba, I figured turnover would be quick and waited a bit on the premises. Then customers who had finished eating came out, and I somehow managed to park.

And when you go inside, jazz is playing as background music. I wonder if this is where the shop's name comes from? Maybe it's a pun on the place name “Aja” and “jazz.” It had a somewhat different atmosphere from other Okinawa soba shops, and felt a bit stylish.

Looking at the menu, besides the standard Okinawa soba, of course, there's also yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) soba and jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice). This time I went for the classic and ordered the “soki soba.”
The meal ticket machine near the entrance (this time I ordered soki soba)
While I waited, I looked around the shop, and maybe because it was lunchtime, it was really bustling. There were lots of locals too, and I felt that it's a popular shop.
Menu
Menu
Now, at last, the soki soba arrives! 🍜
Soki soba　¥880
First, the soup. Mmm, this is the standard pork bone base. It's light and easy to drink. It's just plain delicious, but I don't think it has a particularly standout personality.
Soki soba　¥880
Next, when I slurp the noodles, they're thin straight noodles and fairly soft. Personally, I thought they could have a little more chewiness / bite, but this might be where preferences differ.

Looking at the topping, the soki, there are three large pieces of soki on top! It seems to be one bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) and two soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). The seasoning is on the light side, so you can enjoy the flavor of the meat itself. However, there are some sinewy parts too.
Looking at it overall, “Ajazu's” soki soba doesn't do anything particularly unusual, but it's a stable taste.
But honestly, maybe because I saw how packed it was at lunchtime and expected too much, the taste was about “Yeah, just plain delicious.” It wasn't like I was especially moved! 😅

But Okinawa soba eaten in a shop with a nice atmosphere where jazz plays feels a little special just for that, doesn't it. If you've come to Naha sightseeing and want to enjoy Okinawa soba in a somewhat stylish atmosphere, I think “Ajazu” would be a good option.

Rating (9/15): Just plain delicious, but nothing particularly stands out; that's my impression. When you come to Akebono, Naha City, how about enjoying Okinawa soba in a somewhat stylish atmosphere at jazz-filled “Ajazu”? 😊 Now, which Okinawa soba shop should I go to next~. The Okinawa soba tour continues! Well then, look forward to next time~! 👋

かめぜん食堂.name: Kamezen Shokudo
かめぜん食堂.desc: A shokudo with a Showa-retro atmosphere in a corner of American Village. The wall of soda bottles and tables remade from sewing machine stands are photogenic. The signature dish is the Kamezen soba with melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) in a light soup fragrant with bonito.
t: *This article was created with AI (Chat GPT 5) and partially edited by me 😆
I ate here in December 2024 😄　Mihama, Chatan Town: American Village, bustling with tourists. I visited “Kamezen Shokudo,” located in a corner of it.
Kamezen Shokudo
Kamezen Shokudo
Kamezen Shokudo

As you climb the stairs, an orange neon sign and lanterns jump out at you, and it's an atmosphere as if you've slipped back in time to a Showa-era shokudo. The exterior alone is packed with “Okinawa feel,” and it seems even first-timers would get drawn right in.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

This time I ordered the “Kamezen soba,” which bears the shop's name, without hesitation. The bowl brought out had a clear, golden soup with thin wavy noodles. And on top, thin strips of yellow omelet and a large soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) sit there boldly. It looks simple, but it's the classic Okinawa soba style.
Kamezen soba　¥980
First, a sip of the soup. The bonito broth is softly fragrant, a light type with a faint touch of saltiness.
Kamezen soba　¥980
The noodles are thin with a loose wave. A fairly good texture 😄
The soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) is almost melt-in-your-mouth tender. It's so tender it comes apart in your mouth, but there's just a little sinewy texture.

Rating (9/15): It tastes just plain delicious. This shop, being located in Chatan Town, is close to American Village, in a convenient place to drop by between sightseeing. It's a shop I'd love people who want to enjoy Okinawa soba in the Chatan area to visit at least once 😄

すながわ製麺所.name: Sunagawa Seimenjo
すながわ製麺所.desc: A stylish noodle-factory-style soba shop in American Village. A combined broth of bonito, kombu, dried sardines, mackerel, scallops, and chicken, with chewy medium-thick fresh noodles. The signature dish is the special soba with everything on top, handy during sightseeing.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and partially edited by me lol 🍜✨

I ate here in November 2024 😄　This time I visited “Sunagawa Seimenjo” in American Village in Mihama, Chatan Town. Being a spot popular with tourists, not only locals but also many tourists were visiting the shop.
Sunagawa Seimenjo
The shop's exterior has a stylish feel, and photos of the signature menu items were displayed near the entrance. Just looking at that sign conveys that the soup seems good 😊
The menu inside the shop
The menu inside the shop
The menu set up inside and outside the shop
The menu set up inside and outside the shop
The menu set up inside and outside the shop
The menu set up inside and outside the shop
An Okinawa soba explanation panel set up inside and outside the shop
An Okinawa soba explanation panel set up inside and outside the shop
An Okinawa soba explanation panel set up inside and outside the shop
The menu set up inside and outside the shop

Looking at the menu, there are various kinds of Okinawa soba, and I decided to order the “special soba,” which was marked as recommended. The menu description says the broth is carefully made from ingredients such as bonito, kombu, dried sardines, mackerel, scallops, and chicken. This looks promising 🤗
Inside the shop (there are no walls, so it's practically outside 😄)

After waiting a while, the “special soba” was brought out. It looks like it has volume from the appearance alone. First, I tasted the soup, as is customary. As described, among combined broths it's a gentle taste with a bit of bonito coming through. On the sign it looked really delicious, but when I actually drank it, my impression was that it's an ordinary taste.
Special soba　¥1,280
Special soba　¥1,280

Next, I have the noodles. Medium-thick fresh noodles with a loose wave, and they're chewy. These are fairly delicious too. Not to the point of being especially moved, but I thought they were just plain delicious.

The toppings, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), are cut long horizontally, and there are parts where a bit of sinewy texture remains, but basically they're finished melt-in-your-mouth tender. I'd say these are a standard taste too.
Given its good location, it seems to be a shop popular with tourists. If you're sightseeing around Mihama American Village, how about dropping by once 😊

Rating (9/15): I thought it was just plain delicious. Although there's nothing that particularly stands out, it's a shop where you can enjoy Okinawa soba of standard deliciousness. It's in American Village, so it's in a good place to drop by while sightseeing.

北谷そば.name: Chatan Soba
北谷そば.desc: A popular shop that uses Chatan salt (100% seawater from off the Miyagi coast). The wall covered in autograph boards is overwhelming, and the signature dish is the seared salt nankotsu soba. You can choose from medium-flat noodles or wavy noodles.
t: This time my Okinawa soba tour took me to “Chatan Soba” in Kuwae, Chatan Town 🍜　I ate here in March 2025 😄
Chatan Soba
Chatan Soba
Chatan Soba

The exterior is a bit unique; it's in a corner of an apartment building, so to speak, with the shop's name written big on the wooden enclosure below the building. White stones are laid around the entrance, along with wooden decorations and handwritten signs, and the contrast with the concrete feel outside was interesting. There was also a notice for the “tofu soba,” limited to 10 servings, and this kind of handmade-feeling presentation felt somehow friendly 😊
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

When you go inside, this is quite distinctive too: autograph boards are lined up across an entire wall, making a strong impact. There were autographs from players of the Kings and the Chunichi Dragons too, a space where you immediately understand, “Ah, this place is pretty famous.” There are also tatami seats with the warmth of wood, and including the lighting and decorations, it had a calm, Okinawan atmosphere overall, and I felt that rather than being aimed at tourists, it must be a shop properly loved by local customers too. However, there were actually lots of local customers and it seems quite popular, so on this day I waited a fair while. Moreover, even after being shown to my seat, the food didn't come out quickly from there, and overall the wait was on the long side. Even if not as long as at Jagaru Soba, it might feel a bit long to impatient people (^0^;)
Menu
Chatan Soba's explanation panel
Menu

Looking at the menu, there were Okinawa soba, soki soba, salt nankotsu soba, mixed soba, and so on, and the way they push Chatan salt was memorable too. There was also a notice that they use “Chatan salt” made from 100% seawater from off the Miyagi coast in Chatan Town, which clearly conveyed their commitment to ingredients. This time I ordered the recommended “seared salt nankotsu soba,” and since I could choose the noodles from medium-flat noodles or wavy noodles, I chose the wavy noodles, which were also recommended. Being able to choose your own noodles is a nice little point.
Seared salt nankotsu soba, large　¥900

The bowl that was brought out looked fairly simple. In a clear soup sat seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), with green onions and omelet alongside. When I first drank the soup, it was pork-bone-based, yet the salt came clearly to the front. As you'd expect from using Chatan salt, it has personality, but personally I felt the saltiness was a bit strong. It's a light type, but rather than gently and slowly soaking in, it was a type of soup that pretty clearly tells you, “The salt is coming through.”
Seared salt nankotsu soba, large　¥900
The medium-thin wavy noodles I chose were on the soft side in texture, and people who want to fully enjoy firmness might find them a bit lacking.

The seared salt soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) have a browned look that whets the appetite, and when I actually ate them, overall they leaned light, with a melt-in-your-mouth tenderness too. However, depending on the part, there were places where a sinewy texture clearly remained, so not all of it was the melting type. I thought the toastiness of the searing would come forward more, but that was surprisingly modest, and my impression was that, for better or worse, it came together safely. The composition of the toppings is simple too, so rather than focusing on impact, it's a calm bowl.

Looking at it as a whole, it was a shop with lots of intriguing elements, like the shop's atmosphere, the commitment to ingredients, its local popularity, and the number of autographs, and I think it actually has an appeal that makes you want to try it once. However, speaking honestly as Anji, compared with how my expectations rose, including the wait, the taste landed at “ordinary.” I didn't feel a strong deciding factor like “I want to come back to eat this again!”

Rating (9/15): It seems to be a popular shop, but my honest impression was that the taste is just plain delicious, I guess~. It's worth experiencing once including the atmosphere, but the decisive factor that makes you want to come back is weak; that's the kind of bowl it was 🙂

まるち 北谷店.name: Maruchi Chatan-ten
まるち 北谷店.desc: Maruchi's third shop, marked by white Ryukyu roof tiles and a shisa. So popular a line forms right at opening; the customization of 3 soups × 3 noodles is the same, and there's also bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba exclusive to the Chatan branch. Lunch comes with complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice).
t: On my Okinawa soba tour, this time I visited “Maruchi Chatan-ten,” an Okinawa soba specialty shop in Yoshihara, Chatan Town 🍜　I ate here in March 2025 😄
Maruchi Chatan-ten
My first encounter with “Maruchi” was the Maruchi Nakagusuku branch, and after that I also visited the Nanjo City Tsukishiro branch, so this time is actually my visit to a third branch.
*By the way, this is the Maruchi Nakagusuku branch (I ate there in January 2024 lol)
*By the way, this is the Maruchi Nanjo City Tsukishiro branch (I ate there in July 2024 lol)
The Nakagusuku branch and the Nanjo City branch were both popular, and this Chatan branch is no exception: customers were lining up in droves right at opening 😲
Maruchi Chatan-ten (a line right at opening lol)
Maruchi Chatan-ten (a line right at opening lol)
Maruchi Chatan-ten (a line right at opening lol)
Maybe because it's in Chatan Town, an area with lots of tourists, it seems to draw a wide range of customers from locals to tourists, and I was reminded again of how popular the Maruchi brand is.

On the exterior, the roof of white Ryukyu tiles, so typical of Okinawa, stands out against the blue sky, and a shisa welcomes you from on top of the roof 🦁　Not only inside, but picnic tables are also lined up outdoors on the gravel, and on a nice day it looks pleasant to eat outside ✨　It's an old-folk-house-style building, but the inside has been neatly renovated, and it gave a calm yet clean impression.
You can eat outdoors too 😄

Now, looking at the menu, a big feature of Maruchi is the system where you can choose the soup and the noodles each from 3 kinds. The soup is a choice of 3: “light soup (our secret recipe),” “rich soup (our pride),” and “salt soup (simple is best).” My experience with the light soup at the Nakagusuku branch had stuck in my memory, so this time I tried choosing the “rich soup” 💪　It's apparently a rich preparation made by simmering prefectural chicken and pork bone for a long time, which raises my expectations 🤤　You can choose the noodles from “thin noodles,” “flat noodles,” and “wavy noodles,” and this time I went with the staff's recommendation and chose “wavy noodles.”
Explanation of the 3 soups
Explanation of the 3 noodles
Menu
Menu
Menu

What I ordered this time was the Chatan-branch-exclusive menu item “bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba (large) ¥980.” It coming with the lunchtime-service jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) was a nice point too 🍚
Bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, large　¥980 (jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) free)

Facing the bowl that was brought out, first a sip of the soup. As expected of the rich type, the chicken and pork bone broth flavor is solid. However, the saltiness is a bit strong, and I got a somewhat different impression from the creamy, mellow smoothness of the pork-bone-based soups at Nankuru, Uehara Soba, and Tsukikuroki. Rather than a deep umami, the salt comes to the front 🤔
Bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, large　¥980
As for the wavy noodles, they're a medium-thick type with a moderate chewiness, and they cling to the soup quite well too 😊

The topping, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), are well simmered and melt-in-your-mouth tender overall, but depending on the part, there were places where a sinewy texture remained, giving the impression of a mix of tender parts and parts with a solid meaty feel 😄　And the jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) that came as a lunchtime-only service is a delight! The combination of Okinawa soba and jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) really is the best ✨

Rating (9/15): Comparing Maruchi's three branches, the Nakagusuku branch, the Nanjo City Tsukishiro branch, and the Chatan branch, you can see they all have steady popularity. The atmosphere created by making use of old folk houses and the high degree of customization, where you can choose the soup and noodles, must be what attracts so many customers. The taste is “just plain delicious,” and my impression is that rather than having a standout personality, it's an Okinawa soba you can eat with peace of mind. Even so, I think the brand power that creates a line right after opening is the real thing ✨

三色屋.name: Sanshoku-ya
三色屋.desc: An Okinawa soba specialty shop with the motto “to become number one in Ginowan.” Its pride is soup you can choose from 3 kinds (chicken, pork, or blend), house-made fresh noodles, and melt-in-your-mouth seared soki served on a separate plate. Changing up the flavor with bonito oil is fun too.
t: ― 2nd Visit (October 2024) ―
*This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), with parts edited and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in October 2024 😁😊　This time I'll introduce “Sanshoku-ya” in Aichi, Ginowan City. This shop is a participating shop in the 14th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally, and this is my 2nd visit.
Sanshoku-ya
Sanshoku-ya

The shop is on the 1st floor of a reddish-brown building, and the white noren (shop curtain) is the landmark 😄　There's a handwritten sign at the entrance, with a notice that the “extra-large seared soki” is sold out. It must be a popular menu item.
The “extra-large seared soki” introduced in the stamp rally booklet was sold out (^0^;)　Too bad 😆
Inside the shop
The interior has a retro atmosphere, with red sofa seats and counter seats. Brick-style tiles are used on the walls, giving it a calm atmosphere 🏮
Menu
Menu

Looking at the menu, standard Okinawa soba items like “braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba” and “seared soki soba” are all there. And what's distinctive is that you can choose the soup from 3 kinds (chicken broth, pork broth, blend). Last time I chose chicken broth, so this time I tried ordering the “seared soki soba” with pork broth.
Seared soki soba　¥900

The Okinawa soba that was brought out after a while has a striking clear soup. First, a sip of the soup. A smooth, pork-bone-based mouthfeel, and I can feel a deep taste a cut above other shops. The depth of the soup is wonderful 😋　However, I also feel the saltiness is a bit strong.

The noodles are medium-thick with a gentle wave, and apparently they use house-made fresh noodles. Along with a chewy texture, they cling to the soup excellently. You can taste the flavor unique to fresh noodles too, and they're delicious 🍜

The topping, the seared soki, is served on a separate plate, a trick to keep its flavor from transferring to the soup. It's simmered melt-in-your-mouth tender, searing adds toastiness, and it's very satisfying to eat. Partway through, when I added the shop's original bonito oil to the soup, I could enjoy a different, deep taste.

Rating (12/15): A wonderful Okinawa soba where every element is finished at a high level. The soup especially has a deep taste with concentrated pork bone umami, and it goes perfectly with the noodles. The balance of the seared soki's tenderness and toastiness is exquisite too. The idea of letting you enjoy a flavor change with the original bonito oil is wonderful. When you come to Ginowan City, how about dropping by? 😊
― 1st Visit (July 2024) ―
*This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), with parts edited and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in July 2024 😁

This time I'll introduce “Sanshoku-ya” in Aichi, Ginowan City. On my journey touring Okinawa soba shops on the main island of Okinawa, I've visited quite a number of shops, but I'm still far from conquering them all. But I'll do my best, one shop at a time, aiming to conquer them all lol
Sanshoku-ya

Now, “Sanshoku-ya,” which I visited this time. Actually, it's a shop I'd been curious about for a while. Why? Because of the words on the sign that catches my eye every time I pass along National Route 330. I'd been drawn in by the catchphrase “Okinawa soba that will become number one in Ginowan,” which is just overflowing with confidence.
Sanshoku-ya's sign along National Route 330 (whether it's modest or overflowing with confidence, it's catchy and eye-catching 😆)
When you turn onto the road with the sign from National Route 330, the shop is right there. There was also a dedicated parking lot diagonally across.
When you turn in from National Route 330, the shop is on the left, and this parking lot is on the right, diagonally across
When you go inside, there are counter seats and table seats; the interior is built like a former snack bar. (Sorry, I didn't take photos)

Looking at the menu, besides Okinawa soba, there are also a few rice dish items. But the purpose this time was, of course, “Okinawa soba that will become number one in Ginowan.” So I decided to order the signature Okinawa soba.
Menu
Menu (they even say themselves that “will become the number one Okinawa soba shop in Ginowan” raises the bar lol)
Explanation of the broth (it seems you can choose from 3 kinds: chicken, pork, or blend)
Explanation of the noodles (fresh noodles, that's nice 👍)
