It seems you can also take the seared soki soba to go
The owner's profile (he seems to be someone who has had all sorts of experiences)
The owner's profile (he seems to be someone who has had all sorts of experiences)
The owner's profile (he seems to be someone who has had all sorts of experiences)
They're on social media too 😆
He seems to do music too and is apparently selling CDs lol
Menu (an unusual one)

When ordering, I learned that you can choose the soup. You can choose from 3 kinds: chicken broth, pork broth, or blend. When I asked the staff, they said the most popular is chicken broth. So this time I tried choosing chicken broth.
While I was looking for a while at the menu, which even includes the profile of a manager who seems to have quite a character? (lol), the Okinawa soba I ordered was brought out.
Okinawa soba that will become number one in Ginowan　¥1,400

First, the soup. When I take a sip... oh, this is unexpected! It's a slightly different taste from other Okinawa soba shops. Maybe because it's based on chicken broth, I sense a taste somewhat close to ramen soup. But it's unmistakably the taste of Okinawa soba. Rich and mellow. Preferences might be divided on this, but personally it was a taste I liked a lot.

Next, I have the noodles. A chewy texture is their characteristic. They have chewiness / bite too and cling well to the soup. I have the impression that many Okinawa soba noodles are on the soft side, but the noodles here have a moderate springiness and are very satisfying to eat. Delicious.

Pay attention to the toppings too. The seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were especially memorable. A tender texture that falls apart. A deliciousness that melts in your mouth. Besides the regular seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), there was also salt-seared soki.

According to the profile of the owner, Mr. Ishikawa, on the menu, he also trained at the famous Okinawa soba shops “Chinchiki Soba” and “Ishigufu.” I see, now that you mention it, there's something similar in the taste, I thought, convinced.

According to Mr. Ishikawa, in July 2023 he temporarily closed Sanshoku-ya (at the time, Sanshokudon-ya), and reopened it renewed in 2024. At that time, he's also taking on the challenge of making noodles using house-made wheat. A story where you truly feel his passion for Okinawa soba.

Rating (12/15): Even while the owner says he's raising the bar, I felt he must also have a fair amount of confidence. No lie in the catchphrase “Okinawa soba that will become number one in Ginowan”! Preferences may vary by person, but I thought it might be the most delicious of the Okinawa soba shops in Ginowan City I've eaten at so far~. How about trying it once? It's recommended 😄

上原そば.name: Uehara Soba
上原そば.desc: Provisional #5 (13.5/15). An "Okinawa soba and local fish cuisine" shop on high ground with a sweeping view of the sea. Cloudy, MSG-free soup with Agu broth × homemade noodles with whole wheat flour and bonito powder. The bone-in pork ribs on a separate plate and the small dish of local fish sashimi are nice touches.
t: ✨I ate here in February 2025. This time it started with a small mishap 😅 I headed excitedly for "Suba Suba" on Yagaji Island, but it was unexpectedly their regular day off... It had been featured on the local Okinawan TV program "Uchiran", so my expectations were high, and honestly the shock was big. But I switched gears, telling myself that Okinawa soba touring is fun including twists like this, and decided to look for a shop open nearby. That's where I came across "Okinawa Soba and Local Fish Cuisine Uehara Soba" in Yohena, Nago City.
Uehara Soba
Uehara Soba (business hours sign near the entrance outside the shop)

The building's exterior looks like an apartment, so for a moment I felt a little uneasy, wondering if this was really the right place, but a "UEHARA SOBA" sign welcomes you clearly. The sign at the entrance lists the business hours, and there's a homey atmosphere.
Meal ticket machine near the entrance inside
It's a meal ticket machine style with an extensive menu. Besides the standards like hon-soki soba, tebichi soba, and sanmai-niku soba, there's also a sea grape rice bowl on the menu.

When you go inside, the first thing that jumps out at you is the view from the windows. It's on high ground, so the location with a sweeping view of the sea is the best 🌊 It was a bit cloudy that day, but even so the view was plenty refreshing. With wooden tables and calm lighting, it's a stylish, café-like space. It gives the impression of a dining room with a sea view rather than an Okinawa soba shop.
You can see the sea from inside the shop
Inside the shop

This time I ordered the "hon-soki soba". You can choose between rich and light soup, and when I asked the staff, they said "The rich one is ordered a lot". I obediently followed the recommendation and chose rich 😄 The bowl that was brought out has a striking cloudy white soup. Apparently they use Agu broth, and a soft, gentle aroma rises with the steam.
Agu broth, MSG-free, they say
Hon-soki soba (large noodles) ¥1,050

First, a sip of the soup. Smooth and creamy, a perfect balance 😋 It's a different type from Kame Soba's Agu broth, and the flavor reminded me of Getto in Naha City and Tsukikurogi in Uruma City. Delicious 😋
Hon-soki soba (large noodles) ¥1,050

The noodles are homemade, medium-thin and straight, with whole wheat flour and bonito powder kneaded in. These are great too. They have solid chewiness. They go well with the cloudy soup, which clings to them nicely. Personally, these were noodles very much to my liking.

The bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), served on a separate plate, look hearty right from the start. When you pick them up with chopsticks there's a bit of a sinewy texture, but in return you can enjoy a properly meaty texture. The seasoning is a little on the sweet side, well soaked in, and simply tasty 😋 Dipping them in the soup gives them yet another character. What made me even happier was the small dish of sashimi. A style you rarely see at other shops, and it shows how much effort they put into local fish cuisine. Sashimi being served at a soba shop is pretty rare, isn't it.

Rating (13.5/15): It was a pinch-hitter shop I went into on short notice, but in the end it was a big hit. Location, soup, noodles, toppings — whichever you look at, the level is high, and honestly I can proudly say it's "recommended-shop level 😄". It's a shop I'd love both tourists and locals to visit at least once. High level. If you like Agu-broth-style Okinawa soba, please give it a try.

上江門そば.name: Uejo Soba
上江門そば.desc: A stamp rally participant with a lovely red-tiled old-house-style building and terrace seats. Its feature is that you can choose the soup from three types: bonito, miso, or soy sauce, and it's equipped with a cashless ticket machine.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o), with some parts added by me 😁
I ate here in October 2024 😆
This time I visited "Uejo Soba" 🍔, which is also a stamp rally participant.
Uejo Soba
When you see the "Uejo" sign along Route 331, turn in from there
Parking lot (it's spacious, so even large crowds are OK 😄)

When I arrived at the shop, the first thing that caught my eye was the spacious parking lot ⛽. A welcome point for customers who come by car 🚗. And then there's the old-house-style building with its striking red-tiled roof 🏡. The interior has a warm wooden feel, the seats are spaciously arranged, and there's a somehow relaxing atmosphere 😌. There are also terrace seats outside, and being able to enjoy a meal while feeling nature on sunny days was appealing too 🌞.
There are outdoor tables, not just indoor seating

Looking at the menu, the "Uejo soba" is set up so you can choose the soup from three types: bonito, miso, or soy sauce 🍲. This is a slightly ramen-like approach, and as a soba lover it struck me as fresh 😊. This time I chose bonito, which is said to be the recommendation 👍. It's a style where you buy a ticket from a ticket machine, and it's perfectly cashless-ready too 💳. Ingenuity typical of an area with many tourists shines through ✨. This time I had the shop's signature item, the "Uejo soba".
A cashless-ready meal ticket machine is nice 👍
Menu
Inside the shop (new and clean)
The "Uejo soba" that was brought out has a look that's simple yet appetizing 🍜. When you take a sip of the soup, a solid bonito broth flavor spreads out 🍼.
Uejo soba (bonito) ¥1,150
Uejo soba (bonito) ¥1,150

The noodles are medium-thick straight noodles with solid chewiness 🍟. They're both chewy and silky smooth, and personally it was a texture I quite liked 😋. The toppings are generous braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs, each well infused with flavor 🍖. The soft-bone pork ribs in particular are simmered tender, with a nice texture that crumbles in your mouth... but it was a little disappointing that both had some sinewiness depending on the cut 🙅‍♀️.
You can also add jushi or small side dishes with the set menu to adjust the volume, which is a nice point 🍳. This time I had just the soba, but next time I come I'd definitely like to try a set 😎.

Looking at it overall — the atmosphere of the whole shop, the many soup options, and service that caters to tourists too — I got the impression that this "Uejo soba" is proposing a new style of Okinawa soba 🌟.
Got Uejo Soba's stamp 👍

Rating (9/15): Simply tasty 🎨 Its coziness and beautiful old-house-style appearance make it worth visiting once 🙌. It was a shop that made me think I might try a different flavor next time 🍲✨. How about everyone giving it a try once?

下地そば.name: Shimoji Soba
下地そば.desc: An old-house diner just like grandma's house from the old days. The ordering system, where you place a magnet on a whiteboard, is fun. The signature Shimoji soba is an everything-on-top bowl with braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, yushi-dofu, and mozuku.
t: I ate here in January 2024. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 33rd of 34 shops 😊 I've steadily eaten my way through the stamp rally and finally made it this far 😆
Shimoji Soba
Shimoji Soba (an old house with a traditional tiled roof 😆)
Entrance
When you go inside, it feels like grandma's house from the old days 😆 So nostalgic lol
Inside the shop (where the family Buddhist altar used to be, there's now a self-service water dispenser 😆)
Inside the shop (Gaggle Sale's autographs are on display)

It was my first time at this shop, so I didn't know the system, but there was no ticket machine, and I had planned to order the "Shimoji soba" featured in the stamp rally booklet anyway, so I said "Shimoji soba, please", and was told, "Put a magnet on number 4 on the whiteboard", so I put a magnet on number 4. The number 4 order on the whiteboard in the photo is mine 😆
It seems the soba menu items are numbered. Maybe the numbers were written on the photo menu posted on the wall, but I didn't notice (^0^;)
They seem to use fresh noodles, and maybe because they take time to boil, I had the impression it took a little while to arrive.
Shimoji soba ¥1,050

As it was also written on the menu on the wall, the "Shimoji soba" is a so-called "everything-on-top" with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu), and mozuku.
The "everything-on-top" menu item reminded me of "Futami Soba" in Nago City, which I introduced in "Holds its own against the recommended ones" 😆
First I taste the soup. Maybe the yushi-dofu broth is mixed in, so the broth base was hard to make out, but it tasted light with a slight pork bone base — rather thin, though.
Shimoji soba ¥1,050

Next I try the noodles. A thin noodle type, and being fresh noodles, they do have a chewy quality. Then I tried the toppings: the braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs were on the small side, and their flavor was also thin and light. Including the yushi-dofu and mozuku, it's a light style overall.
Rating (9/15): Ordinary. The building is an old house like an Okinawan grandma's house from the old days, and the atmosphere is very Okinawan, so how about it when you come to this area sightseeing?

与那原家.name: Yonabaru-ya
与那原家.desc: A famous shop along Route 329. Its feature is that you can choose light (bonito flavor) or rich soup, and the rich soup made from pork bones and chicken carcasses comes with gently wavy noodles. Even the regular size includes soft-bone pork ribs, so it's satisfying.
t: I ate here in June 2022 😊
Yonabaru-ya (along Route 329)
Menu
I ordered the "nankotsu soki soba", recommended as the most popular. On top of that, it's a system where you can choose "light" or "rich" soup, and this time I chose the "rich flavor".
The soup, with broth made from pork bones and chicken carcasses, is simply tasty.
Nankotsu soki soba
The noodles are a gently wavy type, and the regular size includes soft-bone pork ribs, so I'm satisfied. The shop is on the large side too.
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. This is also a famous shop, so how about trying it once? Next time I'd like to try it with the "light soup, bonito flavor" 😊

並松そば.name: Nanmatsu Soba
並松そば.desc: A shop on high ground between the Kin Town Office and the baseball stadium. The clear soup has an exquisite flavor where you can taste both bonito and pork bone, and the braised pork belly and pork spare ribs toppings come on a separate plate. You can choose thin or flat noodles, and the freedom of 7 size levels plus extra noodles in 100g units is fun too.
t: I ate here in May 2023 😊
Nanmatsu Soba (set back from Route 329)
Menu

I ordered the "Nanmatsu soba", which shares the shop's name. You can choose thin or flat noodles, and when I asked the staff for a recommendation, they recommended "thin noodles", so I chose thin noodles. The sizes were finely divided into 7 levels, from mini to toku-toku-toku-dai (extra-extra-extra large), but this time I ordered the "medium" size 😊
Nanmatsu soba (medium) ¥935

It's called "medium" size, but I thought at other shops it would be in the "large" class. A decent volume. Like a ramen shop, this shop also has a "kaedama" (extra noodles) menu, and it seems you can order in 100g units from 100g (¥110) to 500g (¥550). (I didn't order extra noodles this time)

The soup is a beautiful clear color. I took a sip wondering, "Bonito-based?" I sensed an exquisite flavor where you can taste not just bonito broth but pork bone broth too. Like the "Awase Soba Shokudo" I ate at the other day, I could taste both bonito and pork.
The soy-sauce-based toppings (braised pork belly, pork spare ribs) were on a separate plate, perhaps so their flavor and color wouldn't transfer to the clear color of the soup 😊

The thin noodles are on the soft side. The braised pork belly and pork spare ribs are infused with flavor and tender, and even the soki bones were soft (・・) I don't think I've had soft bones at any other shop so far. Proof of how tenderly they're simmered 😄
Rating (9.5/15): Simply tasty. The soup is a beautiful clear soup, with a flavor where you can taste both bonito and pork, which was nice.

中村商店.name: Nakamura Shoten
中村商店.desc: A shop whose selling point is Agu broth. The Murasho soba, topped with yushi-dofu, pig's feet, braised pork belly, and fish cake, is a very hearty bowl that even comes with a small dish of Agu-broth curry. Set meals with free rice refills too.
t: I went to eat here in March 2023, before surfing (Itoman City, Suicide Cliff point) 😊
Nakamura Shoten
Looking at the menu, it seems Agu is their selling point 😁
Menu
Murasho soba ¥950

Agu broth soup with smooth medium-thick noodles. The toppings — yushi-dofu, pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and fish cake (kamaboko) — make it super hearty (・・) On top of that, it comes with a small dish of curry rice made with Agu broth ^^;
I ordered without looking at the small print on the menu, but it was indeed written there ^^; I thought this wasn't a meal to eat before going into the sea. I'm stuffed.
Rating (9/15): This shop has very hearty menu items, such as champuru dishes and set meals with free rice refills. It's simply tasty 😊, so I recommend it for people who want to eat heartily.

おきなわすばやぁ太陽.name: Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo
おきなわすばやぁ太陽.desc: An Okinawa soba shop in the food court of Uruma City's farmers' market facility "Uru Marche". It's fun that you can choose your noodles, such as curly noodles, fresh sea lettuce (āsa) noodles and fresh mozuku noodles, and they also have goat soba and nationwide shipping. You can casually enjoy a bowl at the open outdoor seats.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o) and partly added to by me 😆
I ate here in October 2024 😄
This time I visited "Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo" in the food court of "Uru Marche" in Uruma City!
Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo (inside the Uru Marche food court)
🌺Various shops are lined up in the food court, and they all look delicious, so it's hard to decide 😋.
There are all kinds of shops inside the Uru Marche food court

What I chose from among them was, of course, the "Soft-bone Soki Soba" at Okinawa soba stamp rally participant "Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo". Normally I always order the Okinawa soba introduced in the stamp rally booklet, but for this shop it was "goat soba" that was introduced, and after eating goat soba before at "Mukashi Mukashi" in Nago City, the impression of the gamy smell afterward stayed with me strongly, so somehow I couldn't choose it (^0^;)　I gave up on it this time (^0^;)　While I was eating it, I thought it had no quirkiness (^0^;)　It's the after-meal part that bothers me 😄
They also ship Okinawa suba nationwide 😄
It's nice that you can choose the noodles too 👍
Menu panel board
There's also goat (hijaa) soba.
On top of that, for the noodles I tried choosing "fresh mozuku noodles" 🎶. I'm looking forward to the unusual noodle texture!

While waiting for the soba at the roofed outdoor seats, a pleasant breeze blew in and I was in the best mood ☀️. Eating in an open space like this on a nice day feels really good, doesn't it. It really boosts the vacation mood too ⛱️.
It feels nice outdoors 😄
It feels nice outdoors 😄

And now, the long-awaited soba arrives ✨. The bowl is full of jiggly soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki)! The broth has a clear color, and the fresh mozuku noodles look delicious too 🍜. My heart is full of anticipation: time to eat!
Soft-bone Soki Soba　¥800

First, a sip of the broth. The pork-bone-based stock comes through solidly, with a deep flavor 😊. However, overall the saltiness is a bit on the strong side, so opinions may be divided. But it might be perfect for people who like strong flavors!
Soft-bone Soki Soba　¥800

Next I have the "fresh mozuku noodles". They have a chewy, springy texture that's satisfying to eat ✨! However, to be honest, the "mozuku feel" is a bit restrained, and the flavor is on the faint side? 🤔　That said, there's mozuku in it as a topping, so eating them together, you can properly enjoy the mozuku. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) 🍖 are tender and melt-in-your-mouth too 😳

Rating (9/15): My overall impression is "fairly plain tasty", but with the openness of eating outdoors and the liveliness of the whole food court added in, I had a fun time 😊. Also, Uru Marche has lots of other gourmet food too, so next time I'd like to try other shops as well 🍔🍣.
"Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo" was a shop you can drop into casually and enjoy Okinawa soba in a relaxed way 🍜. When you head out to Uru Marche, please do pay it a visit! 🌈

お肉の店仲村.name: Oniku no Mise Nakamura
お肉の店仲村.desc: An Okinawa soba shop run by a pork specialty store. It uses Terukina Soba's handmade noodles, and the Special Soba topped with spare-rib-style soki, pig's feet (tebichi) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) has big impact. Carefully selected pork and beef are also sold at the shop front.
t: I ate here in December 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 25th of 34 shops 😊
Oniku no Mise Nakamura ("Meat Shop Nakamura")　*From the shop name alone, you can't tell it's an Okinawa soba shop (^0^;)
With this shop, it's hard to realize it's an Okinawa soba shop from the name alone (^0^;) But looking carefully, the cute pig on the sign is promoting Okinawa soba (lol)
*You can park about 4 cars in the parking lot out back.
Menu

I went straight into the shop and checked the menu. First there's an explanation of the noodles. It says, "We use Terukina Soba's handmade noodles." On top of that, these noodles "can't be bought at the supermarket", which gave me a sense of anticipation that they'd be delicious 😄
Menu
This time I decided to order the "Special Soba (medium)" introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Menu
Being a pork specialty store, they have a lineup of rice bowls too 😁　In the photo of the bone soup, the toppings are out of control (^0^;)
Menu
True to a meat specialty store, they sell meat too lol　They handle not only pork but beef too 😆
Menu
Apparently carefully selected pork is butchered at this shop. I'm looking forward to the meat too 😄
Special Soba (medium)　¥900

It came 😁　The toppings have impact; as expected of a pork specialty store, there's soki like spare ribs, and pig's feet (tebichi) (pork trotters), which I haven't had in a while lol　Also thinly sliced braised pork belly (sanmai-niku).
But first, as usual, the broth. Thinking "Hm?", I tasted the broth several times with my spoon. It looks rich in color, but it's a quite light seasoning with a faint pork-bone-based stock.
Next, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). This too has a surprisingly light seasoning, and it feels like a little sinewy texture remains.
Special Soba (medium)　¥900

Next, I have the "Terukina Soba handmade noodles". These noodles are medium-thick and a straight type. On the soft side. Continuing with the toppings, the pig's feet (tebichi). These are tender and full of collagen, but the seasoning feels weak. The spare-rib-style soki also has tender meat, but the flavor feels light.
Fuchiba (mugwort for free topping)

It wasn't placed on the table where I sat, but on the next table there was fuchiba (mugwort). In the second half I ate just a little with the noodles, and the faint bitterness makes a nice accent. I wish it had been placed on my table too.

Rating (8/15): Well, hearing it was Okinawa soba from a pork specialty store, I got my hopes up, but the broth felt weak in flavor, and while the meat had visual impact, I ended up thinking other shops' meat is just plain tastier.

がじまるそば.name: Gajimaru Soba
がじまるそば.desc: A soba shop operating at lunchtime that's the izakaya "iZAKAYA" at night. The signature is the Gajimaru Soba with a blended pork bone × bonito broth and lots of green onions, plus reasonable menu items like the ¥500 Nikuzu Soba. Look for the kijimuna sign.
t: This time I visited "Gajimaru Soba" in Gusukuma, Urasoe City. I went to eat here in March 2025 😁😊
Gajimaru Soba

Looking at the exterior, the big sign on the building's wall reading "iZAKAYA　Sake, Snacks and Charcoal Grill　Gajimaru Soba" catches the eye 😄　The sign has illustrations of a banyan tree and a kijimuna, giving off a very Okinawan atmosphere.
Gajimaru Soba
Gajimaru Soba

Near the entrance there's a yellow, handwritten-style guide sign reading "Gajimaru Soba →" and a stand with menu photos, so even first-timers can get there without getting lost ✨　Lanterns hang at the entrance, giving a glimpse of its other face as an izakaya at night.
Inside the shop

Stepping into the shop, a simple yet stylish space opens up, with counter seats lined along walls in an exposed-concrete style. There's a big TV mounted on the wall, so it feels like you can eat leisurely while watching TV 😊　It's cash only, so don't forget to have cash ready (these days more and more shops accept cashless payment, so I do hope something can be done about this lol).
Menu
Menu

Looking at the menu, starting with the signature "Gajimaru Soba (¥980)", there's a richly varied lineup with "Nikuzu Soba (¥500)", "Meat-Piled Mazesoba (¥880)", "Braised Pork Belly Soba (¥700)" and "Vegetable Soba (¥700)". What stands out is that the "Nikuzu Soba" is set at quite a reasonable ¥500 🎵　On top of that, side dishes like "Small Soba ¥300", "Pork Tamago Onigiri ¥200" and "Curry Rice ¥400" are plentiful too, so it seems they'd make good companions for the evening izakaya hours as well. By the way, looking at the drink menu, they have everything from awamori, shochu, highballs and chuhai to jasmine (matsurika) cocktails, and apparently there's an all-you-can-drink plan for ¥2,000. If you came at night, the drinks would surely be delicious lol 🍺
The ice water looks like a chuhai (^0^;)
This time I ordered the "Gajimaru Soba (¥980)", which shares the shop's name. If you're going to eat here, you've got to try the soba bearing the shop's name 😊

While I was waiting at the table, the Gajimaru Soba appeared on a wooden tray, set on the table's glossy, stylish top 🍜　The visual of a very Okinawan bowl with a pale blue rim topped with plenty of green onions whets the appetite.
Gajimaru Soba　¥980

First, as usual, a sip of the broth. It's a blended stock of pork bone and bonito, finished so you can properly taste the savoriness of both 😋　If anything, the pork bone comes through slightly more. It feels plain tasty.
Gajimaru Soba　¥980
Next, lifting the noodles, medium-thick curly noodles appeared 😄　You can clearly see the wavy curls. Eating them, they have a slightly chewy texture.

For toppings there are both braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), with a chunky sense of volume ✨　However, both the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) had quite a sinewy texture, and honestly I'd have been even happier if they'd been simmered a bit more melt-in-your-mouth 😅　The green onion topping is generous, and its crisp texture and refreshing aroma make a nice accent
Rating (9/15): All in all, it was a stable bowl that's "plain tasty"~. It's the lunchtime operation of a shop that's an izakaya at night, so when you're in the area, why not drop by?

きしもと食堂八重岳店.name: Kishimoto Shokudo Yaedake branch
きしもと食堂八重岳店.desc: The Yaedake branch of the long-established "Kishimoto Shokudo", founded in Meiji 38 (1905). The menu has a clean-cut single item: "Kishimoto Soba" with wood-ash noodles. A solid flavor with authentic bonito broth; a line is a given, but turnover is fast.
t: It's a shop whose name often comes up when you search "Okinawa soba", so I went in March 2023 😀　This was my first time at an Okinawa soba shop in Motobu Town 😁
Kishimoto Shokudo (Yaedake branch)　I lined up a little, but turnover was fast and the wait was short
The menu is just one item: "Kishimoto Soba (extra-large) (large) (small)". Somehow that's cool.
The menu is only one item, Kishimoto Soba (it's a style where you choose the size and buy a meal ticket)
I ordered "Kishimoto Soba (large)" from the meal ticket machine.
Kishimoto Soba (large)　¥850
First, a sip of the broth. An authentic bonito broth with a solid flavor. It's delicious, but it felt a bit salty. I drank it all to the end, but I thought some people might find it salty.

The noodles are Okinawa soba made using wood ash, a slightly thick medium-thick type. They go well with the broth 😀　The toppings are green onions, fish cake (kamaboko), and lean pork and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), well seasoned, tender and delicious.
Rating (9.5/15): I thought the broth was a bit salty, but the noodles, broth and toppings were all well balanced and delicious overall.

きんそば.name: Kin Soba
きんそば.desc: A shop with real skill, with an aromatic broth blending kelp and chicken bones into a bonito-forward stock. You can choose from 3 kinds of noodles from Nishizaki Seimenjo, and the yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) from Unashi Tofu-ten is superb too. A bowl I think is the best in the Shuri area.
t: I ate here in December 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 29th of 34 shops 😊
Kin Soba
Kin Soba entrance
This shop opens at 11:00, so I came timed to the opening, and wow, the 3 parking spaces in front of the shop filled up all at once (^0^;)
I thought, this is a popular shop 😄
Inside the shop

This shop is pay-first, and you pay at the counter. As the stamp rally booklet introduction said, "A broth blending kelp and chicken bones into a bonito-forward stock!", there's a nice bonito-based smell in the shop 🤤　The broth seems delicious from the smell alone.
This time I ordered the "Kin Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet. On top of that, they accept cashless payment (PayPay), and being able to pay quickly is nice too 😆
Menu
Explanation of their dedication to noodles

At this "Kin Soba", you choose from 3 kinds of noodles from Nishizaki Seimenjo. When I asked the staff for a recommendation, they answered that "No.1 (fresh noodles) and No.2 (whole wheat fresh noodles) are ordered a lot", so I figured No.1 must be the recommendation after all and chose "fresh noodles" lol
Kin Soba　¥880

From the stamp rally booklet introduction and the delicious smell of bonito broth wafting through the shop, I already knew it was bonito broth as I took a sip of the broth. No doubt about it, a delicious broth where the bonito stock really comes through 😋
Kin Soba　¥880
Next, I have the fresh noodles. The translucent noodles are medium-thick with a chewy texture. These are delicious too. The texture is fairly thick, like udon, and satisfying to eat 😄
Next, the topping of yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) from Unashi Tofu-ten. You can taste the flavor of the tofu, and this is tasty too. It seemed to me like tofu that had just been freshly made.
However, what was disappointing among the toppings was the meat (^0^;)　The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) had a sinewy texture remaining, and I thought it was just one step short.

Rating (10.5/15): I felt the bonito-forward broth, the chewy fresh noodles and the yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) were very delicious. What's disappointing is that the meat has a sinewy texture, which is a shame. There were several autographs in the shop too, and I thought it's a popular shop, but the parking seems limited, so right after opening may be the way to go.
I think it's the most delicious of the Okinawa soba shops in Naha's Shuri area that I've eaten at so far, so how about everyone trying it once?

くくる.name: Kukuru
くくる.desc: A shop of "Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba" along Prefectural Route 7. A spicy broth fragrant with sesame, with homemade noodles aged for 48 hours with seafood powder mixed in. Free large noodles plus an after-meal ice cream. The solid homemade chili paste kōrēgūsu is unusual too.
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 2nd of 34 shops 😊
"Kukuru" along Prefectural Route 7

I'd often seen this shop on my way back from the point where I always surf (Itoman City: Suicide Cliff point), and I'd always wanted to eat here someday, and when I learned it was a participant in the "Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally" that I'd found out about a few days earlier, I was finally pushed to go in (;^ω^)

There are Okinawa soba shops all over that I've never been to, so it's hard to decide (;^ω^)　But this time I had a goal of prioritizing the 34 shops participating in the limited-time stamp rally, so I went in lol
The stamp rally booklet has an introduction to each shop and a photo of what seems to be their recommended Okinawa soba, so I decided to order that.
For "Kukuru" this time, "Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba" was introduced, so I ordered that. It was featured at the very top of the meal ticket machine too, so it seems to be this shop's top pick 🤗
The meal ticket machine installed near the entrance　The upper-left button is the "Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba" shown in the photo above.
Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba　¥930　Large noodles (free)

First, as usual, the broth 😁　It's completely different from the bonito-stock, pork-stock and chicken-stock types of Okinawa soba I usually eat lol　It's not super spicy, but it's a little spicy, and you can taste the sesame aroma and flavor too. It feels like ordinary tantanmen 😊　The noodles seem to have seafood powder in them, and you can tell something is kneaded into them. The aged noodles, rested for 48 hours, have a chewy texture and are delicious.
Vinegar and Sichuan pepper flowers were brought out with the Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba, so I added those in the second half.

I thought I'd added quite a lot of vinegar, but since the broth is rich to begin with, I couldn't really tell the change in flavor (;^ω^)　You may not be able to experience the flavor change unless you add a lot.
Menu placed on the table　Next time I'd like to try the regular Okinawa soba too
Anyway, I got my stamp for shop 2 of 34 😁

Kōrēgūsu (homemade chili paste) promoted above the meal ticket machine　Usually it's a liquid, but this kōrēgūsu is solid, which is unusual. It didn't come with the Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba, but I'd like to try it someday too.

Rating (9.5/15): It was more tantanmen than Okinawa soba 😊　The carefully made homemade noodles had a chewy texture and were delicious. For those who want to eat something different from regular Okinawa soba, how about this Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba? It comes with large noodles and an after-meal ice cream (brown sugar OR mango) sweet too.

田舎庵みどり町店.name: Inaka-an Midorimachi Branch
田舎庵みどり町店.desc: A rare shop where, under the supervision of the owner of the renowned "Shuri Soba" in Shuri, Naha City, you can taste Shuri Soba, normally guaranteed to have a line, in Uruma City. It faithfully recreates the clear, light, gentle soup and the slightly firm straight noodles. The complimentary purple sweet potato pudding after your meal is a nice touch.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1 to 2024.2.29)," and I went as my 13th of 34 shops😊
Inaka-an Midorimachi Branch
The menu item introduced in the stamp rally booklet was "Shuri Soba," so I came wondering, "Why Shuri (Naha City) soba in Uruma City?", but looking at the menu it made sense😁
Menu
It seems this shop serves Shuri soba under the supervision of the owner of "Shuri Soba" in Shuri, Naha City. I see, so that's why it's "Shuri Soba"😊
There also seem to be "yushi-dofu soba" and "nakami soba," but the staff said "The yushi-dofu soba is sold out," so "yushi-dofu soba" may be popular too. This time I ordered the "Shuri Soba Regular."
Menu
Shuri soba regular　¥650
It looks exactly like the "Shuri Soba" from Shuri Soba that I've eaten before😁
When I ate at the original Shuri Soba, the soup was a pretty light, gentle flavor, and I took a sip of the soup wondering how this one would be.

It's exactly the soup of "Shuri Soba" in Shuri, Naha City: clear, quite light and gentle. As I wrote in a previous blog post, to me it tastes quite weak, so I prefer a soup with more flavor and a stronger broth (;^ω^)
Shuri soba regular　¥650

Next, the noodles. The noodles are straight and a little on the firm side. As for toppings, the lean meat (loin) has a lingering sinewy texture, but the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is tender and delicious.

Rating (8.5/15): I think they've completely recreated Shuri Soba's Shuri soba. "Shuri Soba" always seems to have a line and be crowded, so if you have a chance to stop by Uruma City, I recommend tasting Shuri soba here at Inaka-an Midorimachi Branch. However, the flavor is quite on the light side. After the meal, purple sweet potato pudding came complimentary too.

白虎外伝.name: Byakko Gaiden
白虎外伝.desc: A stylish Okinawa soba specialty shop in a renovated former foreigners' house in Minatogawa Stateside Town. The seafood x pork bone soup made by an owner who switched over from running a ramen shop, and the homemade noodles made from four kinds of wheat, mixed with pink hibiscus noodles, are distinctive.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions of my own.

This time I'd like to introduce "Byakko Gaiden" in Minatogawa, Urasoe City, which I learned about from a local newspaper. I ate here in July 2024. An Okinawa soba specialty shop run by an owner who switched over from running a ramen shop, makes you curious, right?😉
Okinawa Soba Specialty Shop　Byakko -Gaiden- (it's a former foreigners' house, so it's stylish)

"Byakko Gaiden," in Minatogawa Stateside Town, catches the eye with the stylish exterior of a renovated former foreigners' house. The light blue window frames accent the white walls, giving it a full-on Okinawan atmosphere!🏠✨ The surrounding foreigners' houses are also an area lined with stylish restaurants😄
The surroundings (an area lined with other stylish restaurants in renovated former foreigners' houses)
The surroundings (an area lined with other stylish restaurants in renovated former foreigners' houses)
Inside the shop (I couldn't get a photo, but it's like a stylish café done in pink and white)
When you go in, an interior based on pink and white welcomes you. The contrast with Okinawa's blue sky is lovely, and it makes you want to take photos📸
The meal ticket machine near the entrance (the recommendation seems to be the meat-loaded soba on the top-left button)
The menu next to the ticket machine

So, what I ordered this time was the "Nikumori Soba" (meat-loaded soba), which was also introduced in the newspaper article. As the ticket machine's description says, it seems to be the everything-on-top version with pork spare ribs (soki), pig's feet (tebichi) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku).
Meat-loaded soba　¥1,100
A bowl topped with luxurious toppings was brought out.

The soup is a well-balanced flavor combining a seafood broth of bonito and mackerel with pork bone broth. I can feel a personality a cut above other Okinawa soba shops. Neither the seafood nor the pork bone flavor is too assertive; they harmonize gently, making it easy to drink😌
Meat-loaded soba　¥1,100

Next, the noodles😄　Actually, these noodles are really unique. They're homemade noodles using four kinds of wheat, and believe it or not, a few pink noodles kneaded with hibiscus are mixed in as an accent. Totally Okinawan, right?🌺 They're firm, and the texture is fun too.
Meat-loaded soba　¥1,100 (Check out the colorful noodles that are a treat for the eyes!💖)

The toppings are the classic Okinawa soba trio: pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and pork spare ribs (soki). They're lightly seasoned and don't get in the way of the soup and noodles. However, I thought they could have had a bit more presence.

The defining feature of "Byakko Gaiden" is, above all, its originality. You can sense an approach that makes use of skills honed at a ramen shop while also valuing the traditions of Okinawa soba. I think it's a bowl packed with the owner's passion and ingenuity💪

Rating (9.5/15): Overall, the distinctive taste and beauty of the noodles were impressive. The soup also has a flavor in a class apart from other shops, making me sense new possibilities for Okinawa soba. There may be some room for improvement in the toppings, but as a whole I think it's a well-balanced bowl.

"Byakko Gaiden" is a shop that values the traditions of Okinawa soba while trying to bring in a fresh breeze. I recommend it not only to Okinawa soba lovers, of course, but also to anyone interested in Okinawan cuisine😊
If you want to enjoy a stylish exterior and interior along with original Okinawa soba, please do visit "Byakko Gaiden." I'm sure you'll discover a new charm of Okinawa soba!

神里そば.name: Kanzato Soba

みはま食堂.name: Mihama Shokudo

t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o) and partly edited by me 😆
In August 2024, this time I visited "Mihama Shokudo" in Mihama, Chatan Town 😆
Mihama Shokudo (it was incredibly busy with locals and tourists)

The shop's exterior has a somehow nostalgic feel, with the atmosphere of an old-fashioned Okinawan diner. It has a simple, tasteful charm, and a ticket machine sits enthroned at the entrance. The ticket machine has an extensive menu, all at affordable prices. There are also many quintessentially Okinawan soul-food dishes such as pork bone soup. I bought a ticket at this ticket machine and went on inside the diner.
Ticket machine near the entrance

The interior also has a simple, rustic atmosphere, with tables and chairs lined up and old autographs and menus posted on the walls, which felt somehow homey. The slightly dim lighting and warm wooden tables are somehow calming. Many of the customers seemed to be local regulars, plus some tourists. It felt like a place loved by both tourists and locals. I love the atmosphere of diners like this 😊
Inside the shop (lots of autographs on the walls)
Among the soba-only items on the ticket machine, I ordered the "Mihama Soba" in the top left, named after the shop, which seemed to be the top recommendation.
Mihama soba ¥850 (unexpected pork offal (nakami) (^0^;) I'd been saving my pork offal soba for a famous shop in Nago all this time (^0^;))

At other shops I've toured so far, the soba that shares the shop's name has generally been an Okinawa soba with all the meats on top (soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), pig's feet (tebichi), etc.), so I was imagining that kind of Okinawa soba this time too, but to my great surprise (°°), it had pork offal (nakami) in it lol
I'd been saving my chance to eat pork offal soba at a famous "Nakami Soba" shop in Nago all this time, so having my first pork offal experience here was a bit unplanned 😅

Now, the all-important "Mihama Soba." When I first looked at the bowl that was brought out, the first thing that leapt into view was a generous amount of "pork offal (nakami)." This would make it my first pork offal soba experience, and just from the look of it, it's packed with volume. The broth is bonito-flake-based, and it tasted a little strongly salty. The bonito flavor is solid, but because the salt was overdone, my first impression was that it was a bit salty.
Mihama soba ¥850

The noodles are thin, straight, and soft in texture. However, I felt I'd like a bit more firmness. Personally, I thought noodles with a bit more springiness might go better with the broth. But this softness creates a nostalgic feel, and that works in its own way ✨

There were also braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), seasoned on the light side and simmered until tender. The braised pork belly in particular was very tender, but some sinew remained and it was a bit chewy. The soft-bone pork ribs were tender and I could enjoy them right down to the bone, but they didn't have any special impact, and overall my impression was "it's ordinary" 😅 The pork offal was also decently tasty.

Overall, Mihama Shokudo's "Mihama Soba" was a dish that let me feel the goodness of old-fashioned Okinawa soba. The shop's atmosphere and diner-like simplicity were really good, but the soba itself had no particularly standout features; it's something you can enjoy without any surprises. It felt like an everyday spot for locals. The prices are reasonable too, and I think it's a very good place to casually drop by for an everyday lunch.

For an Okinawa soba tour, Mihama Shokudo scores pretty high in that you can enjoy the local flavor while feeling the atmosphere of the area, but if you're looking for surprise or novelty in taste, another option might be better. Still, it's the perfect shop for when you want to immerse yourself in the local Okinawan vibe or spend a relaxed time 🌺
Rating (9/15): It's decently tasty. It's an Okinawan diner near the tourist area of Chatan Town, so why not give it a try once when you come sightseeing 😄

I have the goal of touring every Okinawa soba shop on the main island of Okinawa, and I'm eating my way through little by little. I'm still far from conquering every shop, but this time I'll introduce “Mendokoro Mannen” in Nakanishi, Urasoe City 😊
Mendokoro Mannen
Mendokoro Mannen

“Mendokoro Mannen” is located a little way in from National Route 58 in Nakanishi, Urasoe City. The exterior is an ordinary soba shop, but when I went inside and looked at the menu, I noticed it has a feature different from other Okinawa soba shops. Believe it or not, like a ramen shop, you can choose from 3 kinds of soup: “salt,” “soy sauce,” and “miso”! 😲
Menu
Menu (the yushi soba is served with salt or soy sauce soup 😄)
Menu (the vegetable soba is served with salt, soy sauce, or miso-flavored soup 😄)

This is interesting. I'd previously eaten Okinawa soba with miso soup at “Nagomi” in Nago City, so I was going to go with miso soup this time too, but a staff member told me “The salt soup is recommended,” so I obediently switched to salt soup.

Looking at the menu, in addition to the signature “Mannen soba,” there's also “vegetable soba.” It seems you can choose salt, soy sauce, or miso for both. Moreover, at the top of the menu there was an explanation that they had changed from pork belly to chicken breast. Pork is the standard for Okinawa soba, but chicken is an interesting new attempt too 🐔
Inside the shop
Inside, there are counter seats and table seats; it's simple but clean. On the tables were condiments such as house-made kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) and shichimi.

The “Mannen soba (salt)” I ordered has arrived! Visually, there's chicken breast, chopped green onions, and the distinctive red fish cake (kamaboko), vivid in a clear soup 😄

First, a sip of the soup. Hm? This tastes more like ramen soup than Okinawa soba! It's a salt soup based on chicken broth, and I can taste the flavor of sesame oil too. There's not much of the pork bone flavor typical of Okinawa soba, but this is delicious in its own way 😋
Mannen soba, medium? (salt) ¥900? (sorry, I forgot the details 🙏)

Next, I have the noodles. Medium-thin noodles with a loose wave, a smooth texture with a slight chewiness, and I wondered, are these house-made fresh noodles? They go well with the soup and cling to it properly.

The topping, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), has a light seasoning and is simmered melt-in-your-mouth tender. The chicken breast, which replaced the pork belly, also surprisingly suits this soup and didn't feel out of place. The combination of the salt soup's refreshing taste and chicken actually feels natural.
What I suddenly thought after finishing was, “Next time I'd like to try the miso soup too.” I got curious, wondering what Okinawa soba with miso soup tastes like.

I felt that “Mendokoro Mannen” is a shop that, while protecting the tradition of Okinawa soba, is pursuing new possibilities for Okinawa soba by adding the options of salt, soy sauce, and miso. It's a creative type of Okinawa soba, but I think it's a dish worth trying at least once 😊

Rating (10.5/15): An Okinawa soba shop with distinctive soups you can choose from salt, soy sauce, or miso. This time's salt soup tasted more like ramen than Okinawa soba, but I enjoyed it as delicious in its own way. The noodles were smooth with a moderate chewiness, and the toppings were cooked tender too. It's recommended for people who want to enjoy a new variation of Okinawa soba!

I went on an Okinawa soba tour in Asato, Nakagusuku Village 🍜✨　This time I visited "Kwacchiiya Shokudo". At a glance, the location is along the street with a simple exterior that makes you go "Oh, is this it?", and the sign has a lot of character too.
Kwacchiiya Shokudo

Location-wise it's not the kind of place packed with tourists, and honestly I went in thinking "Maybe it's quiet today?", but it was surprisingly bustling with local customers. I think this kind of "diner that's part of everyday life" feel is one of the good things about Okinawa soba~ 😊
Meal ticket machine near the entrance inside the shop
Menu posted inside the shop

When you enter it's a meal ticket style, with a big ticket machine. The menu is easy to understand too, and my impression is that Okinawa soba, soki soba and tebichi soba and the like are solidly covered. This time I went with "Soki Soba" without hesitation. And happily, it comes with complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice)… that gets me excited 🍚✨
Autographs of famous people posted inside the shop

While waiting, I looked around the shop and there were autograph boards all in a row, giving off an air that this must be a shop that's been loved for a long time~. The interior isn't flashy either, with a calming feel; there are people who eat quickly and leave, and people eating while leisurely chatting, and it felt like the center of local lunchtime.
Soki Soba (regular)　¥950 (jushi free)

Now, here's the soki soba that arrived. My first impression is "soupy!" There's a generous amount of broth, and from the look alone it's the "warm-you-up type". Taking a sip, the bonito broth comes through. Honestly, it's not the "super shocking!" type, but it has a reassuring feel where you can honestly say it's "fairly tasty" ☺️
Soki Soba (regular)　¥950 (jushi free)

The noodles are a medium-thick straight type, with a soft-ish texture. Rather than hitting you with firmness, they're the smooth, easy-to-eat type. I think people who like soft noodles will get hooked, and conversely people in the "plump and firm camp" may find them a little lacking. The memorable punch is restrained… that's where it stands.

And then the star, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki). They look like they have solid presence, but the seasoning is the light type. While there are tender parts, there are also parts where a bit of sinewy texture remains.

I also have the complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice). This too is lightly flavored, not the richly cooked type, a just-right balance when eaten with the soba. Since the soki soba is soupy, eating it alternately with the jushi feels like it resets your mouth, and this was a welcome combination 🍚🍜

Rating (9/15): My honest take overall is that rather than "I totally recommend it!", it's "an ordinary bowl that makes you want to keep coming as a local". It's not flashy, but there's the soupy broth with bonito stock coming through, the soft-ish medium-thick straight noodles, the light soki, and the complimentary jushi. With this set, there's solid satisfaction. Rather than making it a sightseeing destination where you "absolutely must go", my impression was that it's a shop to drop into casually when you're nearby and enjoy everyday Okinawa soba 🏝️✨　It makes sense that it's bustling with local customers.
